// Every slice of this part is two squares touching at a corner point. The slicer must guess whether that is one
// polygon with a pinch or two polygons, and the printed joint has zero width: fused by luck or broken.

const fixed = j.part('pair').add(c1.union(c2.moved(j.tx.move(-0.45, -0.45, 0))), { id: 'pair' })
j.compile(fixed).diagnostics            // → []

// ── 5. Multi-body parts and op modes ──────────────────────────────────────────
const plate = j.sketch('p', { on: j.plane.XY }).rect('r', 50, 30, { center: true })
const post = j.sketch('q', { on: j.plane.XY }).circle('c', 6, { at: [0, 0] })
const spare = j.sketch('t', { on: j.plane.XY }).circle('c', 6, { at: [40, 0] })

const holder = j.part('holder')
  .extrude(plate.profiles(), mm(5), { id: 'base' })                     // op 'new' (first feature)
  .extrude(post.profiles(), mm(30), { id: 'post' })                     // op 'join' (overlaps base)
  .extrude(spare.profiles(), mm(30), { id: 'spare' })                   // op 'new' (touches nothing: a spare post, body2)
  .cut(j.sketch('h', { on: j.feat('spare').endFace() }).circle('c', 1.7, { at: [40, 0] }).profiles(), mm(8), { id: 'pilot' })
  .boolean('cut', j.feat('post').body(), j.cyl(mm(1.7), mm(10)).moved(j.tx.move(0, 0, 22)), { id: 'bore' })   // CSG tool, one body only

const H = j.compile(holder)
H.summary()
// → { bodies: 2, features: 5, volume: 13'575 mm³ }
//   = base 7500 + post above base π·6²·25 (2827.4) + spare π·6²·30 (3392.9) − pilot 72.6 − bore 72.6
H.decisions.filter(d => d.kind === 'op').map(d => [d.at, d.chose])
// → [['base', 'new'], ['post', 'join'], ['spare', 'new'], ['pilot', 'cut']]
// op: 'intersect' keeps only the overlap with what exists, e.g. trimming a silhouette with a side-view extrude.

// ── 6. Timelines compose, and the unchanged prefix stays cached ──────────────
// Feature chains are functions builder → builder; composing them concatenates timelines.
const drill = p => p.hole([j.pt(-20, -10, 5), j.pt(20, -10, 5)], j.hole.clearance('M3', { depth: mm(5) }), { id: 'mount' })
const soften = p => p.fillet(j.sel.edges('|Z').of('holder'), mm(2), { id: 'soft' })

j.hash(holder.use(drill, soften)) === j.hash(holder.use(drill).use(soften))            // → true  (grouping doesn't matter)
j.compile(holder.use(drill, p => p.fillet(j.sel.edges('|Z').of('holder'), mm(3), { id: 'soft' }))).trace
  .filter(t => t.level === 'L4').map(t => [t.pass, t.cached])
// → [['feature:base', true], ['feature:post', true], ['feature:spare', true], ['feature:pilot', true], ['feature:mount', true], ['feature:soft', false]]
j.compile(holder.use(drill).suppress('mount')).metric('volume')
  .eq(H.metric('volume'))                                                              // → true  (a suppressed feature changes nothing)

08 Selectors and persistent naming: CSS selectors for topology

08-selectors-persistent-naming.js · 99 lines
// 08 · Selectors and persistent naming: CSS selectors for topology
//
// Model
//   A Selector is a query that denotes a set of faces, edges, vertices or bodies.
//   Selectors form a Boolean algebra: and = ∩, or = ∪, minus = \, not = complement within the scope.
//   Resolution happens at L4 against a genealogy graph: every face records the feature and the
//   sketch entity that generated it, and every later feature records which faces it split,
//   merged or replaced. A persistent name is a path in that graph:
//     boss/side[base.l3]                       the side face swept from sketch edge l3
//     fillet2/face[boss/side[base.l3] ∩ boss/end]   the fillet face born from that edge
//   Genealogy names survive upstream edits. Index-based names ("face 7") do not.
//
// Grounding
//   Persistent naming in history-based modelling (Kripac 1997). The query syntax is borrowed from CadQuery.
//
// Notice
//   - Prefer feature-based selectors (j.feat('boss').sideFace('l3')) to geometric ones, and geometric ones to nth().
//   - .expect(n) turns a silent topological naming break into a loud error at the right place.
//   - prog.why(sel) explains every resolution: candidates, filters, and the genealogy chain.
//   - The selector algebra is property-tested like any other law (see 43).
//
// Results in `// →` comments show the illustrative shape of a result.

import { j, mm, deg } from 'jig'

// ── Fixture: an open box with a screw boss in one corner ──────────────────────
const base = j.sketch('base', { on: j.plane.XY })
  .line('l1', [0, 0], [60, 0]).line('l2', 'l1.end', [60, 40])
  .line('l3', 'l2.end', [0, 40]).line('l4', 'l3.end', 'l1.start')
  .constrain(j.c.horizontal('l1'), j.c.horizontal('l3'), j.c.vertical('l2'), j.c.vertical('l4'), j.c.fix('l1.start'))
  .dim('l1', 'w').dim('l2', 'd')

const boxFrom = sketch => j.part('box')                  // a model is a value, so a function of a sketch is a model family
  .params({ w: mm(60), d: mm(40), h: mm(30), wall: mm(2) })
  .extrude(sketch.profiles(), 'h', { id: 'body' })
  .shell(j.feat('body').endFace(), 'wall', { id: 'shell' })
const box = boxFrom(base)

// ── 1. Three ways to say "the top rim" ───────────────────────────────────────
const rimByGenealogy = j.feat('body').endFace().minus(j.feat('shell').faces()).expect(1)  // what is left of the end face
const rimByGeometry = j.sel.faces('>Z').of('box').expect(1)                               // the highest face
const rimByIndex = j.sel.faces().of('box').nth(7)                                       // works today, breaks tomorrow

const B = j.compile(box.fillet(rimByGenealogy.edges(), mm(0.6), { id: 'soften' }))
B.why(rimByGenealogy)
// → { resolved: ['body/end ∖ shell'],
//     chain: ['body/end ← extrude(base) cap', 'shell removed the inner region; remaining ring keeps its name'],
//     candidates: 1, filters: ['minus shell.faces → 1'] }
j.compile(box).diagnostics.filter(d => d.kind === 'ref.fragile')
// → []   (rimByIndex has not been used in a feature yet; it becomes a warning as soon as it is)

// ── 2. The query mini-language ────────────────────────────────────────────────
j.sel.edges('|Z').of('box')                       // the vertical edges: 4 outside + 4 inside
j.sel.edges('|Z').of('box').where(e => e.convex)  // the 4 outside corners
j.sel.faces('+Z')                                 // faces whose normal points up: the rim and the inside floor
j.sel.faces('<Z').expect(1)                       // the bottom face, which will sit on the bed
j.sel.faces('%plane and #Z')                      // the walls: planar faces perpendicular to Z
j.sel.edges('%circle').radius(mm(1.7))            // every M3 clearance hole edge

// ── 3. Feature-based selectors read like the design intent ────────────────────
const front = j.feat('body').sideFace('l1')       // the face swept from sketch edge l1, whatever its index
const sideEdges = j.feat('body').sideFaces().edges('|Z')
const insideFloor = j.feat('shell').faces().and(j.sel.faces('+Z')).expect(1)

const labelled = box
  .emboss(j.region.text('PARTS', { size: mm(8), font: 'Inter Bold' }), mm(0.6), { on: front, op: 'cut', id: 'label' })
  .fillet(j.sel.edges().of(insideFloor).and(j.sel.edges().of(j.feat('shell').faces())), mm(3), { id: 'scoop' })   // finger-friendly floor

// ── 4. The topological naming problem, staged ───────────────────────────────
// Add a notch to sketch edge l1. The front face now splits in two, and every index shifts.
const base2 = base.line('n1', [25, 0], [25, 6]).line('n2', 'n1.end', [35, 6]).line('n3', 'n2.end', [35, 0])
  .trim('l1', [30, 0])                     // l1 now runs 0–25 and 35–60; it keeps its id on both pieces
const boxNotched = boxFrom(base2)

const N = j.compile(boxNotched.emboss(j.region.text('PARTS', { size: mm(8) }), mm(0.6), { on: front, op: 'cut', id: 'label' }))
N.why(front)
// → { resolved: ['body/side[base.l1]#a', 'body/side[base.l1]#b'], note: 'l1 was split by trim; 2 faces descend from it' }
N.diagnostics
// → [{ level: 'error', kind: 'ref.expect', at: 'label.on', message: 'emboss target resolved to 2 faces; expected 1',
//      fix: "pick one: j.feat('body').sideFace('l1').largest()  or  .near([12, 0, 15])" }]

// The fix states the intent precisely, and the IR records it.
const fixedFront = j.feat('body').sideFace('l1').largest().expect(1)

// ── 5. Index selectors: what breaks, and how jig tells you ───────────────────
const fragile = box.fillet(j.sel.edges().of('box').nth(3), mm(1), { id: 'f' })
j.compile(fragile).diagnostics
// → [{ level: 'warning', kind: 'ref.fragile', at: 'f.edges', message: 'nth(3) depends on face order',
//      fix: "j.feat('body').sideFaces().edges('|Z').near([60, 0, 15])" }]

// ── 6. Selectors as values: compose them, name them, test them ───────────────
const outsideCorners = j.feat('body').sideFaces().edges('|Z').minus(j.feat('shell').faces().edges())
const allRounded = box.fillet(outsideCorners.expect(4), mm(3), { id: 'corners' })

// Robustness: run the suite's refs.robust law on this model. It perturbs every parameter and checks that
// each selector still resolves to the same genealogy, so naming breaks show up before a user edits the model.
j.laws.check(j.laws.for(allRounded), { only: ['refs.robust'], n: 50, seed: 1 })
// → [{ law: 'refs.robust', tier: 'invariant', ok: true, n: 50, justifies: 'catches topological naming breaks' }]

09 Fillets, chamfers, shells and ribs: local operations with global consequences

09-fillets-chamfers-shell.js · 106 lines
// 09 · Fillets, chamfers, shells and ribs: local operations with global consequences
//
// Model
//   A fillet of radius r replaces an edge by the surface a ball of radius r traces while touching both faces.
//   Locally it is an opening (convex edge: remove material) or a closing (concave edge: add material)
//   with a disk of radius r, applied only in the edge's neighbourhood; faces away from the edge keep their names.
//   Feasibility: r is bounded by the room on each adjacent face. Two fillets sharing a 30 mm side allow r ≤ 15 mm.
//   A chamfer cuts with a plane at setbacks (d, d2) or (d, angle). A shell is the erosion R ⊖ B_t with open faces
//   removed, so an outer corner radius r becomes an inner radius max(r − t, 0).
//   On a bed edge, a fillet's normal turns towards −Z: below z = r(1 − cos 45°) it overhangs more than 45°.
//
// Grounding
//   Rolling-ball blends from solid-modelling practice. The 45° bed-edge chamfer follows the FDM overhang
//   rule, which is a calibrated heuristic.
//
// Notice
//   - Concave edges are filleted before convex ones by default; the order is a recorded decision.
//   - fillet.tooLarge reports the largest radius that would work, not just "failed".
//   - The radius slot takes a lambda per edge, and the shape slot can wrap ctx.default.
//   - Print opinion: bed edges get a 45° chamfer (no overhang, absorbs elephant's foot), not a fillet.
//
// Results in `// →` comments show the illustrative shape of a result.

import { j, mm, deg, lw, layer } from 'jig'

const base = j.sketch('base', { on: j.plane.XY }).rect('r', 60, 40, { center: true })
const block = j.part('caddy')
  .params({ wall: mm(2) })
  .extrude(base.profiles(), mm(30), { id: 'body' })                     // 72'000 mm³

// ── 1. Fillets are local ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
const corners = j.feat('body').sideFaces().edges('|Z').expect(4)
const rounded = block.fillet(corners, mm(5), { id: 'corners' })

const R = j.compile(rounded)
R.metric('volume')               // → 71'356 mm³ = 72'000 − 4 · (1 − π/4) · 5² · 30
R.genealogy('corners/face[body/side[base.r.top] ∩ body/side[base.r.right]]')
// → { feature: 'corners', kind: 'fillet', from: ['body/side[base.r.top]', 'body/side[base.r.right]'], radius: 5 mm }
R.trace.filter(t => t.level === 'L4').map(t => [t.pass, t.note])
// → [['feature:body', 'extrude, 6 faces'], ['feature:corners', 'fillet, 4 edges; modified 6 faces; 0 faces renamed']]

// ── 2. Concave before convex ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
const mount = j.part('mount')
  .extrude(j.sketch('p', { on: j.plane.XY }).rect('r', 50, 30, { center: true }).profiles(), mm(4), { id: 'plate' })
  .extrude(j.sketch('b', { on: j.feat('plate').endFace() }).circle('c', 6, { at: [0, 0] }).profiles(), mm(10), { id: 'boss' })
  .fillet(j.feat('boss').edges('%circle'), mm(1.5), { id: 'blend' })   // the root (concave) and the rim (convex)

j.compile(mount).decisions.find(d => d.at === 'blend')
// → { at: 'blend', kind: 'fillet.order', chose: ['boss/side ∩ plate/end (concave)', 'boss/side ∩ boss/end (convex)'],
//     reason: 'concave first: the root blend adds material, so the rim keeps a full face to roll on' }

// ── 3. Too large: report the feasible maximum ────────────────────────────────
const tooBig = mount.fillet(j.feat('plate').sideFaces().edges('|Z'), mm(20), { id: 'huge' })
j.compile(tooBig).diagnostics
// → [{ level: 'error', kind: 'fillet.tooLarge', at: 'huge',
//      message: 'r = 20 mm exceeds 15 mm on 4 edges: two fillets share each 30 mm side',
//      fix: 'r ≤ 15 mm (a full round end); 14.9 mm keeps a 0.2 mm flat' }]

// ── 4. Per-edge radius, and a shape slot that wraps the default ──────────────
const soft = block.fillet(
  j.feat('body').sideFaces().edges('|Z').or(j.feat('body').endFace().edges()),
  (edge, ctx) => edge.convex ? (edge.length.gt(mm(35)) ? mm(3) : mm(2)) : mm(1),
  { shape: (edge, ctx) => edge.length.gt(mm(50)) ? 'g2' : ctx.default, id: 'soft' })   // curvature-continuous on long, visible edges

j.compile(soft).feature('soft').edges.map(e => [e.name, e.radius, e.shape])
// → [['body/side[base.r.top] ∩ body/end', 3 mm, 'g2'], ['body/side[base.r.right] ∩ body/end', 3 mm, 'rolling-ball'],
//    …, ['body/side[base.r.top] ∩ body/side[base.r.right]', 2 mm, 'rolling-ball'], …]   (60 mm edges: g2; 40 mm: default)

// ── 5. Bed edges: chamfer, not fillet ────────────────────────────────────────
const bedEdges = j.sel.faces('<Z').of('caddy').edges()
const bedRound = block.fillet(bedEdges, mm(3), { id: 'bedRound' })
const bedChamfer = block.chamfer(bedEdges, mm(0.4), { angle: deg(45), id: 'bedChamfer' })

j.compile(j.print('a', { parts: [bedRound] })).diagnostics
// → [{ level: 'warning', kind: 'print.overhang', at: 'bedRound',
//      message: 'fillet on bed edges: the lowest 0.88 mm of the 3 mm round overhangs > 45° (90° at the bed)',
//      fix: 'chamfer at 45° instead: block.chamfer(bedEdges, mm(3), { angle: deg(45) })' }]
j.compile(j.print('b', { parts: [bedChamfer] })).diagnostics     // → []

// preset.fdm does this for you, using s.bed(): the edges on the plate in the chosen orientation.
// Orientation is decided by the print job, so this is one of the fixpoints in 21.
j.compile(j.print('c', { parts: [block.use(j.preset.fdm)] })).decisions.find(d => d.kind === 'bedChamfer')
// → { at: 'caddy', kind: 'bedChamfer', chose: '0.4 mm × 45° on 4 edges', reason: 'elephant’s foot: first layers squish ≈ 0.2 mm outwards' }

// ── 6. Shell with open faces ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
const caddy = rounded
  .shell(j.feat('body').endFace(), 'wall', { direction: 'in', id: 'shell' })     // open top

const C = j.compile(caddy)
C.metric('volume')               // → 15'125 mm³ = 71'356 − (56 × 36 − 4·(1 − π/4)·3²) × 28
C.feature('shell')
// → { open: ['body/end'], thickness: 2 mm, innerCornerRadius: 3 mm (= 5 − 2), note: 'offset of a fillet is a fillet' }

// Shelling thicker than the corner radius gives sharp inner corners: max(r − t, 0).
j.compile(rounded.shell(j.feat('body').endFace(), mm(6), { id: 'thick' })).feature('thick').innerCornerRadius   // → 0 mm

// ── 7. Ribs: walls grown from a line ─────────────────────────────────────────
const divider = j.sketch('div', { on: j.plane.XZ }).line('l', [-28, 25], [28, 25])
const sorted = caddy
  .rib(divider.wire(['l']), mm(1.6), { direction: '-Z', id: 'divider' })          // grows down to the floor, out to the walls
  .chamfer(j.feat('shell').faces().edges().and(j.sel.edges('>Z')), mm(0.6), { id: 'lead' })   // lead-in for a lid

j.compile(sorted).metric('volume')   // → 17'153 mm³ = 15'125 + 1.6 × 56 × 23 (rib) − 0.18 mm² × 179 mm (inner-rim chamfer)
j.compile(sorted.use(j.rules.fdm)).diagnostics
// → []   (rib 1.6 mm = 3.6 lw ≥ 2 lw; walls 2 mm; no overhangs beyond 45° with the open top up)

10 Patterns as group actions

10-patterns-group-actions.js · 115 lines
// 10 · Patterns as group actions
//
// Model
//   A Pattern is a finite set of transforms G acting on a feature f: instances = { g·f | g ∈ G }.
//   linear(n) ≅ {0, …, n−1} ⊂ ℤ   grid = linear × linear ⊂ ℤ²   hex = the triangular lattice ℤ[ω], ω = e^{iπ/3}
//   circular(n) = the cyclic group Cₙ, generated by a rotation of 2π/n   mirror = C₂   circular × mirror = Dₙ (order 2n)
//   Products multiply counts: |P × Q| = |P|·|Q|. When f has a symmetry of its own, coincident instances
//   collapse: |orbit| = |G| / |Stab(f)| (orbit–stabiliser).
//   filter restricts G to a subset. vary attaches a parameter override to each g, so instances stop being congruent.
//
// Grounding
//   Group actions and the orbit–stabiliser theorem; pattern features as in Fusion and FreeCAD.
//
// Notice
//   - A pattern is a value: build it once, reuse it in a sketch, a part or an assembly.
//   - Partial arcs are subsets of a cyclic group, not groups; the law reports closure honestly.
//   - Coincident instances are de-duplicated and recorded as a decision, not silently fused.
//   - A failing instance is skipped with a warning while iterating, and is an error under preset.production.
//
// Results in `// →` comments show the illustrative shape of a result.

import { j, mm, deg, lw } from 'jig'

// ── 1. Linear, graded with .vary: a drill-bit stand ──────────────────────────
const stand = j.part('drill-stand')
  .params({ d: mm(1) })
  .extrude(j.sketch('base', { on: j.plane.XY }).rect('r', 104, 20, { center: true, r: 3 }).profiles(), mm(18), { id: 'block' })
  .hole([j.pt(-43.75, 0, 18)], j.hole.simple(j.fit.hole('d', 'free'), mm(15)), { id: 'bit' })
  .pattern(j.feat('bit'), j.pattern.linear(j.dir('+X'), { count: 8, step: mm(12.5) })
    .vary((inst, ctx) => ({ d: mm(1).add(mm(1).mul(inst.index)) })), { id: 'bits' })

const S = j.compile(stand)
S.feature('bits').instances.map(i => i.params.d.toString())
// → ['1mm', '2mm', '3mm', '4mm', '5mm', '6mm', '7mm', '8mm']
S.feature('bits').instances.map(i => i.modelled.d.toString())
// → ['1.7mm', …, '8.7mm']   (free class: + 2 × 0.30 mm, plus 0.10 mm hole compensation; uncalibrated defaults)
S.decisions.find(d => d.kind === 'pattern')
// → { at: 'bits', kind: 'pattern', chose: 'per-instance rebuild', reason: '.vary makes instances non-congruent; 8 hole solves' }

// ── 2. Grid = linear × linear: a pegboard ────────────────────────────────────
const gx = j.pattern.linear(j.dir('+X'), { count: 4, step: mm(25) })
const gy = j.pattern.linear(j.dir('+Y'), { count: 3, step: mm(25) })
const grid = j.pattern.grid(j.dir('+X'), j.dir('+Y'), { count: [4, 3], step: [mm(25), mm(25)] })

gx.times(gy).count                  // → 12   known before any geometry is built (orbit sizes multiply)
gx.times(gy).eq(gy.times(gx))        // → true (translations commute, so the order of the product doesn't matter)

const pegboard = j.part('pegboard')
  .extrude(j.sketch('p', { on: j.plane.XY }).rect('r', 100, 75, { r: 4 }).profiles(), mm(4), { id: 'board' })
  .hole([j.pt(12.5, 12.5, 4)], j.hole.clearance('M3', { fit: 'slide' }), { id: 'peg' })
  .pattern(j.feat('peg'), gx.times(gy), { id: 'pegs' })
j.compile(pegboard).feature('pegs').count            // → 12

// ── 3. Circular = Cₙ: a knurled knob ─────────────────────────────────────────
const c24 = j.pattern.circular(j.axis.Z, { count: 24 })
const knob = j.part('knob')
  .extrude(j.sketch('k', { on: j.plane.XY }).circle('c', 15, { at: [0, 0] }).profiles(), mm(12), { id: 'body' })
  .cut(j.sketch('g', { on: j.plane.XY }).circle('c', 1.2, { at: [15, 0] }).profiles(), { through: 'all' }, { id: 'groove' })
  .pattern(j.feat('groove'), c24, { id: 'knurl' })

c24.closed                          // → true   (24 steps of 15° return to the start: the last groove is not a duplicate of the first)

const arc = j.pattern.circular(j.axis.Z, { count: 5, angle: deg(120) })
arc.closed                          // → false  (a partial arc of 30° steps: both ends are real instances)

// ── 4. Mirror and Dₙ: the orbit–stabiliser collapse ─────────────────────────
const d6 = j.pattern.circular(j.axis.Z, { count: 6 }).times(j.pattern.mirror(j.plane.XZ))   // |D₆| = 12

const chiral = knob                                    // a model is a value: branch the knob twice
  .extrude(j.sketch('fin', { on: j.plane.XY }).polygon('t', 3, 3, { at: [20, 2] }).profiles(), mm(4), { id: 'fin' })   // off-axis: no mirror symmetry
  .pattern(j.feat('fin'), d6, { id: 'fins' })
j.compile(chiral).feature('fins').count               // → 12

const spoke = knob
  .extrude(j.sketch('sp', { on: j.plane.XY }).rect('r', 10, 3, { at: [20, 0], center: true }).profiles(), mm(4), { id: 'spoke' })
  .pattern(j.feat('spoke'), d6, { id: 'spokes' })      // symmetric about XZ: Stab = {id, mirror}
const W = j.compile(spoke)
W.feature('spokes').count                             // → 6  = 12 / 2
W.decisions.find(d => d.at === 'spokes')
// → { kind: 'pattern.dedupe', chose: 6, alternatives: [12], reason: 'mirror(XZ) fixes spoke; 6 coincident instances removed' }

// ── 5. Hex, filtered to a disk: a honeycomb vent ────────────────────────────
const lid = j.part('vent-lid')
  .params({ pitch: mm(6), web: lw(2.7) })               // web 1.2 mm on a 0.45 mm line width
  .extrude(j.sketch('l', { on: j.plane.XY }).circle('c', 26, { at: [0, 0] }).profiles(), mm(3), { id: 'lid' })
  .cut(j.sketch('cell', { on: j.feat('lid').endFace() })
    .polygon('hex', 6, '(pitch - web) / 2', { at: [0, 0], inscribed: false })   // r = across-flats / 2 = 2.4 mm
    .profiles(), { through: 'all' }, { id: 'cell' })
  .pattern(j.feat('cell'),
    j.pattern.hex(j.plane.XY, { pitch: 'pitch', rings: 5 })              // 3·5·6 + 1 = 91 centres (a centred hexagonal number)
      .filter((inst, ctx) => inst.at.sub(j.origin).norm().lte(mm(22))),  // keep centres within 22 mm
    { id: 'vent' })

const V = j.compile(lid)
V.feature('vent').count                               // → 55   (rings 0–4 contribute 1 + 6 + 12 + 18 + 18)
V.feature('vent').filtered                            // → 36
j.inspect.section(lid, j.plane.offset(j.plane.XY, mm(1.5))).area
// → 1'026 mm²   = π·26² − 55 × (√3/2)·4.8²  =  2'124 − 1'097  (open area 52 % of the disk)
j.check(V, j.rules.fdm).filter(d => d.kind === 'print.thinWall')
// → []   web 1.2 mm ≥ lw(2) = 0.9 mm

// ── 6. onFail: skip, and say so ─────────────────────────────────────────────
const postsWith = pattern => j.part('posts')
  .extrude(j.region.circle(40).subtract(j.region.rect(80, 20, { at: [-40, -40] })), mm(3), { id: 'base' })   // a disk, flat below y = −20
  .extrude(j.sketch('p', { on: j.feat('base').endFace() }).circle('c', 3, { at: [0, 32] }).profiles(), mm(10), { id: 'post' })
  .pattern(j.feat('post'), pattern, { id: 'ring' })     // instances at 90°, 150°, 210°, 270°, 330°, 30°

const c6 = j.pattern.circular(j.axis.Z, { count: 6 })
j.compile(postsWith(c6)).diagnostics
// → [{ level: 'warning', kind: 'pattern.instanceSkipped', at: 'ring[3]', message: 'instance 3 (270°, y = −32 mm) starts off the base: nothing to join',
//      fix: 'c6.skip([3]) or a .filter() that tests inst.at' }]
j.compile(postsWith(c6).use(j.preset.production)).diagnostics[0].level   // → 'error'

const intended = postsWith(c6.skip([3]))                // the same model with the intent stated: 5 posts, no warning

11 Sweeps, lofts and printed threads: frames along curves

11-sweeps-lofts-threads.js · 108 lines
// 11 · Sweeps, lofts and printed threads: frames along curves
//
// Model
//   sweep(P, γ, F) = ⋃ₛ γ(s) + F(s)·P, where F : [0, L] → SO(3) is a frame field along the path γ.
//   Frenet frame (T, N, B): built from γ′ and γ″. Undefined where the curvature κ = 0, and it flips at inflections.
//   Rotation-minimising frame (RMF): no spin about T (ω·T = 0); computed by double reflection (Wang et al. 2008).
//   The two differ by the integrated torsion: twist(Frenet → RMF) = ∫ τ ds.
//   Helix γ(t) = (r cos t, r sin t, c·t), c = pitch/2π:  κ = r/(r² + c²),  τ = c/(r² + c²).
//   loft(P₀, …, Pₙ) interpolates sections; the correspondence between their boundaries decides the twist.
//
// Grounding
//   Rotation-minimising frames by double reflection (Wang, Jüttler, Zheng & Liu 2008); the ISO metric thread
//   profile (ISO 68-1).
//
// Notice
//   - RMF is the default because Frenet breaks on straight segments and S-curves; helices are the exception.
//   - Wrapping the default with a lambda keeps RMF everywhere except where it is the wrong opinion.
//   - Thread profiles are judged against the printer: crest width versus line width, flank overhang versus layer step.
//   - Loft end conditions ('normal') make a lofted duct meet straight collars without a crease.
//
// Results in `// →` comments show the illustrative shape of a result.

import { j, mm, deg, lw } from 'jig'

// ── 1. RMF versus Frenet on an S-shaped handle ──────────────────────────────
const path = j.sketch('path', { on: j.plane.XZ })
  .spline('s', [[0, 0], [20, 15], [40, 0], [60, -15], [80, 0]], { fit: 'interp' })   // an inflection at x = 40
const grip = j.sketch('grip', { on: j.plane.normalTo(j.sel.edges().of('path'), { at: 0 }) })
  .rect('r', 12, 6, { center: true, r: 2 })

const handleWith = frame => j.part('handle').sweep(grip.profiles(), path.wire(['s']), { frame, id: 'handle' })
const H1 = j.compile(handleWith('rmf'))
const H2 = j.compile(handleWith('frenet'))

H1.feature('handle').frame       // → { kind: 'rmf', flips: 0, totalTwist: 0°, selfIntersecting: false }
H2.feature('handle').frame       // → { kind: 'frenet', flips: 1, at: [0.5], totalTwist: 180°, selfIntersecting: true }
H2.diagnostics
// → [{ level: 'error', kind: 'brep.invalid', at: 'handle', message: 'sweep self-intersects where the Frenet normal flips (κ = 0 at s = 0.50)',
//      fix: "frame: 'rmf' (the default)" }]

// ── 2. A helix, and the integrated torsion ──────────────────────────────────
const helix = j.sketch3d('coil').helix('h', { axis: j.axis.Z, r: mm(10), pitch: mm(6), turns: 5 })
// c = 6/2π = 0.955 mm   L = 5 · 2π·√(10² + 0.955²) = 315.6 mm   τ = 0.955 / 100.9 = 0.00946 /mm
// ∫ τ ds = 2π · 5 · 0.955 / √100.9 = 2.99 rad = 171°

const square = j.sketch('sq', { on: j.plane.normalTo(j.sel.edges().of('coil'), { at: 0 }) }).rect('r', 2, 2, { center: true })
const springWith = frame => j.part('spring').sweep(square.profiles(), helix.wire(['h']), { frame, id: 'coil' })
j.compile(springWith('rmf')).feature('coil').frame
// → { kind: 'rmf', totalTwist: 171°, note: 'the square section drifts 34.2° per turn relative to the axis' }
j.compile(springWith('frenet')).feature('coil').frame
// → { kind: 'frenet', totalTwist: 0° relative to the axis, note: 'N points at the axis on a helix' }

// Keep the default everywhere, except on helices: a lambda that wraps ctx.default.
const axisAware = (curve, ctx) => (curve.isHelix ? 'frenet' : ctx.default)
const spring = springWith(axisAware)

// ── 3. Printed threads: why the trapezoid prints better ─────────────────────
// A threaded rod and its nut, both with the slide fit class.
const rodWith = (spec, profile) => j.part('rod')
  .extrude(j.sketch('c', { on: j.plane.XY }).circle('c', 6, { at: [0, 0] }).profiles(), mm(30), { id: 'core' })
  .add(j.lib.thread(spec, { length: mm(25), profile, fit: 'slide' }), { at: j.feat('core').sideFaces().expect(1) })

const iso = j.compile(rodWith('M12x1.75', 'iso'))
const tr = j.compile(rodWith('Tr12x3', 'trapezoid'))

iso.feature('thread')
// → { crest: 0.22 mm (P/8), root: 0.44 mm (P/4), depth: 1.07 mm, layersPerPitch: 8.75, flankFromVertical: 60° }
tr.feature('thread')
// → { crest: 1.10 mm (0.366·P), root: 1.10 mm, depth: 1.75 mm, layersPerPitch: 15, flankFromVertical: 75° }

// The crest is the deciding feature on FDM. ISO's crest is narrower than one line width, so the nozzle
// rounds it off and engagement drops. The trapezoid's crest is about 2.4 line widths wide and survives.
j.check(iso, j.rules.fdm).map(d => d.kind)   // → ['print.thinFeature', 'print.overhang']   crest 0.22 mm < nozzle(1); flank 60°
j.check(tr, j.rules.fdm).map(d => d.kind)    // → ['print.overhang']                        flank 75°

// Both lower flanks break the 45° rule, but by different amounts. Each layer steps out by layer·tan θ:
// ISO 0.2·tan 60° = 0.35 mm < lw(1), which usually prints; trapezoid 0.2·tan 75° = 0.75 mm > lw(1), which droops.
// So the trapezoid wins on crests and loses on overhangs. A buttress profile wins on both when oriented:
// a 45° flank facing down and the steep load flank facing up.
const buttress = j.compile(rodWith('Bu12x3', 'buttress'))
buttress.feature('thread').flankFromVertical  // → { lower: 45° (the 45° variant), upper: 87° (faces up, so never an overhang) }
j.check(buttress, j.rules.fdm)                // → []

const nut = j.part('nut')
  .extrude(j.sketch('h', { on: j.plane.XY }).polygon('hex', 6, 10, { at: [0, 0], inscribed: false }).profiles(), mm(10), { id: 'hex' })
  .add(j.lib.thread('Tr12x3', { length: mm(10), internal: true, profile: 'trapezoid', fit: 'slide' }), { at: j.axis.Z, op: 'cut' })
j.compile(nut).feature('thread').modelled
// → { major: 12.9 mm (D4 12.5 + 2 × 0.2), minor: 9.4 mm (D1 9 + 2 × 0.2), flankGap: 0.2 mm per side (slide, uncalibrated) }

// ── 4. A loft with end conditions: a vacuum-hose adapter ────────────────────
const slot = j.sketch('slot', { on: j.plane.XY }).rect('r', 60, 20, { center: true, r: 3 })              // the crevice nozzle end
const round = j.sketch('round', { on: j.plane.offset(j.plane.XY, mm(50)) }).circle('c', 17.5, { at: [0, 0] })   // Ø35 hose end

const adapter = j.part('hose-adapter')
  .loft([slot.profiles(), round.profiles()], { ends: { start: 'normal', end: 'normal' }, id: 'duct' })
  .extrude(slot.profiles(), mm(-10), { id: 'collarA' })                        // straight collars meet the duct tangentially
  .extrude(round.profiles(), mm(15), { id: 'collarB' })
  .shell(j.feat('collarA').endFace().or(j.feat('collarB').endFace()), lw(4), { id: 'walls' })   // 1.8 mm walls, both ends open

const A = j.compile(adapter)
A.feature('duct')
// → { correspondence: 'seam-aligned', twist: 0°, sections: 2, ends: { start: 'normal', end: 'normal' } }
const duct = adapter.rollback('walls')                  // the timeline before shelling: the flow envelope
j.inspect.section(duct, j.plane.XY).area                // → 1'192 mm²  (60·20 − (4 − π)·3²)
j.inspect.section(duct, j.plane.offset(j.plane.XY, mm(50))).area      // → 962 mm²  (π·17.5²): 19 % less flow area
j.inspect.overhang(adapter, { dir: '+Z', max: deg(45) })
// → { faces: [], maxAngle: 14° }   (half-width 30 → 17.5 mm over 50 mm: atan(12.5/50) = 14°; prints without support)

12 Fields: signed distance, smooth blends, graded lattices

12-fields-sdf-lattices.js · 103 lines
// 12 · Fields: signed distance, smooth blends, graded lattices
//
// Model
//   A Field is f : ℝ³ → ℝ (mm), and its solid is { p | f(p) ≤ 0 }. A signed distance field has |∇f| = 1.
//   union = min, intersect = max, subtract(a, b) = max(a, −b). Pointwise, (min, max) form a distributive lattice.
//   min and max of 1-Lipschitz functions are 1-Lipschitz, so they stay safe bounds for meshing and sphere tracing.
//   smoothUnion(a, b, k) = min(a, b) − h²k/4 with h = max(k − |a − b|, 0)/k. Its gradient is a convex combination
//   of ∇a and ∇b, so it stays 1-Lipschitz. It deviates from min by at most k/4, so it → union as k → 0.
//   shell(t) = |f| − t/2   offset(d) = f − d   gyroid g = sin x cos y + sin y cos z + sin z cos x, x = 2π·pₓ/cell
//   A TPMS sheet |g| ≤ w is not a distance; jig normalises it by |∇g| so `thickness` means millimetres.
//
// Grounding
//   Signed distance fields and Lipschitz bounds (Hart 1996); polynomial smooth minimum; dual contouring (Ju
//   et al. 2002); the gyroid (Schoen 1970) in its trigonometric approximation.
//
// Notice
//   - Fields never fail a boolean: there is no topology to repair until meshing.
//   - Meshing is a lowering with a report. It names features thinner than the voxel instead of losing them silently.
//   - Grading is a lambda over space: walls thicken where the load goes and thin out where it doesn't.
//   - The mesh cache is per voxel brick, so a local edit re-meshes locally.
//
// Results in `// →` comments show the illustrative shape of a result.

import { j, mm, lw } from 'jig'

// ── 1. Distance, and the lattice laws ───────────────────────────────────────
const ball = j.field.sphere(mm(10))
const slab = j.field.box(mm(30), mm(30), mm(6), { r: mm(1) })
ball.at(j.pt(0, 0, 0))                    // → −10 mm   (inside: negative)
ball.at(j.pt(15, 0, 0))                   // → 5 mm     (the distance to the surface)

const pod = slab.union(ball.map(j.tx.move(0, 0, 8)))
const cut = slab.subtract(j.field.cyl(mm(3), mm(20)))

// union = min and intersect = max are total functions, so a field boolean never fails, and a min of distance
// fields is still a distance bound, so meshing can take safe steps (suite: field.lattice).
pod.at(j.pt(0, 0, 8))                     // → −10 mm   (inside the ball, deeper than the slab)

// ── 2. Smooth union, and its limit ──────────────────────────────────────────
const seam = j.pt(8.66, 0, 3)                        // on both surfaces: slab top z = 3 meets the sphere (√(10² − 5²) = 8.66)
;[mm(4), mm(2), mm(1), mm(0.1), mm(0)].map(k => slab.smoothUnion(ball.map(j.tx.move(0, 0, 8)), k).at(seam))
// → [−1 mm, −0.5 mm, −0.25 mm, −0.025 mm, 0 mm]      the deviation −k/4 at |a − b| = 0 vanishes with k

const blended = slab.smoothUnion(ball.map(j.tx.move(0, 0, 8)), mm(2))
blended.mesh({ voxel: mm(0.5) }).report.warnings   // → []   (polynomial smooth-min keeps the distance bound)

// A raw trig field is not a distance, and meshing says so.
const raw = j.field.fn((p, ctx) => {
  const [x, y, z] = [p.x, p.y, p.z].map(v => 2 * Math.PI * v.div(mm(5)).value)
  return mm(Math.sin(x) * Math.cos(y) + Math.sin(y) * Math.cos(z) + Math.sin(z) * Math.cos(x))
})
raw.mesh({ voxel: mm(0.5) }).report.warnings
// → [{ kind: 'field.notDistance', maxSlope: 1.9, fix: 'use j.field.gyroid(cell, { thickness }), which normalises by |∇g|' }]

// ── 3. A shelled, blended organic shape ─────────────────────────────────────
const pebble = j.field.sphere(mm(18))
  .smoothUnion(j.field.sphere(mm(14)).map(j.tx.move(22, 0, -3)), mm(8))
  .smoothUnion(j.field.capsule(j.pt(-20, 0, 0), j.pt(20, 0, 0), mm(9)), mm(6))   // rigid maps keep the distance property
const vessel = pebble.shell(lw(4)).intersect(j.field.plane(j.plane.offset(j.plane.XY, mm(8))))   // a 1.8 mm wall, open at z = 8

// ── 4. Gyroid infill, graded thicker near the load ──────────────────────────
// A bracket made the usual way, then filled with a field instead of the slicer's infill.
const bracket = j.part('bracket')
  .extrude(j.sketch('s', { on: j.plane.XZ }).polyline('L', [[0, 0], [60, 0], [60, 12], [12, 12], [12, 50], [0, 50]], { closed: true }).profiles(),
    { symmetric: mm(24) }, { id: 'body' })
  .hole([j.pt(45, 0, 12)], j.hole.clearance('M4', { fit: 'free' }), { id: 'load' })

const loadPoint = j.pt(45, 0, 6)
const infill = j.field.gyroid(mm(8), { thickness: mm(0.6) })
  .grade('thickness', (p, ctx) => mm(0.6).add(mm(1.0).mul(Math.exp(-p.sub(loadPoint).norm().div(mm(15)).value))))   // 1.6 mm at the hole → 0.6 mm far away

const filled = bracket.infill(j.sel.bodies().of('bracket'), infill.clip(j.field.sdf(bracket).offset(lw(-3))))   // inside the walls only

j.compile(filled).feature('infill1')
// → { cell: 8 mm, thickness: [0.6, 1.6] mm, relativeDensity: [23 %, 62 %]   (≈ 3.09 · t / cell),
//     selfSupporting: true, overhangArea: 0 mm² beyond 45° }
j.compile(filled).diagnostics
// → [{ level: 'info', kind: 'ref.autoId', at: 'infill1', message: 'generated id; pass { id } to reference it' }]

// ── 5. Meshing is a lowering, with a report ─────────────────────────────────
const fine = vessel.mesh({ voxel: lw(0.5) })            // 0.225 mm, dual contouring
j.compile(fine).mesh()
// → { faces: 412'880, watertight: true, manifold: true, genus: 0,
//     report: { method: 'dual-contouring', voxel: 0.225 mm, maxDeviation: 0.03 mm, featuresBelowVoxel: 0 } }

const coarse = j.compile(filled.use(j.preset.iterate))   // iterate: voxel lw(2) = 0.9 mm
coarse.diagnostics.filter(d => d.kind === 'field.featureBelowVoxel')
// → [{ level: 'warning', kind: 'field.featureBelowVoxel', at: 'infill1', message: 'gyroid walls 0.6–0.9 mm vs voxel 0.9 mm: 41 % of the sheet may vanish',
//      fix: 'mesh({ voxel: lw(0.5) }) before printing' }]

// ── 6. The per-brick cache ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
const filledWith = gain => bracket.infill(j.sel.bodies().of('bracket'),
  j.field.gyroid(mm(8), { thickness: mm(0.6) })
    .grade('thickness', (p, ctx) => mm(0.6).add(gain.mul(Math.exp(-p.sub(loadPoint).norm().div(mm(15)).value))))
    .clip(j.field.sdf(bracket).offset(lw(-3))))

const P1 = j.compile(filledWith(mm(1.0)))
const P2 = j.compile(filledWith(mm(1.4)))                // stronger near the hole; everything else identical
P1.trace.find(t => t.pass === 'field.mesh')             // → { pass: 'field.mesh', level: 'L6', ms: 2'140, cached: false, note: 'bricks 1'536' }
P2.trace.find(t => t.pass === 'field.mesh')
// → { pass: 'field.mesh', level: 'L6', ms: 310, cached: 'partial', note: 'bricks 1'536: 214 re-meshed, 1'322 cached' }
// The change is negligible beyond ~4·15 mm from the hole (e^{−4} < 2 %), so only bricks inside that radius re-mesh.

13 Mesh remixing: topology you can count, repairs you can audit

13-mesh-remix.js · 102 lines
// 13 · Mesh remixing: topology you can count, repairs you can audit
//
// Model
//   A mesh is a simplicial 2-complex (V, E, F). It is printable when it is a closed, oriented 2-manifold:
//   every edge has exactly two faces, consistent winding, no self-intersections.
//   Euler characteristic per shell: χ = V − E + F = 2 − 2g − b, where g is the genus and b the boundary loops.
//   For a closed triangle mesh E = 3F/2, so χ = V − F/2.
//   Hausdorff distance d_H(A, B) = max(sup_a d(a, B), sup_b d(b, A)) bounds what decimation or fitting moved.
//   Remixing is a pure function of a loaded, content-hashed value; attribution travels in L0.
//
// Grounding
//   Simplicial complexes and the Euler characteristic; ICP registration (Besl & McKay 1992); Hausdorff
//   distance for deviation.
//
// Notice
//   - Loading is the only effect. After `await`, the STL is a value with a hash, and every step below is cached.
//   - Every repair is reported as data: what was filled, flipped, removed. Nothing is "fixed" silently.
//   - Mesh and B-rep mix: a downloaded mesh can be the base feature of a parametric part.
//   - The licence and the original author ride along into the 3MF metadata.
//
// Results in `// →` comments show the illustrative shape of a result.

import { j, mm } from 'jig'

// ── 1. Load (the effect), then look before touching ──────────────────────────
const src = await j.load.stl('downloads/headphone-hook.stl')
src.hash                                   // → 'sha256:9f2c…e41a'   (pure from here on)

const raw = j.mesh(src)
j.compile(raw).mesh()
// → { faces: 48'212, vertices: 24'113, manifold: false, watertight: false, shells: 3, boundaryLoops: 2,
//     selfIntersections: 14, eulerChar: { main: -2, debris: [2, 2] }, genus: null (open) }
j.compile(raw).diagnostics.map(d => d.kind)
// → ['mesh.open', 'mesh.nonManifold', 'mesh.selfIntersecting']

// ── 2. Repair, with a receipt ───────────────────────────────────────────────
const fixed = raw.repair({ holes: true, normals: true, selfIntersections: true, degenerate: true, shells: 'keep-largest' })
const F = j.compile(fixed)
F.mesh()
// → { faces: 48'200, vertices: 24'100, manifold: true, watertight: true, shells: 1, boundaryLoops: 0,
//     selfIntersections: 0, eulerChar: 0, genus: 1 }        (the hook's screw hole is the one handle)
F.decisions.filter(d => d.kind.startsWith('repair'))
// → [{ kind: 'repair.holes', chose: 'fill 2 loops (38 triangles)' }, { kind: 'repair.shells', chose: 'drop 2 debris shells (12 triangles)' },
//    { kind: 'repair.selfIntersections', chose: 'resolve 14 by local remesh' }, { kind: 'repair.normals', chose: 'flip 210 faces' }]

// χ = V − E + F = 24'100 − 72'300 + 48'200 = 0 = 2 − 2g, so g = 1. A closed triangle mesh has E = 3F/2,
// so these counts are consistent; the suite checks this on every repaired mesh (mesh.euler) before slicing.

// ── 3. Cut off the old base, and cap the cut ────────────────────────────────
const trimmed = fixed.cut(j.plane.offset(j.plane.XY, mm(4)), { keep: 'above', cap: true })
j.compile(trimmed).mesh().watertight        // → true   (the cap is a planar triangulation of the cut loops)

// ── 4. Add a parametric clamp tab: mesh as the base feature of a part ──────
// A C-clamp under the hook: a 40 × 45 × 45 mm block with a desk-sized gap open towards +Y.
const hook = j.part('hook-desk-clamp')
  .params({ desk: mm(25), jaw: mm(10) })
  .import(trimmed, { id: 'remixed' })
  .extrude(j.sketch('tab', { on: j.plane.offset(j.plane.XY, mm(4)) })
    .rect('t', 40, 'desk + 2 * jaw', { center: true }).profiles(), mm(-45), { op: 'join', id: 'clamp' })   // z from 4 to −41
  .cut(j.sketch('slot', { on: j.plane.YZ })
    .rect('s', 37.5, 'desk', { at: [6.25, -18.5], center: true }).profiles(), { through: 'all' }, { id: 'jawGap' })   // y −12.5…25, z −31…−6
  .hole([j.pt(0, 6.25, -41)], j.hole.insert('M4x8.1', { kind: 'heat-set' }), { id: 'thumbscrew' })   // into the 10 mm lower jaw

const H = j.compile(hook)
H.decisions.find(d => d.at === 'clamp')
// → { kind: 'op', chose: 'join', reason: 'mesh–B-rep boolean: remixed is faceted; faces born from clamp stay exact' }
H.summary().faces                            // → { faceted: 46'930, exact: 17 }   selectors work on the exact ones

// Same remix as a pure mesh pipeline, when you don't need parameters:
const quick = trimmed.boolean('union', j.box(mm(40), mm(45), mm(45)).moved(j.tx.move(0, 0, -41)))

// ── 5. Decimate, and bound the damage ───────────────────────────────────────
const light = fixed.decimate({ ratio: 0.2, keep: 'features' })
j.inspect.hausdorff(fixed, light)
// → { max: 0.031 mm, mean: 0.004 mm, at: j.pt(12.4, -3.1, 40.2) }     well under lw(0.25) = 0.11 mm: invisible once printed
j.compile(light).mesh().faces                // → 9'640

// ── 6. Hollow for resin, with a drain ──────────────────────────────────────
const resin = fixed.hollow(mm(2), { drain: { at: j.pt(0, 0, 4.2), d: mm(3) } })
const R = j.compile(resin)
R.mesh()                                     // → { shells: 2 → 1 after the drain joins inner and outer, genus: 2, eulerChar: -2 }
j.inspect.mass(resin, { material: j.material('resin-standard') })
// → { volume: 11.2 cm³ (was 38.4), mass: 12.8 g, saved: 71 % }
R.diagnostics
// → []   (no trapped volume: every cavity reaches a drain; see j.rules.msla for the suction-cup check)

// ── 7. Back to B-rep where the geometry is prismatic ───────────────────────
const brep = fixed.toBrep({ mode: 'fit', tol: mm(0.05) })
j.compile(brep).summary()
// → { bodies: 1, faces: 41, fitted: { plane: 30, cylinder: 9, freeform: 2 }, maxDeviation: 0.048 mm }
// Now selectors work: j.sel.faces('%cylinder').radius(mm(2.1)) finds the old screw hole.

// ── 8. Attribution travels with the model ──────────────────────────────────
const mine = j.remix(hook, { from: 'alex.k / headphone-hook (Printables)', license: 'CC BY 4.0' })
j.compile(mine).ir.text('L0')
// → L0 source
//     model  hook-desk-clamp  sha256:51ab…
//     remix  of 'alex.k / headphone-hook (Printables)'  licence CC BY 4.0  input sha256:9f2c…e41a
//     edits  repair(4 kinds) · cut(z = 4 mm) · import → part · clamp · jawGap · thumbscrew
j.export.tmf(j.compile(j.print('hook', { parts: [mine] }))).report.kept
// → ['plates', 'settings', 'Designer: alex.k (original), remix by you', 'License: CC BY 4.0']

14 Printable joints and hardware: where plastic meets metal, and plastic meets itself

14-printable-joints-hardware.js · 115 lines
// 14 · Printable joints and hardware: where plastic meets metal, and plastic meets itself
//
// Model
//   A lib item is a parametric part or feature with ports (frames you can mate to) and a fit-aware size.
//   Every hole size is resolved in context: modelled Ø = nominal + 2·c(class) + holeComp(printer).
//   Cantilever snap hook (rectangular section, constant thickness), from beam theory:
//     strain at the root ε = 1.5·t·y / L²   ⇔   permissible deflection y = 0.67·ε·L² / t
//   A living hinge is a thin flexure (t ≈ 2 layers) whose life depends on the extrusion direction, not just the material.
//   Embedded parts (magnets, nuts) need a pause at the layer where the pocket is bridged over: z_top / layer.
//
// Grounding
//   Cantilever beam theory as used in snap-fit design guides (y = 0.67·ε·L²/t); insert and fastener sizes
//   from vendor tables and ISO standards.
//
// Notice
//   - Hardware sizes come from standards tables, and clearances come from the fit profile, so one design adapts per printer.
//   - j.inspect.snap uses the beam formula the design check uses; the suite tests it as snap.deflection.
//   - Orientation matters as much as geometry: hooks and hinges must bend within layers, not across them.
//   - Ports turn "put the screw here" into a frame that survives edits (used in 15).
//
// Results in `// →` comments show the illustrative shape of a result.

import { j, mm, deg, lw, layer } from 'jig'

// ── Fixture: the bottom shell of a small sensor case ─────────────────────────
const shell = j.part('sensor-case')
  .material(j.material('PETG'))
  .extrude(j.sketch('b', { on: j.plane.XY }).rect('r', 60, 40, { center: true, r: 4 }).profiles(), mm(20), { id: 'body' })
  .shell(j.feat('body').endFace(), lw(4), { id: 'walls' })                      // 1.8 mm walls, 1.8 mm floor
const floor = j.feat('walls').faces().and(j.sel.faces('+Z')).expect(1)

// ── 1. Heat-set insert bosses ───────────────────────────────────────────────
const insert = j.lib.insert('M3x5.7')
const withBosses = shell
  .add(insert.boss({ wall: lw(3) }), { at: j.frame.on(floor).moved(j.tx.move(-24, -14, 0)), id: 'boss' })
  .pattern(j.feat('boss'), j.pattern.mirror(j.plane.YZ).times(j.pattern.mirror(j.plane.XZ)), { id: 'bosses' })
  .port('lid', j.frame.on(j.feat('body').endFace()))

j.compile(withBosses).feature('boss')
// → { hole: Ø4.0 × 6.7 mm (insert 5.7 + 1.0 melt room), boss: Ø6.7 mm (4.0 + 2·lw(3)), height: 8 mm,
//     suggests: { modifier: 'walls 4 within 2 mm of the hole' } }   (picked up by the print job, see 19)

// ── 2. Screws: clearance, self-tap, and a side-loaded nut trap ──────────────
const ear = j.sketch('ear', { on: j.feat('body').sideFace('r.right') }).rect('e', 12, 8, { at: [0, 4], center: true })
const mounted = withBosses
  .extrude(ear.profiles(), mm(8), { id: 'ear' })
  .hole([j.point.center(j.feat('ear').endFace())], j.hole.clearance('M3', { fit: 'slide', depth: mm(8) }), { id: 'through' })
  .hole([j.pt(0, -14, 1.8)], j.hole.tapped('M3', { depth: mm(8), method: 'self-tap' }), { id: 'pcbScrew' })
  .hole([j.pt(-20, 0, 10)], j.hole.nutTrap('M3', { kind: 'hex', from: 'side' }), { id: 'trap' })

const M = j.compile(mounted)
M.feature('through').modelled              // → Ø3.5 mm   = 3 + 2 × 0.20 (slide) + 0.1 (holeComp)
M.feature('pcbScrew').modelled             // → Ø2.9 mm   prints ≈ 2.75 mm, so the screw cuts its own thread
M.feature('trap').modelled
// → { slot: 5.9 × 2.8 mm (AF 5.5 + 2 × 0.2; nut 2.4 + 0.4), roof: 'bridge 5.9 mm', bolt: Ø3.5 mm }
j.check(M, j.rules.fdm).filter(d => d.at === 'trap')    // → []   bridge 5.9 mm ≤ 10 mm

// ── 3. A cantilever snap-fit, and its law ───────────────────────────────────
const hook = j.lib.snap.cantilever({
  length: mm(12), thickness: mm(1.6), deflection: mm(1.0),
  material: j.material('PETG'), angle: deg(30), retention: deg(90),
})
j.inspect.snap(hook)
// → { strain: 0.0167 (1.5·1.6·1.0/12²), allowable: 0.025 (PETG), permissibleDeflection: 1.51 mm (0.67·0.025·144/1.6), ratio: 0.67 }
j.compile(mounted.add(hook, { at: j.frame.on(j.feat('walls').faces().and(j.sel.faces('-X')).expect(1)) })).metric('snapStrain')
// → 0.67   (peak strain / allowable)

const stubby = j.lib.snap.cantilever({ length: mm(8), thickness: mm(1.6), deflection: mm(1.0), material: j.material('PETG') })
j.compile(shell.add(stubby, { at: j.frame.on(floor) })).diagnostics
// → [{ level: 'error', kind: 'print.snapStrain', message: 'ε = 3.75 % > 2.5 % allowable (PETG)',
//      fix: 'length ≥ 9.8 mm at t = 1.6 mm, or thickness ≤ 1.07 mm at L = 8 mm' }]

// Orientation: the hook must bend in the XY plane of the print, or it splits along a layer line.
j.compile(j.print('case', { parts: [mounted.add(hook, { at: j.frame.on(floor) })] }).use(j.preset.functional)).summary().orientation
// → { 'sensor-case': '+Z', reason: 'functional: snap hooks bend within layers (layerStrengthRisk 0.00)' }

// ── 4. A living hinge: thickness in layers, life in line direction ──────────
const cap = j.part('flip-cap')
  .material(j.material('PP'))
  .extrude(j.sketch('c', { on: j.plane.XY }).rect('base', 30, 20, { at: [0, 0] }).rect('lid', 30, 20, { at: [31, 0] }).profiles(), mm(2), { id: 'leaves' })
  .add(j.lib.hinge.living({ length: mm(30), thickness: layer(2), material: 'PP' }),
    { at: j.frame({ origin: j.pt(30.5, 10, 0), x: j.dir('+Y'), z: j.dir('+Z') }), id: 'hinge' })
j.compile(cap).feature('hinge')
// → { thickness: 0.4 mm (2 layers), gap: 1 mm, bendRadius: 0.5 mm, mustPrint: 'flat, first layers, lines across the hinge' }
const capJob = j.print('cap', { material: j.material('PP'), parts: [cap] })
  .modifier(j.feat('hinge').faces(), { lineAngle: 'across' })           // lines along the hinge break within a few flexes

// ── 5. A dovetail with a fit class ──────────────────────────────────────────
const tail = j.lib.dovetail({ width: mm(20), depth: mm(6), angle: deg(15), fit: 'slide' })
const left = j.part('left').extrude(j.region.rect(80, 40), mm(10), { id: 'b' })
  .add(tail, { at: j.frame.on(j.sel.faces('>X').of('left').expect(1)), op: 'join', id: 'dovetail' })
const right = j.part('right').extrude(j.region.rect(80, 40), mm(10), { id: 'b' })
  .add(tail, { at: j.frame.on(j.sel.faces('<X').of('right').expect(1)), op: 'cut', id: 'dovetail' })
j.compile(right).feature('dovetail').modelled
// → { socket: 20.4 × 6.2 mm at 15°, gap: 0.2 mm per flank (slide) }   (op 'cut' gets the gap; op 'join' stays nominal)

// ── 6. A magnet pocket, closed over with a pause ────────────────────────────
const magnet = j.lib.magnet({ d: mm(6), h: mm(3) })
const tile = left.add(magnet, { at: j.frame.on(j.sel.faces('<Z').of('left')).moved(j.tx.move(0, 0, 1.0)), op: 'cut', fit: 'press', id: 'magnet' })
j.compile(tile).feature('magnet').modelled                       // → { pocket: Ø6.2 × 3.2 mm, z: 1.0–4.2 mm, closed: true (10 mm tile) }
const tileJob = j.print('tile', { parts: [tile] })
  .modifier(j.feat('magnet').faces(), { pause: 'before-cover', message: 'insert 6×3 magnet, north up' })
j.compile(tileJob).layers.pauses
// → [{ afterLayer: 21, z: 4.2 mm, message: 'insert 6×3 magnet, north up' }]   (4.2 / 0.2 = 21; layer 22 bridges the pocket)

// ── 7. Pins and ports ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
const dowel = j.lib.dowel({ d: mm(3), l: mm(10), fit: 'press' })   // a steel dowel aligning the two dovetailed halves
const pinned = left.add(dowel, { at: j.frame.on(j.sel.faces('>X').of('left')).moved(j.tx.move(0, 12, 0)), op: 'cut', id: 'pin' })
j.compile(pinned).feature('pin').modelled                        // → { hole: Ø3.2 × 5.5 mm }  = 3 + 2 × 0.05 (press) + 0.1 (holeComp)
const screw = j.lib.screw('ISO 7380', 'M3x8')
screw.port('head')                                               // → Frame at the bearing face, z along the axis
screw.port('tip')
j.compile(withBosses).node('port:lid')
// → { kind: 'port', frame: { origin: [0, 0, 20], z: '+Z' }, from: 'body/end' }   mate 'sensor-case:lid' in an assembly (15)

15 Assemblies and print-in-place: joints as subgroups, clearance as a sweep

15-assembly-print-in-place.js · 98 lines
// 15 · Assemblies and print-in-place: joints as subgroups, clearance as a sweep
//
// Model
//   An occurrence is a part placed by a transform in SE(3). A joint between two ports restricts their
//   relative transform to a subgroup H ⊂ SE(3); its DOF is dim H.
//     rigid {e}: 0 · revolute SO(2): 1 · slider ℝ: 1 · cylindrical SO(2)×ℝ: 2 · planar SE(2): 3 · ball SO(3): 3
//   Grübler–Kutzbach mobility: M = 6(n − 1 − j) + Σ fᵢ for n bodies (ground included) and j joints.
//   It counts constraints, not geometry, so special positions (coaxial hinges) make it disagree with the solver.
//   Print-in-place: components printed as one job with fit-class gaps; the joint is swept through its range
//   and the swept volume of each moving part is intersected with the rest.
//
// Grounding
//   Joints as subgroups of SE(3). Mobility by Grübler–Kutzbach is an analysis, not a law: it cannot see
//   special geometry.
//
// Notice
//   - Ports turn mates into intent: 'lid:hinge' to 'base:hinge' survives any edit to either part.
//   - The default pose puts each joint at its first limit, so the print pose is just a joint value.
//   - Making the hinge height an expression removes a whole class of collisions by construction.
//   - Joint values are parameters (named by joint id), so a pose is an override like any other.
//
// Results in `// →` comments show the illustrative shape of a result.

import { j, mm, deg, lw } from 'jig'

// ── 1. Joints are subgroups: the DOF table is data ──────────────────────────
;[j.joint.rigid(), j.joint.revolute(), j.joint.slider(), j.joint.cylindrical(), j.joint.planar(), j.joint.ball(), j.joint.snap()]
  .map(k => [k.kind, k.group, k.dof])
// → [['rigid', '{e}', 0], ['revolute', 'SO(2)', 1], ['slider', 'ℝ', 1], ['cylindrical', 'SO(2)×ℝ', 2],
//    ['planar', 'SE(2)', 3], ['ball', 'SO(3)', 3], ['snap', '{e} once engaged', 0]]

// ── 2. A clamshell box, printed open and flat ───────────────────────────────
// Two trays side by side; the hinge axis runs along X between them. Closing is a 180° rotation.
const hingeAt = z => j.frame({ origin: j.pt(0, 0, z), x: j.dir('+Y'), z: j.dir('+X') })   // the axis is the frame's z
const knuckles = j.lib.hinge.pin({ knuckles: 5, length: mm(50), d: mm(3), clearance: 'printInPlace' })

const tray = (name, side, leaf) => j.part(name)
  .params({ h: mm(15), axisZ: mm(12.5) })
  .material(j.material('PETG'))
  .extrude(j.sketch('t', { on: j.plane.XY }).rect('r', 60, 40, { at: [0, side * 22], center: true, r: 3 }).profiles(), 'h', { id: 'body' })
  .shell(j.feat('body').endFace(), lw(4), { id: 'walls' })
  .add(knuckles, { at: hingeAt('axisZ'), leaf, id: 'hinge' })                               // leaf 'a': knuckles 1, 3, 5 + pin
  .port('hinge', hingeAt('axisZ'))

const clamshell = j.assembly('clamshell')
  .params({ hBase: mm(15), hLid: mm(12), axisZ: mm(12.5) })                                 // the axis height, hard-coded for now
  .add('base', tray('base', -1, 'a'), { params: { h: 'hBase', axisZ: 'axisZ' } })
  .add('lid', tray('lid', +1, 'b'), { params: { h: 'hLid', axisZ: 'axisZ' } })
  .joint('h', j.joint.revolute({ limits: [deg(0), deg(180)] }), 'lid:hinge', 'base:hinge')   // 0° = open flat (print pose)
  .printInPlace(['base', 'lid'], { clearance: 'printInPlace' })
  .sweep('h', { steps: 36 })

// ── 3. Grübler, and when it disagrees ───────────────────────────────────────
j.inspect.mobility(clamshell)
// → { grubler: { n: 2, joints: 1, M: 6·(2 − 1 − 1) + 1 = 1 }, solverDOF: 1 }

const twoHinges = clamshell.joint('h2', j.joint.revolute(), 'lid:hinge', 'base:hinge')     // a second hinge on the same axis
j.inspect.mobility(twoHinges)
// → { grubler: { M: 6·(2 − 1 − 2) + 2 = −4 }, solverDOF: 1, redundant: 5,
//     note: 'coaxial revolutes: all 5 constraints of h2 repeat h (special geometry the formula cannot see)' }
// This is why mobility is an analysis, not a law: the formula is a count, and geometry can beat it.

// ── 4. The sweep finds a collision, and an expression removes it ────────────
// With the axis at 12.5 mm, the closed lid rim lands at 2·12.5 − 12 = 13 mm, inside the 15 mm base walls.
const P = j.compile(clamshell)
P.sweep('h')
// → { range: [0°, 180°], steps: 36, sweptInterference: 681 mm³, first: 165°, worst: 180°,
//     between: ['lid/walls', 'base/walls'] }          (wall ring ≈ 341 mm² with r 3 corners × 2 mm overlap)
P.diagnostics.find(d => d.kind === 'asm.sweptInterference')
// → { level: 'error', at: 'h', message: 'lid walls enter base walls from 165° to 180° (681 mm³)',
//      fix: 'put the axis at (h_base + h_lid) / 2 = 13.5 mm, or shorten the lid by 2 mm' }

// Closing by 180° maps z ↦ 2a − z, so the rims meet exactly when a = (h_base + h_lid) / 2. Say so:
const fixed = clamshell.params({ axisZ: '(hBase + hLid) / 2' })
const Q = j.compile(fixed)
Q.param('axisZ')                           // → { value: 13.5 mm, expr: '(hBase + hLid) / 2', src: 'params', deps: ['hBase', 'hLid'] }
Q.sweep('h')                               // → { sweptInterference: 0 mm³, minClearance: 0.4 mm (knuckle gaps, printInPlace) }
j.check(Q, j.rules.printInPlace)
// → []   gaps ≥ 0.40 mm everywhere; knuckles are conical (45°) on their lower half, so no support is needed between parts

// ── 5. Poses are overrides; occurrences carry their transforms ──────────────
j.compile(fixed).occurrence('lid')
// → { joint: 'h', value: 0°, tx: identity, note: 'print pose (first limit)' }
j.compile(fixed.override({ h: deg(180) })).occurrence('lid')
// → { joint: 'h', value: 180°, tx: rotate(axis: x through (0, 0, 13.5), 180°), bbox: [[-30, -42, 15], [30, -2, 27]] mm }
j.compile(fixed.override({ h: deg(90) })).joint('h')
// → { kind: 'revolute', value: 90°, limits: [0°, 180°], dof: 1, reactions: 'n/a (kinematics only)' }

// ── 6. Hardware, explode, BOM ───────────────────────────────────────────────
const latched = fixed
  .add('magnet', j.lib.magnet({ d: mm(6), h: mm(3) }), { qty: 2, at: j.frame.on(j.on('base', j.sel.faces('<Y').of('base'))) })   // front rim latch
  .explode([{ id: 'lid', tx: j.tx.move(0, 0, mm(30)) }, { id: 'magnet', tx: j.tx.move(0, 0, mm(15)) }])

j.compile(latched).bom({ group: 'part' })
// → [{ item: 'clamshell (base + lid + knuckles, printed in place)', qty: 1, kind: 'printed', material: 'PETG', mass: 24.3 g },
//    { item: 'magnet 6×3 mm', qty: 2, kind: 'purchased' }]
j.compile(latched).dof()                   // → { total: 1, joints: { h: 1 }, grounded: 'base' }

16 Fit: clearances calibrated to your printer, and tolerance stacks

16-fit-calibration-stacks.js · 109 lines
// 16 · Fit: clearances calibrated to your printer, and tolerance stacks
//
// Model
//   A fit class is a radial gap per side, totally ordered: press < snug < slide < free < printInPlace.
//   A printer distorts sizes; for holes the map is close to affine: actual = a · nominal + b.
//   Calibration is least squares on a printed coupon; compensation is the inverse map: model = (target − b) / a.
//   A fit profile = (printer, material, classes, compensation). It is context: fit-aware slots resolve through it.
//   Tolerances add as intervals (worst case: Σ |tᵢ|) or as random variables (RSS: √Σ σᵢ²; Monte Carlo).
//
// Grounding
//   Interval and statistical (RSS, Monte Carlo) tolerance analysis. Printed fit classes are empirical and
//   calibrated with coupons; ISO 286 covers machined parts only.
//
// Notice
//   - Defaults are honest starting points and say so (fit.uncalibrated) until a coupon replaces them.
//   - Holes are compensated by the inverse of the measured map, not by a fudge constant.
//   - Every fitted size carries provenance: class, profile, coupon and date.
//   - Every Monte Carlo sample lies inside the worst-case interval: the interval-soundness law.
//
// Results in `// →` comments show the illustrative shape of a result.

import { j, mm } from 'jig'

// ── 1. Defaults, flagged as defaults ─────────────────────────────────────────
j.fit.classes()
// → { press: 0.05 mm, snug: 0.10 mm, slide: 0.20 mm, free: 0.30 mm, printInPlace: 0.40 mm }   (radial, per side)

const pegBoard = j.part('peg-board')
  .params({ pin: mm(3) })
  .extrude(j.sketch('s', { on: j.plane.XY }).rect('r', 30, 20, { center: true }).profiles(), mm(6), { id: 'body' })
  .hole([[-8, 0], [8, 0]], j.hole.simple(j.fit.hole(j.ref('pin'), 'slide'), mm(6)), { id: 'pins' })

const P0 = j.compile(pegBoard)
P0.why(j.feat('pins').bores())
// → { value: 'Ø 3.50 mm', chain: ['pin 3.00 mm', '+ 2 × slide 0.20 mm (default class)', '+ holeComp 0.10 mm (default)'] }
P0.diagnostics
// → [{ level: 'info', kind: 'fit.uncalibrated', at: 'pins',
//      message: 'fit classes and hole compensation are defaults', fix: "print j.fit.coupon({ kind: 'pin-hole' }) and run j.fit.calibrate" }]
j.compile(pegBoard.use(j.preset.production)).diagnostics[0].level   // → 'warning'

// ── 2. Coupons: printable experiments ────────────────────────────────────────
// Coupons print with compensation off: they measure the raw printer.
const coupon = j.fit.coupon({ kind: 'pin-hole', range: [mm(0.05), mm(0.5)], steps: 10 })
const pip = j.fit.coupon({ kind: 'print-in-place', range: [mm(0.2), mm(0.5)], steps: 7 })

j.compile(coupon).summary()
// → { pins: '10 × Ø 6.00 mm', holes: 'Ø 6.10 … 7.00 mm (gap 0.05 … 0.50 mm per side)', labels: "'05' … '50' embossed",
//     printTime: 24 min, filament: 6.1 g }

// ── 3. Measure, then calibrate ───────────────────────────────────────────────
// Hole diameters measured with gauge pins; the ten printed pins average 6.04 mm (calipers).
const holes = [[6.10, 5.91], [6.20, 6.01], [6.30, 6.11], [6.40, 6.21], [6.50, 6.31],
               [6.60, 6.41], [6.70, 6.51], [6.80, 6.61], [6.90, 6.72], [7.00, 6.82]]   // [nominal, measured] mm
const outcomes = ['no-fit', 'no-fit', 'press', 'snug', 'slide', 'slide', 'free', 'free', 'loose', 'loose']

const cal = j.fit.calibrate([
  { coupon, pin: mm(6.04), holes, outcomes },
  { coupon: pip, outcomes: ['fused', 'fused', 'stiff', 'free', 'free', 'free', 'loose'] },
])
cal
// → { hole: { a: 1.0097, b: -0.252 mm, r2: 0.9999, residualSD: 0.003 mm, range: [6.1, 7.0] mm },
//     pinOversize: 0.04 mm,
//     classes: { press: 0.035 mm, snug: 0.085 mm, slide: 0.135 mm, free: 0.235 mm, printInPlace: 0.35 mm },
//     coupons: ['a3f9…', '71c2…'], date: '2026-10-12' }
// Classes are *true* gaps: (measured hole − measured pin) / 2 at the first row with that outcome,
// e.g. slide: (6.31 − 6.04) / 2 = 0.135 mm.

// ── 4. A profile: compensation is the inverse map, written as a lambda in its slot ─
const mk4petg = j.fit.profile('mk4-petg', {
  printer: j.printer('mk4'),
  material: j.material('PETG'),
  classes: cal.classes,
  holeComp: (d, ctx) => d.sub(cal.hole.b).div(cal.hole.a).sub(d),   // model − target, from actual = a·model + b
  xyComp: mm(-0.02),                                                // pins print 0.04 mm oversize in diameter
  elephantFoot: mm(0.15),
})

// ── 5. Fit-aware sizes in a model ────────────────────────────────────────────
const P1 = j.compile(pegBoard.fit(mk4petg))
P1.why(j.feat('pins').bores())
// → { value: 'Ø 3.49 mm',
//     chain: ['pin 3.00 mm', '+ 2 × slide 0.135 mm (mk4-petg)', '= 3.27 mm actual target', 'model = (3.27 + 0.252) / 1.0097 = 3.49 mm'],
//     profile: 'mk4-petg', calibrated: '2026-10-12', coupons: ['a3f9…'] }
// Same as the default for slide, by luck. For press the default was wrong:
//   default press hole 3.20 mm prints at 1.0097 · 3.20 − 0.252 = 2.98 mm: it would not take a 3 mm pin.
//   calibrated press:  (3.00 + 0.07 + 0.252) / 1.0097 = 3.29 mm.

j.fit.gap('slide').resolve({ fit: mk4petg })           // → 0.135 mm
j.fit.hole(mm(3), 'press').resolve({ fit: mk4petg })   // → 3.29 mm
j.fit.pin(mm(4), 'press').resolve({ fit: mk4petg })    // → 3.89 mm   (target 4 − 2·0.035 = 3.93, minus 0.04 oversize)
P1.diagnostics                                         // → []

// ── 6. Stacks: will this lid be free on every print? ─────────────────────────
const lidGap = j.stack('lid-gap')
  .add(mm(56).pm(0.15), { dir: +1 })                   // box inner width
  .add(mm(55.4).pm(0.10), { dir: -1 })                 // lid lip outer width
  .add(mm(0).pm(0.08), { dir: -1 })                    // elephant's-foot residual on the lip

lidGap.worstCase()   // → { nominal: 0.60 mm, range: [0.27, 0.93] mm }             Σ|tᵢ| = 0.33 mm
lidGap.rss()         // → { nominal: 0.60 mm, range: [0.40, 0.80] mm, sigma: 0.066 mm }   √(0.15² + 0.10² + 0.08²) = 0.197 = 3σ
lidGap.monteCarlo({ n: 10000, dist: 'normal', truncate: '3σ', seed: 7 })
// → { mean: 0.600 mm, sd: 0.066 mm, p001: 0.40 mm, p999: 0.80 mm, min: 0.37 mm, max: 0.83 mm }

// Every sample lies inside the worst-case interval, as it must (the suite's stack.soundness oracle).

// Per side the gap is half: 0.30 mm nominal against the calibrated free class of 0.235 mm.
// P(gap / 2 < 0.235 mm) = P(gap < 0.47 mm) = Φ((0.47 − 0.60) / 0.066) ≈ 2.4 %: a few lids will feel like 'slide'.
lidGap.monteCarlo({ n: 10000, seed: 7 }).p(g => g.lt(mm(0.47)))   // → 0.024

17-materials-mass-cost-inspect.js · 90 lines
// 17 · Materials, mass, cost, and the printability analyses
//
// Model
//   Solid mass is a volume integral: m = ρ ∫_V dV, computed on the B-rep via the divergence theorem.
//   As printed, a part is three regions: perimeters (walls · lw deep from every side face), solid top/bottom
//   skins (layers · t), and the interior at infill fraction φ:   V_print = V_walls + V_skins + φ · V_interior.
//   Filament length = V_print / (π · (1.75 mm / 2)²);   cost = mass · price.
//   Overhang, measured from vertical: a face with unit normal n and build direction u overhangs when
//   n·u < 0 and θ = arcsin(−n·u) > θ_max (vertical wall θ = 0°, downward ceiling θ = 90°).
//   Bridges are downward faces supported at both ends; islands are layers that start in mid-air.
//
// Grounding
//   Volume integrals via the divergence theorem; filament length from the filament's cross-section. As-
//   printed mass is an approximate wall-and-infill model.
//
// Notice
//   - Material is excluded from geometry cache keys: switching PLA → PETG recomputes mass, not shape.
//   - The as-printed estimate uses the same slicer settings the print job will use, so it agrees with 20.
//   - Every analysis returns located, named results that diagnostics and rules can point at.
//
// Results in `// →` comments show the illustrative shape of a result.

import { j, mm, deg, lw, nozzle } from 'jig'

// ── 1. The material library ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
const pla = j.material('PLA')
// → { name: 'PLA', density: 1.24 g/cm³, cost: 22 usd/kg, modulus: 3.5 GPa, allowableStrain: 0.02,
//     glassTransition: 60 °C, shrink: 0.003 }
const petg = j.material('PETG')       // density 1.27 g/cm³, glassTransition 80 °C, allowableStrain 0.025
const abs = j.material('ABS')         // density 1.04 g/cm³, glassTransition 105 °C, shrink 0.007
const cheapPla = pla.with({ cost: j.q('17 usd/kg') })   // a value; the library entry is unchanged

// ── 2. Solid versus as-printed ───────────────────────────────────────────────
const block = j.part('block').material(pla)
  .extrude(j.sketch('s', { on: j.plane.XY }).rect('r', 40, 40, { center: true }).profiles(), mm(20), { id: 'body' })

j.inspect.mass(block)
// → { volume: 32'000 mm³, mass: 39.7 g, filamentLength: 13.30 m, cost: 0.87 usd }

j.inspect.mass(block, { walls: 3, infill: 0.15 })   // 0.45 mm lines, 0.2 mm layers, 4 bottom / 5 top
// → { volume: 10'477 mm³, mass: 13.0 g, filamentLength: 4.36 m, cost: 0.29 usd,
//     parts: { walls: 4'174 mm³,       // 160 mm perimeter × 20 mm × 1.35 mm, less corner overlap
//              skins: 2'504 mm³,       // (40 − 2.7)² × 9 layers × 0.2 mm
//              infill: 3'798 mm³ } }   // 0.15 × 37.3² × (20 − 1.8)
// filament: 10'476 / (π · 0.875²) = 10'476 / 2.405 = 4'355 mm

// ── 3. One geometry, three materials ─────────────────────────────────────────
for (const m of [pla, petg, abs]) j.inspect.mass(block.material(m), { walls: 3, infill: 0.15 }).mass
// → 13.0 g, 13.3 g, 10.9 g          (geometry compiled once; the trace shows body cached: true twice)
j.inspect.mass(block.material(cheapPla), { walls: 3, infill: 0.15 }).cost   // → 0.22 usd

// ── 4. A probe part that fails in every interesting way ─────────────────────
const probe = j.part('probe').material(pla)
  .add(j.box(40, 20, 30), { id: 'block' })
  .add(j.box(15, 20, 5), { at: j.tx.move(40, 0, 25), id: 'ledge' })         // a cantilever ledge
  .add(j.box(3, 20, 6), { at: j.tx.move(52, 0, 19), id: 'lip' })            // a lip hanging under its tip
  .add(j.box(12, 20, 8), { at: j.tx.move(14, 0, 6), op: 'cut', id: 'tunnel' })   // a 12 mm wide tunnel along Y
  .add(j.box(0.6, 20, 10), { at: j.tx.move(-0.6, 0, 0), id: 'rib' })        // a 0.6 mm fin on the side
  .emboss(j.region.text('v2', { size: mm(4) }), mm(0.4), { on: j.sel.faces('>Y').of('block'), op: 'join', id: 'label' })

// ── 5. Walls and thin features ───────────────────────────────────────────────
j.inspect.wall(probe, { min: lw(2) })        // lw(2) = 0.90 mm
// → { min: 0.6 mm, violations: [{ at: 'rib', t: 0.6 mm, min: 0.90 mm }] }
j.inspect.thin(probe, { min: nozzle(1) })    // nozzle(1) = 0.40 mm
// → [{ at: 'label', width: 0.36 mm, note: 'strokes of "v2" at 4 mm; below one nozzle width' }]

// ── 6. Overhangs, bridges, islands ───────────────────────────────────────────
j.inspect.overhang(probe, { dir: '+Z', max: deg(45) })
// → { area: 300 mm², faces: [
//      { name: 'ledge/bottom', theta: 90°, area: 240 mm² },   // x 40–52; the lip covers the last 3 mm
//      { name: 'lip/bottom',   theta: 90°, area: 60 mm² } ],
//    excluded: [{ name: 'tunnel/top', reason: 'bridge (supported at both ends)' }] }

j.inspect.bridges(probe, { dir: '+Z' })
// → [{ face: 'tunnel/top', span: 12 mm, length: 20 mm, max: 10 mm, ok: false }]

j.inspect.islands(probe, { dir: '+Z' })
// → [{ z: 19 mm, area: 60 mm², at: 'lip', note: 'starts below the ledge it hangs from; nothing underneath' }]

// The ledge underside is an overhang, not an island: its first layer touches the block in the same layer.
// Turn the ledge into a 45° wedge and the overhang disappears, because 45° from vertical is the limit.
const wedge = j.sketch('wedge', { on: j.plane.XZ }).polyline('p', [[40, 30], [55, 30], [55, 25], [40, 10]], { closed: true })
const probe2 = probe.suppress('ledge').suppress('lip').extrude(wedge.profiles(), mm(20), { id: 'wedge' })
j.inspect.overhang(probe2, { dir: '+Z', max: deg(45) }).area   // → 0 mm²   (wedge/bottom: θ = 45°, at the limit)

// ── 7. Bed contact, and analyses become diagnostics ─────────────────────────
j.inspect.bedContact(probe, { dir: '+Z' })   // → { area: 812 mm², regions: 1 }   40 × 20 + 0.6 × 20 (the fin is fused to the block)
j.compile(probe.use(j.rules.fdm)).diagnostics.map(d => d.kind)
// → ['print.thinWall', 'print.thinFeature', 'print.overhang', 'print.bridge', 'print.island']
