18 Orientation, overhangs and supports: optimisation on the sphere

18-orientation-supports-overhang.js · 102 lines
// 18 · Orientation, overhangs and supports: optimisation on the sphere
//
// Model
//   An orientation is a build direction u ∈ S² (plus a free rotation about u that only matters for packing).
//   Overhang is a predicate on face normals: face f overhangs under u when −n_f · u > sin θ_max (θ from vertical).
//   Support volume ≈ ∫ over overhanging area of the height down to the part or the bed (columns, or trees).
//   Choosing u is minimisation over S²: evaluate 26 candidates (cube faces, edges, corners), then refine by descent
//   along geodesics. Objectives are orders on the candidates: lexicographic and weighted orders can disagree.
//   Orientation and geometry are coupled: horizontal holes (axis ⟂ u) become teardrops, which changes overhangs.
//
// Grounding
//   The 45° overhang rule is an empirical heuristic, calibrated per printer. Choosing an orientation is
//   optimisation over directions on the sphere.
//
// Notice
//   - The default is lexicographic: support volume, then bed contact, then height. Every candidate is kept as an alternative.
//   - When two sensible objectives disagree, the disagreement is the trade-off; jig shows the break-even weight.
//   - preset.functional puts layer strength first, which needs a load: the preset takes it as a parameter.
//   - The teardrop ↔ orientation cycle is a fixpoint; the trace shows it converge.
//
// Results in `// →` comments show the illustrative shape of a result.

import { j, mm, deg } from 'jig'

// ── Fixture: an L-bracket with two screw holes and a cable hole ───────────────
const baseHoles = j.sketch('hb', { on: j.plane.offset(j.plane.XY, mm(5)) }).point('p1', [15, 18]).point('p2', [45, 18])
const cableHole = j.sketch('hc', { on: j.plane.XZ }).point('p', [30, 30])
const bracket = j.part('bracket').material(j.material('PETG'))
  .add(j.box(60, 30, 5), { id: 'base' })                                     // 60 × 30 × 5, on the XY plane
  .add(j.box(60, 5, 40), { at: j.tx.move(0, 0, 5), id: 'upright' })          // 60 × 5 × 40, total height 45
  .hole(baseHoles, j.hole.clearance('M4', { fit: 'free' }), { id: 'screws' })
  .hole(cableHole, j.hole.simple(mm(8), mm(5)), { id: 'cable' })
const job = j.print('bracket', { printer: j.printer('mk4'), material: j.material('PETG'), parts: [bracket] })

// ── 1. Overhang is a predicate on normals ────────────────────────────────────
const up = j.dir('+Z')
const overhanging = j.sel.faces().of('bracket').where(f => -f.normal.dot(up) > j.q.sin(deg(45)))
j.compile(bracket).faces(overhanging)                          // → ['cable/bore (upper 90°)']   the top of a round horizontal hole
j.inspect.overhang(bracket, { dir: '+Z', max: deg(45) }).area   // → 31 mm²: the same face (6.3 mm of arc × 5 mm deep)

// ── 2. The default: 'auto', lexicographic ────────────────────────────────────
const P = j.compile(job)
P.decisions.find(d => d.kind === 'orient')
// → { at: 'bracket', kind: 'orient', chose: '+Y',
//     reason: 'lexicographic: support 0 mm³ → bed contact 2650 mm² → height 30 mm',
//     alternatives: [                                  // scored on the current geometry: holes shaped for +Y
//       { dir: '+Y', supportVolume: 0,       bedContact: 2650 mm², height: 30 mm, printTime: 52 min },
//       { dir: '+Z', supportVolume: 206 mm³, bedContact: 1765 mm², height: 45 mm, printTime: 58 min },   // inside the round cable hole
//       { dir: '+X', supportVolume: 348 mm³, bedContact:  350 mm², height: 60 mm, printTime: 71 min },   // inside all three holes
//       …, { dir: '-Z', supportVolume: 8900 mm³ (tree; grid would be 60'000), bedContact: 300 mm², height: 45 mm, printTime: 96 min } ] }

// ── 3. Orientation as a design variable on S² ────────────────────────────────
const space = j.design({ up: j.param.dir({ samples: 26 }) }, p => job.orient(p.up))
const coarse = await j.search.grid(space, { objective: j.objective.minimize('supportVolume') })
const fine = await j.search.descent(space, { from: coarse.best.point, steps: 20 })
fine.best.point                       // → { up: '+Y' }   moved 0°: a flat face down is a local minimum for prismatic parts
// Each grid point compiles with its orientation fixed, so its holes get their own teardrops: no fixpoint needed there.

// ── 4. Two reasonable objectives disagree ────────────────────────────────────
// A shelf load pushes down on the base; the upright is screwed to a wall.
const loaded = bracket.use(j.preset.functional({
  load: { at: j.sel.faces('>Z').of('base'), dir: '-Z' },
  fixed: j.sel.faces('<Y').of('upright'),
}))
const loadedJob = j.print('bracket-loaded', { printer: j.printer('mk4'), material: j.material('PETG'), parts: [loaded] })
const loadedSpace = j.design({ up: j.param.dir({ samples: 26 }) }, p => loadedJob.orient(p.up))

const lex = j.objective.lexicographic(['supportVolume', j.objective.maximize('bedContact'), 'height'])
const weighted = j.objective.weighted({ time: ['printTime', 1], risk: ['layerStrengthRisk', 40] })   // 40 min per unit of risk

const rLex = await j.search.grid(loadedSpace, { objective: lex })
const rW = await j.search.grid(loadedSpace, { objective: weighted })
rLex.best.point                       // → { up: '+Y' }
rW.best.point                         // → { up: '+X' }
rW.table()
// → up   printTime  layerStrengthRisk  score
//   +X   71 min     0.05               73.0     the L lies flat: bending stays inside each layer
//   +Y   52 min     0.60               76.0     the base bends across its layers
//   +Z   58 min     0.80               90.0     the upright bends across its layers at the corner
// Break-even: +X costs 19 min for 0.55 less risk, so it wins whenever risk is worth more than 19 / 0.55 = 34.5 min.

// ── 5. preset.functional: strength first ─────────────────────────────────────
const F = j.compile(loadedJob)
F.summary().orientation               // → { bracket: '+X', reason: 'functional: layerStrengthRisk 0.05 (next: +Y 0.60)' }
F.metrics()                           // → { supportVolume: 0, bedContact: 350 mm², height: 60 mm, printTime: 71 min, layerStrengthRisk: 0.05 }

// ── 6. Supports, when you cannot avoid them ──────────────────────────────────
const flipped = job.orient('-Z')
j.compile(flipped.supports({ kind: 'tree', angle: deg(45) })).metric('supportVolume')   // → 8'900 mm³
j.compile(flipped.supports({ kind: 'grid' })).metric('supportVolume')                   // → 60'000 mm³  (1500 mm² × 40 mm)
j.compile(flipped.supports({ kind: 'tree', angle: deg(55) })).metric('supportVolume')   // → 8'900 mm³   (the base is flat: 90°)

// ── 7. The teardrop ↔ orientation fixpoint ───────────────────────────────────
P.trace.filter(t => ['orient', 'teardrops', 'fixpoint'].includes(t.pass))
// → [{ pass: 'orient',    level: 'L5', iter: 1, note: '+Y: support 142 mm³ (2 round screw holes) beats +Z 206 mm³, +X 348 mm³' },
//    { pass: 'teardrops', level: 'L4', iter: 1, note: 'screws.p1, screws.p2 → teardrop (axis ⟂ +Y), cable stays round' },
//    { pass: 'orient',    level: 'L5', iter: 2, note: '+Y: support 0 mm³' },
//    { pass: 'teardrops', level: 'L4', iter: 2, cached: true, note: 'unchanged' },
//    { pass: 'fixpoint',  note: 'converged in 2' }]
P.why(j.feat('screws').bores())
// → { chain: ['clearance M4 free → Ø 4.7 mm', 'axis Z ⟂ build direction +Y → 45° teardrop, tip toward +Y'], decidedIn: 'iteration 1' }

19 Split to fit, plates, colours: when the object is bigger than the printer

19-split-to-fit-and-plates.js · 105 lines
// 19 · Split to fit, plates, colours: when the object is bigger than the printer
//
// Model
//   A part fits a bed B when some orientation and placement puts its footprint inside B and its height under B_z.
//   Splitting cuts a solid S by planes into pieces Sᵢ with ∪ Sᵢ = S (volumes add exactly: Σ vol Sᵢ = vol S).
//   The seam cost of a cut plane is the area of S ∩ plane that ends up on visible faces; jig minimises it subject to fit.
//   Joints restore alignment: each dowel needs material d + 2·lw(2) around it, so thin walls get local bosses.
//   Plates are 2D bin packing of footprints (NP-hard; skyline heuristic by default).
//   Packing bound: Σ footprint areas ≤ plates × bed area, so plates ≥ ⌈Σ A / A_bed⌉.
//
// Grounding
//   Plane partitions of solids; 2D bin packing with no-fit polygons, reported against the area lower bound.
//
// Notice
//   - Splitting is a print-job decision, not a modelling one: the part stays whole and parametric.
//   - The cut position is a decision with a reason, and the rejected positions stay listed as alternatives.
//   - Hardware the split needs (dowels) joins the job automatically, so the BOM and plates stay honest.
//   - Colour and material are assigned by selector, so they survive edits like everything else.
//
// Results in `// →` comments show the illustrative shape of a result.

import { j, mm } from 'jig'

// ── Fixture: a desk tray longer than the bed ─────────────────────────────────
const tray = j.part('tray')
  .params({ L: mm(320), W: mm(140), H: mm(40), wall: mm(3) })
  .extrude(j.sketch('s', { on: j.plane.XY }).rect('r', 'L', 'W', { r: 6 }).profiles(), 'H', { id: 'body' })
  .shell(j.feat('body').endFace(), 'wall', { id: 'shell' })
  .emboss(j.region.text('DESK', { size: mm(12), font: 'Inter Black', at: [160, 70] }), mm(0.6),
    { on: j.feat('shell').faces().and(j.sel.faces('+Z')).expect(1), op: 'join', id: 'label' })   // on the floor, x ≈ 140–180
  .add(j.box(10, 10, 1.5), { at: j.tx.move(10, 10, -1.5), id: 'foot' })
  .pattern(j.feat('foot').body(), j.pattern.mirror(j.plane.offset(j.plane.YZ, mm(160))).times(j.pattern.mirror(j.plane.offset(j.plane.XZ, mm(70)))))

const mk4 = j.printer('mk4')            // bed 250 × 210 × 220 mm
const job = j.print('desk', { printer: mk4, material: j.material('PLA') })
  .add('tray', tray)

// ── 1. Too big: the diagnostic says why, and what would work ─────────────────
j.compile(job).diagnostics
// → [{ level: 'error', kind: 'print.bedFit', at: 'tray',
//      message: '320 × 140 × 41.5 mm does not fit 250 × 210 × 220 mm in any orientation (even diagonally: the bed diagonal is 326 mm)',
//      fix: "job.split('tray', { fit: 'bed' })" }]

// ── 2. Split: the default chooses the cut and the joints ─────────────────────
const split = job.split('tray', { fit: 'bed', by: 'auto', joint: j.lib.dowel({ d: mm(4), l: mm(12), fit: 'press' }) })
const S = j.compile(split)

S.decisions.find(d => d.kind === 'split')
// → { at: 'tray', kind: 'split', chose: 'plane x = 130 mm',
//     reason: 'seam 642 mm² (same for every x-cut), avoids label (x 140–180), both pieces fit (130 and 190 ≤ 250)',
//     alternatives: [{ plane: 'x = 160', rejected: 'cuts through label' }, { plane: 'y = 70', rejected: '2 cuts needed (320 > 250)' }] }
// seam = floor 140 × 3 + two walls 2 × 3 × 37 = 420 + 222 = 642 mm²
S.metric('seamArea')                    // → 642 mm²

S.decisions.filter(d => d.kind === 'joint')
// → [{ kind: 'joint', chose: '3 × dowel Ø4 × 12 (press)', reason: 'two walls + floor centre' },
//    { kind: 'boss', chose: '3 × Ø 8 mm boss, 12 mm long each side', reason: 'dowel needs 4 + 2 × 0.9 = 5.8 mm of material; wall is 3 mm' }]
S.bom()
// → [{ part: 'tray.a', qty: 1 }, { part: 'tray.b', qty: 1 }, { part: 'dowel Ø4×12', qty: 3, source: 'printed' }]

S.body('tray.a').volume().add(S.body('tray.b').volume()).sub(S.feature('bosses').volume)
  .eq(j.compile(tray).metric('volume'))   // → true   (the halves partition the tray; the suite checks split.partition)

// ── 3. Choosing the cut yourself: wrap the default ───────────────────────────
// Keep the default's choice unless the cut lands within 20 mm of a foot.
const careful = job.split('tray', {
  fit: 'bed',
  by: (part, ctx) => {
    const cut = ctx.default(part)
    return j.inspect.distance(cut, j.feat('foot').faces()).lt(mm(20)) ? j.plane.offset(j.plane.YZ, mm(120)) : cut
  },
})
j.compile(careful).decisions.find(d => d.kind === 'split').chose   // → 'plane x = 130 mm'   (feet are at x 10–20 and 300–310)

// ── 4. Plates: packing the job ───────────────────────────────────────────────
const bin = j.part('bin').extrude(j.sketch('b', { on: j.plane.XY }).rect('r', 40, 40, { r: 4 }).profiles(), mm(30), { id: 'body' })
  .shell(j.feat('body').endFace(), mm(1.6), { id: 'shell' })

const batch = split
  .add('bin', bin, { qty: 6 })
  .plates({ pack: 'skyline', spacing: mm(5) })

const B = j.compile(batch)
B.plates
// → [{ plate: 1, items: ['tray.b (190 × 140)', 'bin × 1', 'dowel × 3'], utilisation: 0.54 },
//    { plate: 2, items: ['tray.a (130 × 140)', 'bin × 5'], utilisation: 0.50 }]
// The halves cannot share a plate: side by side needs 130 + 5 + 190 = 325 mm > 250 (or 140 + 5 + 140 = 285 > 210 stacked).

B.plates.lowerBound
// → { footprints: 54'544 mm², bedArea: 52'500 mm², plates: 2 }   and the packer used 2
// Σ A = 26'600 + 18'200 + 6 × 1'600 + 3 × 48 = 54'544 mm² → ⌈54'544 / 52'500⌉ = 2: the skyline packing is optimal here.

// ── 5. Colour and material by selector ───────────────────────────────────────
const styled = batch
  .color(j.on('tray', j.feat('label').faces()), 'white')                        // a filament swap for the label layers
  .color(j.on('tray', j.sel.bodies().minus(j.feat('label').body())), 'black')
  .material(j.on('tray', j.feat('foot').body()), j.material('TPU-95A'))         // soft feet, a second material

j.compile(styled).summary()
// → { plates: 2, colors: { black: 'tray, bins, dowels', white: 'label' }, materials: { PLA: 'tray, bins, dowels', 'TPU-95A': '4 feet' },
//     swaps: 6 (label on tray.b: 3 layers × 2 swaps, plate 1 only), purge: 4.1 g, printTime: 9 h 40 min }
j.compile(styled).diagnostics
// → [{ level: 'warning', kind: 'print.firstLayer', at: 'tray.a/foot', message: 'TPU feet start on the first layer; PLA–TPU adhesion is weak on the bed side',
//      fix: 'print feet separately or move them 0.2 mm up into the floor' }]

20 Slicing, cusp height, adaptive layers, 3MF and G-code

20-slicing-cusp-3mf.js · 98 lines
// 20 · Slicing, cusp height, adaptive layers, 3MF and G-code
//
// Model
//   Slicing is a family of level sets: layer k is S_k = M ∩ { z = (k + ½)·t }, a planar region printed t thick.
//   Σ area(S_k)·t is the midpoint rule for ∫ area(z) dz, so it converges to the volume as t → 0 with error O(t²)
//   (Cavalieri again; see 06).
//   Cusp height (the stair-step error) on a face whose normal makes angle θ with the build direction: c = t·|cos θ|.
//   Adaptive layers invert it: t(z) = clamp(c_max / max |cos θ| over faces at height z, t_min, t_max).
//   Print time ≈ Σ toolpath length / speed + per-layer overheads, so it grows with layer count, weighted by area.
//
// Grounding
//   Planar sectioning for layered manufacturing; cusp height (Dolenc & Mäkelä 1994); the layer sum is
//   Cavalieri again.
//
// Notice
//   - The slice law and the cusp law are checks on the slicer, the same way Cavalieri checks the kernel.
//   - Horizontal faces are snapped to layer boundaries, so their cusp is 0 and features keep their heights.
//   - G-code flavour is a four-way slot: a lambda can wrap the default, here to pause for an insert.
//   - Every export says what it kept, approximated and dropped.
//
// Results in `// →` comments show the illustrative shape of a result.

import { j, mm, turn } from 'jig'

// ── Fixture: a dome paperweight with a cavity for steel shot and three inserts underneath ─
const weight = j.part('weight').material(j.material('PLA'))
  .revolve(j.sketch('q', { on: j.plane.XZ }).arc('a', { center: [0, 0], start: [40, 0], end: [0, 40] })
    .line('l1', 'a.end', [0, 0]).line('l2', [0, 0], 'a.start').profiles(), j.axis.Z, turn(1), { id: 'dome' })
  .revolve(j.sketch('cav', { on: j.plane.XZ }).polyline('p', [[0, 3], [15, 3], [15, 13], [0, 28]], { closed: true }).profiles(),
    j.axis.Z, turn(1), { op: 'cut', id: 'cavity' })              // a 45° conical roof prints without support
  .hole(j.sketch('ins', { on: j.plane.XY }).point('c', [25, 0]).pattern(['c'], j.pattern.circular(j.axis.Z, { count: 3 })),
    j.hole.insert('M3x5.7', { kind: 'heat-set' }), { id: 'inserts' })

// volume = ⅔π·40³ − (π·15²·10 + ⅓π·15²·15) − 3·π·2²·6.7 = 134'041 − 10'603 − 253 = 123'186 mm³   (dome − cavity − insert holes)

const job = j.print('weight', { printer: j.printer('mk4'), material: j.material('PLA'), parts: [weight] })
const P = j.compile(job)

// ── 1. Layers are level sets ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
P.layers.length                        // → 200   (40 mm / 0.2 mm)
P.layers[0]                            // → { k: 0, z: [0, 0.2] mm, area: 4'989 mm², regions: 1, holes: 3 }   π·40² − 3 insert holes
P.layers[15]                           // → { k: 15, z: [3.0, 3.2] mm, area: 4'252 mm², regions: 1, holes: 4 }   the cavity appears at z = 3

P.layers.reduce((v, L) => v.add(L.area.mul(mm(0.2))), j.q('0 mm^3'))
// → 123'190.2 mm³   against the exact 123'185.8 mm³: Σ area · t is Cavalieri again, with error O(t²).
//   The slicer gets an as-printed volume for free, and the suite uses the comparison as slice.volume.

// ── 2. Cusp height ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// On the dome, cos θ = z / R: vertical at the equator (no stairs), flat at the pole (a full layer).
// Cusp height = t · |cos θ| (Dolenc & Mäkelä 1994). It costs nothing to evaluate, so adaptive slicing uses it
// to pick each layer's height (section 3), and the suite compares it with the measured stair steps (slice.cusp).
P.metrics()
// → { layers: 200, cuspMax: 0.20 mm, cuspMean: 0.10 mm, printTime: 190 min, filament: 52 g, supportVolume: 0 }
// cuspMean = 0.2 · mean(z / R) = 0.1 mm: on a sphere, area is uniform in z (Archimedes), so mean(z / R) = ½.

// ── 3. Adaptive layers: spend layers where the surface is flat ───────────────
const smooth = job.slice({ adaptive: { maxCusp: mm(0.05), min: mm(0.05), max: mm(0.3) } })
const A = j.compile(smooth)
A.metrics()
// → { layers: 411, cuspMax: 0.05 mm, printTime: 300 min }
// t(z) = min(0.3, 0.05 · 40 / z) = min(0.3, 2 / z): 0.3 mm up to z = 6.7 mm, then thinner towards the pole.
// layers = 6.7 / 0.3 + ∫ z/2 dz from 6.7 to 40 = 22 + 389 = 411
j.compile(job.slice({ layer: mm(0.05) })).metrics()
// → { layers: 800, cuspMax: 0.05 mm, printTime: 760 min }   the same surface quality, 2.5× the time
A.layers.filter(l => l.snapped).map(l => l.z[1])
// → [3.0 mm, 13.0 mm]   cavity floor and roof start: horizontal faces stay layer boundaries

// ── 4. Per-region settings: modifiers ────────────────────────────────────────
const strong = smooth.modifier(j.on('weight', j.feat('inserts').bores()),
  { grow: mm(3), walls: 6, infill: { density: 0.6 } })     // solid material for heat-set inserts to melt into
j.compile(strong).summary().modifiers
// → [{ region: 'inserts.bores ⊕ 3 mm', bodies: 3, walls: 6, infill: 0.6, addedTime: 4 min, addedFilament: 1.1 g }]

// ── 5. G-code: flavours, and a lambda that wraps one ─────────────────────────
const G = j.compile(strong)
G.gcode({ flavor: 'marlin' }).report
// → { kept: ['toolpaths', 'temperatures', 'fan', 'progress M73'], approximated: ['arcs as segments'], dropped: ['part names'] }
G.gcode({ flavor: 'klipper' }).report.kept
// → ['toolpaths', 'temperatures', 'fan', 'EXCLUDE_OBJECT labels per part']

// Pause before the cavity roof closes, to pour in the steel shot.
const withPause = G.gcode({
  flavor: (lyr, ctx) => lyr.z[0].eq(mm(13)) ? ['M0 Pour steel shot into the cavity', ...ctx.default(lyr)] : ctx.default(lyr),
})
withPause.report.notes                 // → ['custom flavor: wraps marlin; 1 layer modified (k = 53, z = 13.0 mm)']
// k = 53: 22 layers of 0.3 mm up to z = 6.7, then ∫ z/2 dz from 6.7 to 13 = 31 adaptive layers

// ── 6. 3MF and STL: what survives the trip ───────────────────────────────────
const tmf = j.export.tmf(G, { plates: true, settings: true, colors: true })
tmf.report
// → { kept: ['units (mm)', 'plates', 'part names', 'slicer settings incl. adaptive layers', 'modifiers', 'colors'],
//     approximated: ['B-rep → mesh: 21'340 triangles, max deviation 0.008 mm'],
//     dropped: ['parametric history', 'persistent names', 'fit provenance'] }
const stl = j.export.stl(G, { chord: mm(0.01), binary: true })
stl.report
// → { kept: ['geometry'], approximated: ['B-rep → mesh: 21'340 triangles, max deviation 0.008 mm'],
//     dropped: ['units (STL has none; assumed mm)', 'settings', 'modifiers', 'plates', 'part names', 'pause'] }

21 The compiler: IR levels, caching, fixpoints, staging, honest exports

21-compiler-ir-cache-fixpoint-io.js · 127 lines
// 21 · The compiler: IR levels, caching, fixpoints, staging, honest exports
//
// Model
//   compile = L0 source → L1 feature graph → L2 resolved → L3 solved sketches → L4 topology → L5 world → L6 products.
//   Each pure unit of work (a sketch, a feature, a mesh, a layer) is cached under a content hash of everything
//   that can change its output, and nothing else. A change invalidates only its downstream cone.
//   Cycles (orientation ⇄ teardrops, in-context sizes) are fixpoints: iterate until values stop changing, cap at 4.
//   Staging splits the work: finite unknowns are tabulated now, continuous ones become a residual program.
//   Exports are lowerings; each reports what it kept, approximated and dropped.
//
// Grounding
//   Compiler practice: content-addressed caching, fixpoint iteration, and partial evaluation for staging.
//
// Notice
//   - Every level has a text dump and a JSON form; the IR bundle ships them together for review, bug reports and agents.
//   - The trace shows cached: true where the cache hit, so you can see why a rebuild was fast or slow.
//   - Non-convergence is a diagnostic with the cycle in it, never a hang.
//   - Determinism is a law: the same model hashes to the same products.
//
// Results in `// →` comments show the illustrative shape of a result.

import { j, mm, deg } from 'jig'

// ── Fixture: a print-in-place hinged box with S/M/L configurations ───────────
const box = j.part('box')
  .params({ w: mm(60), d: mm(40), h: mm(30), wall: mm(2) })
  .extrude(j.sketch('base', { on: j.plane.XY }).rect('r', 'w', 'd').profiles(), 'h', { id: 'body' })
  .shell(j.feat('body').endFace(), 'wall', { id: 'shell' })
  .port('hinge', j.frame.on(j.feat('body').sideFace('r.top').edges('>Z').expect(1)))
const lid = j.part('lid')
  .params({ w: mm(60), d: mm(40), t: mm(2), label: 'PARTS' })
  .extrude(j.sketch('ls', { on: j.plane.XY }).rect('r', 'w', 'd').profiles(), 't', { id: 'plate' })
  .emboss(j.region.text(j.ref('label'), { size: mm(8) }), mm(0.6), { on: j.feat('plate').endFace(), op: 'cut', id: 'label' })
  .port('hinge', j.frame.on(j.feat('plate').sideFace('r.top').edges('<Z').expect(1)))
const kitOf = label => j.assembly('hinged-box')
  .params({ w: mm(60), d: mm(40), h: mm(30), label })
  .configs({ S: { w: mm(40), d: mm(30), h: mm(20) }, L: { w: mm(90), d: mm(60), h: mm(40) } })
  .add('box', box, { ground: true, params: { w: 'w', d: 'd', h: 'h' } })
  .add('lid', lid, { params: { w: 'w', d: 'd', label: 'label' } })
  .add('pin', j.lib.hinge.pin({ knuckles: 5, clearance: 'printInPlace' }), { params: { length: 'w' } })
  .joint('hinge', j.joint.revolute({ limits: [deg(0), deg(180)] }), 'box:hinge', 'lid:hinge')
  .printInPlace(['box', 'lid', 'pin'], { pose: { hinge: deg(180) } })      // printed open, lid flat beside the box
const jobOf = kit => j.print('hinged-box', { printer: j.printer('mk4'), material: j.material('PETG'), parts: [kit] }).fit('mk4-petg')

const job = jobOf(kitOf('PARTS'))
const P = j.compile(job)

// ── 1. Seven levels, each answering one question ────────────────────────────
P.ir.text('L0')   // What was asked?
// → print 'hinged-box' #9c41e2 · printer mk4 #11ab · material PETG #04cd · fit 'mk4-petg' #a3f9 (2026-10-12)
//   └─ assembly 'hinged-box' #c310  params { w: 60 mm, d: 40 mm, h: 30 mm, label: 'PARTS' }  configs [S, L]
//      ├─ part 'box' #5e02    ├─ part 'lid' #77d1    └─ lib hinge.pin@1.2 #e0a7
P.ir.text('L1')   // What operations, on what references?
// → box: base(sketch) → body(extrude h) → shell(wall)              port hinge ← body/side[base.r.top] edge >Z
//   lid: ls(sketch) → plate(extrude t) → label(emboss, cut)        port hinge ← plate/side[ls.r.top] edge <Z
//   hinged-box: hinge = revolute(box:hinge, lid:hinge) [0°, 180°] · printInPlace {box, lid, pin} @ hinge = 180°
//   job: orient(auto) ⇄ teardrops · slice(default) · plates(skyline)
P.ir.text('L2')   // What value, and why?
// → box.w = 60 mm ← hinged-box.w (bound in add) ← params      box.wall = 2 mm ← box.params
//   hinge.clearance = 0.35 mm ← fit 'mk4-petg'.printInPlace (calibrated 2026-10-12, coupon 71c2…)
P.ir.text('L3')   // Are the sketches determined?
// → base: 4 lines, 8 → 0 DOF, fully · ls: 4 lines, 8 → 0 DOF, fully
P.ir.text('L4', { node: 'box' })   // What topology, from where?
// → box/body1: 11 faces · 24 edges · 16 vertices · 12 loops · Euler–Poincaré 16 − 24 + 11 − 1 − 2 = 0 ✓
//   body/start · body/side[base.r.top] · … · body/end ∖ shell (the rim, 2 loops) · shell/floor · shell/wall[base.r.top] · …
P.ir.text('L5')   // Where is everything?
// → box @ identity (ground) · lid @ rot(hinge axis, 180°), gap 0.35 mm · pin @ hinge axis · DOF 1
//   plate 1: hinged-box '+Z' as posed: support 0 mm³, bed contact 4'690 mm² · teardrops: 5 knuckle bores (axis X ⟂ Z)
P.ir.text('L6')   // What goes to the printer?
// → plate 1: 18'204 triangles (max deviation 0.008 mm) · 150 layers × 0.2 mm · supports 0 · 2 h 05 min · 41 g PETG
//   3MF 412 kB · G-code (marlin) 1.9 MB

// ── 2. Change one thing; watch the cache ─────────────────────────────────────
const P2 = j.compile(jobOf(kitOf('SCREWS')))
P2.trace
// → [{ pass: 'parse',    level: 'L1', ms: 0.4 },
//    { pass: 'resolve',  level: 'L2', ms: 0.1, note: "1 change: lid.label 'PARTS' → 'SCREWS'" },
//    { pass: 'sketch',   level: 'L3', ms: 0.0, cached: true, note: '2/2' },
//    { pass: 'features', level: 'L4', ms: 41,  cached: 'partial', note: '5/6 cached; recomputed lid.label' },
//    { pass: 'world',    level: 'L5', ms: 3.2, cached: false, note: 'lid geometry changed: joints re-solved, sweep re-checked' },
//    { pass: 'orient',   level: 'L5', ms: 0.9, cached: false, note: 'same result: +Z' },
//    { pass: 'teardrops', level: 'L4', ms: 0.0, cached: true },
//    { pass: 'fixpoint', note: 'converged in 1 (orientation unchanged)' },
//    { pass: 'mesh',     level: 'L6', ms: 12,  cached: 'partial', note: 'box, pin cached; lid re-meshed' },
//    { pass: 'slice',    level: 'L6', ms: 22,  cached: 'partial', note: '3/150 layers recomputed: the label lies in z 0–0.6 on the bed face' }]
P2.metric('cacheHitRate')   // → 0.86

P2.feature('lid.label').cache
// → { key: 'f3a0…',
//     includes: { type: 'emboss', params: { depth: 0.6 mm, text: 'SCREWS', size: 8 mm, font: 'Inter Regular@4.0' },
//                 inputs: ['lid/plate body #77d1…'], refs: ['plate/end'], strategy: 'default', fit: {}, tol: '1e-7 mm', tables: [] },
//     excludes: ['color', 'material', 'display name'] }

// ── 3. Fixpoints: converging, and refusing to loop ───────────────────────────
P.trace.find(t => t.pass === 'fixpoint')   // → { pass: 'fixpoint', note: 'converged in 2' }   (iteration 2 confirmed '+Z' with teardrops)

const fickle = job.orient((part, ctx) => ctx.previous?.dir === '+X' ? '+Y' : '+X')   // a lambda that always flips
j.compile(fickle).diagnostics
// → [{ level: 'error', kind: 'fixpoint.notConverged', at: 'orient',
//      message: 'orient ⇄ teardrops did not converge in 4 iterations: +X → +Y → +X → +Y',
//      fix: 'make the orient lambda independent of the previous decision, or fix a direction' }]

// ── 4. Staging: tabulate the finite, leave the continuous for run time ──────
const live = j.stage(job)
live.tabulated              // → { config: ['default', 'S', 'L'], compiled: 3, ms: 410 }
live.residual               // → { joints: ['hinge: revolute angle, continuous'], metrics: ['sweptInterference', 'minClearance'] }
live.at({ config: 'L', hinge: deg(80) })
// → { ms: 0.6, solved: 'hinge only (warm start)', sweptInterference: 0 mm³, minClearance: 0.33 mm }

// ── 5. Exports are lowerings, with reports ───────────────────────────────────
j.export.step(P, { schema: 'AP242' }).report
// → { kept: ['exact B-rep per part', 'assembly structure', 'names', 'colors'], approximated: [],
//     dropped: ['plates', 'slicer settings', 'fit provenance'] }
j.export.tmf(P).report
// → { kept: ['units', 'plates', 'settings', 'part names'], approximated: ['B-rep → mesh, max deviation 0.008 mm'],
//     dropped: ['parametric history', 'persistent names', 'joints'] }
j.export.stl(P, { perPart: true }).report
// → { kept: ['geometry (3 files)'], approximated: ['B-rep → mesh, max deviation 0.008 mm'],
//     dropped: ['units (assumed mm)', 'plates', 'settings', 'pose (parts exported in their own frames)'] }

// ── 6. The IR bundle, and determinism ────────────────────────────────────────
j.export.ir(P)
// → { files: ['manifest.json', 'trace.json', 'diagnostics.json', 'decisions.json',
//             'L0.txt', 'L0.json', 'L1.txt', 'L1.json', …, 'L6.txt', 'L6.json'], bytes: 1.4 MB }
j.hash(j.compile(job)) === j.hash(j.compile(job))
// → true   (the hash covers L1–L6 products, not trace timings; the suite runs this as compile.deterministic)

30 Quick start: zero config → preset → tweak → lambda → plate

30-quickstart.js · 87 lines
// 30 · Quick start: zero config → preset → tweak → lambda → plate
//
// Model
//   Three calls give a printable result: a part, a print job, an export.
//   Every opinion on the way is a default you can see in prog.summary() and change at one of four
//   levels: tweak its params, swap a library strategy, wrap the default with a lambda, or .set() it raw.
//
// Notice
//   - Nothing here names a printer, a material or a support style, yet the output is a sliced 3MF.
//   - Defaults are visible, with provenance, before you override any of them.
//   - The same object goes from "it works" to "tuned for my printer" without being rewritten.
//
// Results in `// →` comments show the illustrative shape of a result.

import { j, mm, deg, lw, layer } from 'jig'

// ── 1. Zero configuration: a cable clip ──────────────────────────────────────
const clip = j.part('cable-clip')
  .extrude(j.sketch('s', { on: j.plane.XY })
    .rect('base', 24, 12, { center: true, r: 2 })
    .circle('hole', 1.7, { at: [-7, 0] })
    .profiles(), mm(3), { id: 'base' })
  .extrude(j.sketch('ring', { on: j.plane.XZ })
    .circle('outer', 5, { at: [4, 8] }).circle('inner', 3.5, { at: [4, 8] })
    .profiles(), { symmetric: mm(6) }, { id: 'ring' })
  .cut(j.sketch('gap', { on: j.plane.XZ }).rect('g', 3, 6, { at: [8.5, 10] }).profiles(), { through: 'all' }, { id: 'gap' })

const job = j.print('clip', { parts: [clip] })        // shorthand for j.print('clip').add('cable-clip', clip)
const P = j.compile(job)

P.summary()
// → { printer: 'generic-fdm (default)', material: 'PLA (default)', plates: 1, parts: 1,
//     orientation: { 'cable-clip': '+Z (as modelled)', reason: 'support 0 mm³; bed contact 274 mm²' },
//     holes: { 'cable-clip/hole': 'vertical → +0.1 mm compensation (fit: uncalibrated defaults)' },
//     printTime: 9 min, filament: 0.9 g, warnings: 1 }
P.diagnostics
// → [{ level: 'info', kind: 'fit.uncalibrated', message: 'using default fit classes; print j.fit.coupon() once to calibrate' }]

const { data: tmf, report } = j.export.tmf(P)
report
// → { kept: ['plates', 'settings', 'part names'], approximated: ['B-rep → mesh (max deviation 0.008 mm)'], dropped: [] }

// ── 2. A preset: functional parts get thicker walls and layer-aware orientation ─
const sturdy = j.print('clip', { parts: [clip.use(j.preset.functional)] })
j.compile(sturdy).summary().orientation
// → { 'cable-clip': '+Z', reason: 'functional: ring load path stays within layers; support 0 mm³' }

// ── 3. Tweak a default's params ──────────────────────────────────────────────
const tuned = job
  .slice({ layer: mm(0.16), walls: 4 })                 // partial params: everything else stays default
  .supports(false)

// ── 4. Swap in a library strategy ────────────────────────────────────────────
const lyingDown = job.orient('min-height')

// ── 5. Wrap the default with a lambda ────────────────────────────────────────
// Keep the default orientation, unless it would put the ring's gap facing down.
const careful = job.orient((part, ctx) => {
  const choice = ctx.default(part)
  return choice.faceDown(j.feat('gap').faces()) ? ctx.candidates(part)[1] : choice   // the default's second-best
})
j.compile(careful).decisions.find(d => d.kind === 'orient')
// → { at: 'cable-clip', kind: 'orient', chose: '+Z', alternatives: ['-Z', '+X', …], reason: 'lambda kept default (gap faces +X)' }

// ── 6. The raw escape hatch ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
const raw = job.set('slice.seam', 'rear')

// ── 7. Make it yours: a house preset is just a function ──────────────────────
const house = j.preset('house', b => b
  .with(x => x.slice({ layer: mm(0.2), walls: 3, infill: { density: 0.2, pattern: 'gyroid' } }))
  .with(x => x.supports({ kind: 'tree', only: 'buildplate' })))

const mine = j.print('clip', { printer: j.printer('mk4'), material: j.material('PETG'), parts: [clip] })
  .use(house)
  .fit('mk4-petg')                                      // a calibrated fit profile (see 16)

const M = j.compile(mine)
M.summary().holes
// → { 'cable-clip/hole': 'vertical → +0.14 mm (fit: mk4-petg, calibrated 2026-10-12, slide)' }
M.metrics()
// → { printTime: 11 min, filament: 1.0 g, cost: 0.03 usd, supportVolume: 0, cuspMax: 0.2 mm, plates: 1 }

// ── 8. And the model stays a value ───────────────────────────────────────────
const softer = clip.insertAfter('ring', b => b.fillet(j.feat('ring').edges('%circle'), mm(0.8), { id: 'soft' }))
j.diff(clip, softer)
// → { added: ['soft (fillet, 4 edges)'], changed: [], removed: [] }

31 Random-input router: whatever lands in the folder becomes a printable object

31-router-random-input.js · 140 lines
// 31 · Random-input router: whatever lands in the folder becomes a printable object
//
// Model
//   ingest.auto : Source → { kind, confidence, ranked, features }   (a classifier over file content, not file names)
//   route       : Source × (kind ↦ preset) → Model                  (presets are (data, ctx) => model)
//   Every preset is an ordinary jig model, so the routed result is a value: it hashes, diffs, compiles
//   and prints like anything written by hand. Loading is the only effect; everything after it is pure.
//
// Notice
//   - One table of six presets covers photos, silhouettes, logos, data, meshes and plain-language specs.
//   - The classifier ranks every kind. When confidence is low, build the top two and let metrics or a person decide.
//   - All routed models share one print job, so the batch packs onto plates like any other.
//
// Results in `// →` comments show the illustrative shape of a result.

import { j, mm, lw } from 'jig'

// ── 1. Six presets, one per kind ─────────────────────────────────────────────
const lithophane = (img, ctx) => j.part('lithophane')
  .add(j.ingest.heightmap(img, { size: [mm(100), mm(75)], minT: mm(0.8), maxT: mm(3.2), invert: true }))   // dark → thick
  .extrude(j.region.rect(mm(104), mm(79), { center: true })
    .subtract(j.region.rect(mm(100), mm(75), { center: true })), mm(3.2), { id: 'frame' })

const cookieCutter = (img, ctx) => {
  const shape = j.ingest.trace(img, { threshold: 0.5, smooth: mm(0.5), width: mm(80) })   // → Region
  return j.part('cutter')
    .extrude(shape.offset(lw(2)).subtract(shape), mm(15), { id: 'blade' })                // 0.9 mm blade: two perimeters
    .extrude(shape.offset(mm(5)).subtract(shape.offset(lw(1))), mm(2), { id: 'flange' })
    .chamfer(j.feat('blade').endFace().edges(), mm(0.3), { id: 'edge' })
}

const keychain = (svg, ctx) => {
  const logo = j.region.svg(svg, { width: mm(40) })
  const tag = logo.offset(mm(2.5)).union(j.region.circle(mm(5), { at: [-22, 0] }))         // body + ring tab
  return j.part('keychain')
    .extrude(tag, mm(3), { id: 'tag' })
    .cut(j.region.circle(mm(2.5), { at: [-22, 0] }), { through: 'all' }, { id: 'ring' })
    .emboss(logo, mm(1), { on: j.feat('tag').endFace(), op: 'join', id: 'logo' })
    .color(j.feat('logo').faces(), 'white')                                                // a colour change at z = 3 mm
}

const barChart = (table, ctx) => {
  const rows = table.rows                                   // [{ month: 'Jan', value: 12 }, … { month: 'Dec', value: 21 }]
  const max = Math.max(...rows.map(r => r.value))           // 31 (July)
  return j.part('chart')
    .extrude(j.region.rect(mm(100), mm(20), { center: true }), mm(3), { id: 'base' })
    .extrude(j.sketch('bar', { on: j.feat('base').endFace() }).rect('b', 6, 6, { at: [-44, 0], center: true }).profiles(),
      mm(1), { id: 'bar' })
    .pattern(j.feat('bar'), j.pattern.linear(j.dir('+X'), { count: rows.length, step: mm(8) })     // 12 bars over 94 mm
      .vary((inst, ctx) => ({ extent: mm(40 * rows[inst.index].value / max) })), { id: 'bars' })
    .emboss(j.region.text(rows.map(r => r.month[0]).join('       '), { size: mm(4) }), mm(0.4),
      { on: j.feat('base').endFace(), op: 'cut', id: 'labels' })
}

const remixWithTab = (mesh, ctx) => j.part('hook-remix')
  .import(j.mesh(mesh).repair({ holes: true, normals: true, shells: 'keep-largest' }))
  .extrude(j.sketch('tab', { on: j.sel.faces('<Z').largest() }).slot('t', [0, 0], [18, 0], 8).profiles(), mm(3), { id: 'tab' })
  .hole(j.point.center(j.feat('tab').endFace()), j.hole.clearance('M3', { fit: 'slide' }), { id: 'screw' })

const boxFromSpec = (spec, ctx) => {
  const { w, d, h, wall = lw(3) } = spec.features
  const corners = [[1, 1], [-1, 1], [-1, -1], [1, -1]]
    .map(([sx, sy]) => j.pt(w.div(2).sub(mm(5)).mul(sx), d.div(2).sub(mm(5)).mul(sy), 0))
  return j.part('spec-box')
    .params({ w, d, h, wall })
    .extrude(j.sketch('s', { on: j.plane.XY }).rect('r', 'w', 'd', { center: true, r: 3 }).profiles(), 'h', { id: 'body' })
    .shell(j.feat('body').endFace(), 'wall', { id: 'shell' })
    .add(j.lib.insert('M3x5.7').boss({ wall: mm(2) }), { at: corners })                  // "M3 screws in the corners"
}

const route = {
  'image-photo': lithophane, 'image-silhouette': cookieCutter, 'svg-outline': keychain,
  'table-csv': barChart, 'stl-mesh': remixWithTab, 'spec-text': boxFromSpec,
}

// ── 2. Load (the only effect) and classify ───────────────────────────────────
const inbox = {
  photo: await j.load.image('inbox/grandma.jpg'),
  cat: await j.load.image('inbox/cat-silhouette.png'),
  logo: await j.load.svg('inbox/club-logo.svg'),
  sales: await j.load.csv('inbox/sales-2026.csv'),
  hook: await j.load.stl('inbox/broken-hook.stl'),
  spec: await j.load.json('inbox/request.json'),   // { text: 'a box 80x60x40 mm with 2 mm walls, M3 screws in the corners' }
}

j.ingest.auto(inbox.photo)
// → { kind: 'image-photo', confidence: 0.94,
//     ranked: [['image-photo', 0.94], ['image-silhouette', 0.05], ['svg-outline', 0.01]],
//     features: { px: [1600, 1200], tones: 'continuous', bimodal: false } }
j.ingest.auto(inbox.spec)
// → { kind: 'spec-text', confidence: 0.88, features: { w: 80 mm, d: 60 mm, h: 40 mm, wall: 2 mm, hardware: 'M3', at: 'corners' } }
j.ingest.auto(inbox.sales).features
// → { columns: ['month', 'value'], rows: 12, numeric: ['value'], range: [12, 31] }

// ── 3. Route everything ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
const models = Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(inbox).map(([k, src]) => [k, j.ingest.route(src, route)]))

j.compile(models.hook).summary()
// → { imported: 'broken-hook.stl', repair: { shellsDropped: 1, holesFilled: 3, normalsFlipped: 112 },
//     features: 3, watertight: true, genus: 1 }
j.compile(models.sales).metric('height')
// → 43 mm   (base 3 mm + the July bar at 40 · 31/31 mm)
j.compile(models.spec).param('wall')
// → { value: 2 mm, src: 'params', note: 'from spec-text feature "2 mm walls" (confidence 0.88)' }

// ── 4. A low-confidence case: build both, then decide ────────────────────────
const badge = await j.load.image('inbox/badge-high-contrast.png')
const guess = j.ingest.auto(badge)
// → { kind: 'image-silhouette', confidence: 0.55, ranked: [['image-silhouette', 0.55], ['image-photo', 0.41], …] }

if (guess.confidence < 0.7) {
  const [a, b] = guess.ranked.slice(0, 2)
    .map(([kind]) => j.compile(j.print(kind, { parts: [route[kind](badge, guess)] })))
  a.metrics()   // → { printTime: 38 min, filament: 6.1 g, supportVolume: 0 }        the cookie cutter
  b.metrics()   // → { printTime: 2 h 05 min, filament: 21.4 g, supportVolume: 0 }   the lithophane
  // Neither is wrong. The router keeps both as variants (j.diff shows them as two branches) and asks.
}

// ── 5. One batch, packed onto plates ─────────────────────────────────────────
const batch = j.print('inbox-batch', { printer: j.printer('mk4'), material: j.material('PLA') })
  .add('lithophane', models.photo, { orient: '+Y' })        // stand it up: thickness becomes XY resolution
  .add('cutter', models.cat)
  .add('keychain', models.logo, { qty: 4 })
  .add('chart', models.sales)
  .add('hook', models.hook)
  .add('box', models.spec)
  .modifier(j.sel.bodies().of('lithophane'), { infill: { density: 1 }, walls: 6 })   // lithophanes print solid
  .use(j.rules.fdm)

const B = j.compile(batch)
B.plates
// → [{ plate: 1, parts: ['box', 'chart', 'cutter', 'keychain×4'], fill: 0.61 },
//    { plate: 2, parts: ['lithophane', 'hook'], fill: 0.22 }]
B.diagnostics
// → [{ level: 'warning', kind: 'print.textIllegible', at: 'chart.labels', message: 'stroke 0.42 mm < lw(1) = 0.45 mm',
//      fix: 'size: mm(5), or op: "join" for raised letters' }]

const { report } = j.export.tmf(B, { plates: true, colors: true })
report.kept      // → ['plates', 'settings', 'colors (keychain logo: change at z = 3.0 mm)']

32 PCB enclosure: from a board file to a two-part print that fits on the first try

32-pcb-enclosure.js · 122 lines
// 32 · PCB enclosure: from a board file to a two-part print that fits on the first try
//
// Model
//   The board is the input; the enclosure is a function of it. The outline comes from DXF,
//   the mounting holes and connectors from CSV. Every gap is a fit class, not a magic number:
//     port = connector ⊕ free gap,   lid lip = inner wall ⊖ slide gap,   insert hole = heat-set spec.
//   The assembly places the PCB as a reference body (never printed), checks interference, and
//   the print job takes only the two printable parts, with the lid flipped.
//
// Notice
//   - Ports are cut by folding over the connector table: one row, one cut, on a face chosen by selector.
//   - Base and lid share one params object, so hooks and windows cannot drift apart.
//   - The snap hook is checked by its beam law before anything is printed.
//   - The interference check finds a real clash (hook vs capacitor); the fix is one override.
//
// Results in `// →` comments show the illustrative shape of a result.

import { j, mm, deg } from 'jig'

// ── 1. Inputs: outline, holes, connectors ────────────────────────────────────
const board = await j.load.dxf('board/sensor-hub.dxf')
const outline = board.region({ layer: 'Edge.Cuts' })            // 70 × 50 mm, origin at the board centre
const holes = (await j.load.csv('board/holes.csv')).rows        // x, y, d: (±31, ±21), Ø3.2 mm
const connectors = (await j.load.csv('board/connectors.csv')).rows
// → [{ name: 'usb-c',  face: 'front', u: -15, v: 1.6, w: 8.94, h: 3.26, r: 1.63 },
//    { name: 'barrel', face: 'back',  u: 20,  v: 6.5, d: 8.0 }]

const { w: bw, d: bd } = j.inspect.bbox(outline)
const shared = { bw, bd, gap: mm(1), wall: mm(2), h: mm(23), hookX: mm(22) }
const shell = id => j.sketch(id, { on: j.plane.XY })
  .rect('r', 'bw + 2 * (gap + wall)', 'bd + 2 * (gap + wall)', { center: true, r: 3 })   // 76 × 56 mm outside

// ── 2. The base: shell, standoffs with heat-set inserts ──────────────────────
const base = j.part('base')
  .params({ ...shared, standoff: mm(5) })
  .extrude(shell('s').profiles(), 'h', { id: 'body' })
  .shell(j.feat('body').endFace(), 'wall', { id: 'shell' })     // the floor is a wall too: 2 mm
  .add(j.lib.insert('M3x5.7').boss({ wall: mm(2), height: 'standoff' }),
    { at: holes.map(p => j.pt(p.x, p.y, 2)), op: 'join' })
  .cut(j.sketch('win', { on: j.feat('body').sideFace('r.top') })
    .rect('w', 7, 2, { at: ['hookX', 'h - 4'], center: true }).profiles(), mm(4), { id: 'window' })
  .pattern(j.feat('window'), j.pattern.mirror(j.plane.XZ).times(j.pattern.mirror(j.plane.YZ)), { id: 'windows' })   // 4 windows
  .port('rim', j.frame.on(j.feat('body').endFace()))
  .port('standoffs', j.frame({ origin: j.pt(0, 0, 7), x: j.dir('+X'), z: j.dir('+Z') }))   // floor 2 + standoff 5

// ── 3. Ports from the connector table: a fold over rows ──────────────────────
const faceOf = { front: 'r.bottom', back: 'r.top', left: 'r.left', right: 'r.right' }
const free = j.fit.gap('free')                                   // resolved from the fit profile in context
const boardTop = 7 + 1.6

const ported = connectors.reduce((part, c) => {
  const sk = j.sketch(`port-${c.name}`, { on: j.feat('body').sideFace(faceOf[c.face]).expect(1) })   // x along the wall, y up
  const opening = c.d
    ? sk.circle('o', mm(c.d / 2).add(free), { at: [c.u, boardTop + c.v] })
    : sk.rect('o', mm(c.w).add(free.mul(2)), mm(c.h).add(free.mul(2)), { at: [c.u, boardTop + c.v], center: true, r: mm(c.r).add(free) })
  return part.cut(opening.profiles(), mm(4), { id: `port-${c.name}` })
}, base)

// ── 4. The lid: plate, lip, snap hooks, vents, label ─────────────────────────
const hook = j.lib.snap.cantilever({ length: mm(8), thickness: mm(1.2), deflection: mm(0.6), material: 'PETG',
  angle: deg(30), retention: deg(90) })
j.inspect.snap(hook)
// → { strain: 0.0169 (= 1.5 · 1.2 · 0.6 / 8²), allowable: 0.025, permissibleDeflection: 0.89 mm, ratio: 0.68 }

const lid = j.part('lid')
  .params(shared)
  .extrude(shell('p').profiles(), mm(2), { id: 'plate' })
  .extrude(j.sketch('lip', { on: j.feat('plate').startFace() })
    .rect('r', j.fit.pin(j.expr('bw + 2 * gap'), 'slide'), j.fit.pin(j.expr('bd + 2 * gap'), 'slide'), { center: true, r: 1 })
    .profiles(), mm(3), { id: 'lip' })
  .shell(j.feat('lip').endFace(), mm(1.6), { id: 'lipShell' })
  .add(hook, { at: [['hookX', 'bd / 2'], ['-hookX', 'bd / 2'], ['hookX', '-bd / 2'], ['-hookX', '-bd / 2']].map(([x, y]) => j.pt(x, y, 0)) })
  .cut(j.sketch('vent', { on: j.feat('plate').endFace() }).polygon('v', 6, 1.8, { at: [-8, 0] }).profiles(), { through: 'all' }, { id: 'vent' })
  .pattern(j.feat('vent'), j.pattern.hex(j.plane.XY, { pitch: mm(5), count: [9, 4] }), { id: 'vents' })
  .emboss(j.region.text('SENSOR HUB', { size: mm(6), font: 'Inter Bold' }), mm(0.6),
    { on: j.feat('plate').endFace(), op: 'cut', id: 'label' })
  .port('seat', j.frame.on(j.feat('plate').startFace(), { flip: true }))

// ── 5. Assembly with the PCB as a reference body ─────────────────────────────
const pcb = j.part('pcb')
  .extrude(outline, mm(1.6), { id: 'board' })
  .extrude(j.region.circle(mm(4), { at: [22, 21] }), mm(13.6), { id: 'cap' })   // 470 µF electrolytic, 12 mm above the board
  .port('bottom', j.frame.on(j.feat('board').startFace(), { flip: true }))

const asm = (basePart, lidPart) => j.assembly('sensor-hub')
  .add('base', basePart.fit('mk4-petg'))
  .add('pcb', pcb)
  .add('lid', lidPart.fit('mk4-petg'))
  .joint('mount', j.joint.rigid(), 'pcb:bottom', 'base:standoffs')
  .joint('close', j.joint.snap(), 'lid:seat', 'base:rim')
  .interference({ clearance: mm(0.3) })

j.compile(asm(ported, lid)).diagnostics
// → [{ level: 'error', kind: 'asm.interference', at: ['lid/hook#1', 'pcb/cap'], message: 'overlap 18 mm³ near [22, 23.6, 17]',
//      fix: 'move the hooks along x (hookX) or onto the short walls' }]

const fix = { hookX: mm(12) }                                   // one value, both parts
const [baseOk, lidOk] = [ported.override(fix), lid.override(fix)]
const A = j.compile(asm(baseOk, lidOk))
A.metrics()   // → { interferenceVolume: 0, assemblyDOF: 0, parts: 3, uniqueParts: 3 }
A.bom()
// → [{ part: 'base', qty: 1 }, { part: 'lid', qty: 1 }, { part: 'pcb', qty: 1, note: 'reference, not printed' },
//    { part: 'insert M3x5.7', qty: 4 }]

// ── 6. Print the two printable parts ─────────────────────────────────────────
const job = j.print('enclosure', { printer: j.printer('mk4'), material: j.material('PETG') })
  .add('base', baseOk)
  .add('lid', lidOk, { orient: '-Z' })                          // flipped: the label prints on the bed, hooks point up
  .fit('mk4-petg')
  .use(j.rules.fdm)

const P = j.compile(job)
P.summary()
// → { plates: 1, orientation: { base: '+Z', lid: '-Z (given)' }, supports: 0 mm³,
//     bridges: { 'base.port-usb-c': 9.5 mm, 'base.port-barrel': 8.6 mm, 'base.windows': 7.0 mm }, warnings: 0 }
P.param('lid.lip')   // → { value: 71.6 × 51.6 mm, src: 'fit mk4-petg (slide 0.20 mm per side)', expr: 'pin(bw + 2·gap, slide)' }
P.metrics()          // → { printTime: 2 h 31 min, filament: 42.0 g, cost: 0.92 usd, supportVolume: 0 }

const { report } = j.export.tmf(P, { plates: true, settings: true })
report               // → { kept: ['plates', 'settings', 'part names'], approximated: ['mesh, max deviation 0.009 mm'], dropped: [] }
j.export.step(A)     // the whole assembly, PCB included, for the electronics side of the team

33 Grid storage bins: a Gridfinity-compatible family, a baseplate, and a batch on plates

33-grid-storage-bins.js · 103 lines
// 33 · Grid storage bins: a Gridfinity-compatible family, a baseplate, and a batch on plates
//
// Model
//   The grid is a lattice: a cell sits at 42 mm · (i, k), heights come in 7 mm units, and a bin of
//   gx × gy cells is (42·gx − 0.5) × (42·gy − 0.5) mm, leaving 0.25 mm per side.
//   One foot per cell is three stacked extrudes. Two 45° tapers around a straight band form the
//   stepped profile (0.8 / 1.8 / 2.15 mm), so each foot is a stack of frusta (see 06).
//   A bin is a function of (gx, gy, u, options): a model family. The design space over it is finite
//   (4 · 4 · 3 = 48 bins), so it tabulates, and every foot after the first comes from the cache.
//
// Notice
//   - Compatibility beats fit here: the magnet pockets are 6.5 × 2.4 mm because the grid's convention says so.
//   - The label shelf is exactly 45°, so the overhang rule passes at its boundary without supports.
//   - The fdm preset's bed chamfer is skipped, and recorded as a decision, because the foot is already chamfered.
//
// Results in `// →` comments show the illustrative shape of a result.

import { j, mm, deg } from 'jig'

const PITCH = 42, UNIT = 7, FOOT = 4.75                       // mm; FOOT = 0.8 + 1.8 + 2.15

// ── 1. One foot: a stack of three extrudes ───────────────────────────────────
const footAt = (x, y) => b => b
  .extrude(j.sketch(`f${x}_${y}`, { on: j.plane.XY }).rect('r', 35.6, 35.6, { center: true, at: [x, y], r: 0.8 }).profiles(),
    mm(0.8), { taper: deg(45), id: `f${x}_${y}a` })                       // 35.6 → 37.2 mm
  .extrude(j.feat(`f${x}_${y}a`).endFace(), mm(1.8), { id: `f${x}_${y}b` })
  .extrude(j.feat(`f${x}_${y}b`).endFace(), mm(2.15), { taper: deg(45), id: `f${x}_${y}c` })   // 37.2 → 41.5 mm

// ── 2. The bin family ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
const cells = (gx, gy) => Array.from({ length: gx * gy }, (_, n) => [
  PITCH * ((n % gx) - (gx - 1) / 2), PITCH * (Math.floor(n / gx) - (gy - 1) / 2)])

const bin = ({ gx, gy, u, magnets = true, label = true, dividers = 0 }) => {
  const W = PITCH * gx - 0.5, D = PITCH * gy - 0.5, H = UNIT * u
  const rim = j.sketch('rim', { on: j.plane.offset(j.plane.XY, mm(H)) }).rect('r', W, D, { center: true, r: 3.75 })
  return j.part(`bin-${gx}x${gy}x${u}`)
    .with(b => cells(gx, gy).reduce((acc, [x, y]) => footAt(x, y)(acc), b))
    .extrude(j.sketch('body', { on: j.plane.offset(j.plane.XY, mm(FOOT)) }).rect('r', W, D, { center: true, r: 3.75 }).profiles(),
      mm(H - FOOT), { id: 'body', op: 'join' })
    .shell(j.feat('body').endFace(), mm(1.2), { id: 'walls' })
    .sweep(j.sketch('lipProfile', { on: j.plane.normalTo(rim.wire(['r']), { at: 0 }) })
      .polyline('p', [[0, 0], [0.7, 0.7], [0.7, 2.5], [2.6, 4.4], [0, 4.4]], { closed: true }).profiles(),
      rim.wire(['r']), { frame: 'rmf', id: 'lip' })                                     // the stacking lip, 4.4 mm tall
    .with(b => !magnets ? b : b.hole(
      cells(gx, gy).flatMap(([x, y]) => [[13, 13], [-13, 13], [-13, -13], [13, -13]].map(([dx, dy]) => j.pt(x + dx, y + dy, 0))),
      j.hole.simple(mm(6.5), mm(2.4)), { id: 'magnets' }))                               // 6 × 2 mm magnets + glue
    .with(b => !label ? b : b.extrude(j.sketch('tab', { on: j.plane.offset(j.plane.YZ, mm(-W / 2 + 1.2)) })
      .polyline('t', [[D / 2 - 1.2, H], [D / 2 - 13.2, H], [D / 2 - 1.2, H - 12]], { closed: true }).profiles(),
      mm(W - 2.4), { id: 'label' }))                                                    // a 45° shelf along the back wall
    .with(b => dividers === 0 ? b : b
      .extrude(j.sketch('div', { on: j.plane.offset(j.plane.YZ, mm(-W / 2 + W / (dividers + 1))) })
        .rect('d', D - 2.4, H - FOOT - 2, { at: [0, FOOT + (H - FOOT - 2) / 2], center: true }).profiles(), { symmetric: mm(0.6) }, { id: 'div' })
      .pattern(j.feat('div'), j.pattern.linear(j.dir('+X'), { count: dividers, step: mm(W / (dividers + 1)) }), { id: 'dividers' }))
}

const b213 = j.compile(bin({ gx: 2, gy: 1, u: 3, dividers: 1 }))
b213.summary()
// → { bodies: 1, features: 13, bbox: [83.5, 41.5, 25.4] mm (21 + 4.4 lip), sketchDOF: 0 }
b213.decisions.find(d => d.kind === 'bedChamfer')
// → { at: 'bin-2x1x3', kind: 'bedChamfer', chose: 'skip', reason: 'bed edges already chamfered 45° by f*a (0.8 mm ≥ 0.4 mm)' }

// ── 3. The baseplate: the same profile, cut downwards ────────────────────────
const baseplate = (gx, gy) => j.part(`base-${gx}x${gy}`)
  .extrude(j.sketch('p', { on: j.plane.XY }).rect('r', PITCH * gx, PITCH * gy, { center: true, r: 4 }).profiles(), mm(4.65), { id: 'plate' })
  .with(b => cells(gx, gy).reduce((acc, [x, y], n) => acc
    .cut(j.sketch(`c${n}`, { on: j.feat('plate').endFace() }).rect('c', 42, 42, { center: true, at: [x, y], r: 4 }).profiles(),
      mm(2.15), { taper: deg(-45), id: `c${n}a` })
    .cut(j.feat(`c${n}a`).endFace(), mm(1.8), { id: `c${n}b` })
    .cut(j.feat(`c${n}b`).endFace(), mm(0.7), { taper: deg(-45), id: `c${n}c` }), b))

// ── 4. The family as a finite design space: tabulate, and the cache does the work ─
const family = j.design({ gx: j.param.int(1, 4), gy: j.param.int(1, 4), u: j.param.choice([3, 6, 9]) }, p => bin(p))
const table = j.stage(family)
table.summary()
// → { kind: 'tabulated', points: 48, compiled: 48, rebuildMs: 9'400, cacheHitRate: 0.64,
//     note: 'feet are separate new bodies keyed by (x, y) offset: 147 unique of 900 foot features; joins recomputed per bin' }

// ── 5. A batch from a design table, packed onto plates ───────────────────────
const order = (await j.load.csv('bins.csv')).rows
// → [{ name: '1x1x3', gx: 1, gy: 1, u: 3, qty: 4 }, { name: '2x1x6', gx: 2, gy: 1, u: 6, qty: 2, dividers: 1 },
//    { name: '2x2x3', gx: 2, gy: 2, u: 3, qty: 1, label: false }]

const job = order.reduce((p, r) => p.add(r.name, bin(r), { qty: r.qty }),
  j.print('drawer', { printer: j.printer('mk4'), material: j.material('PLA') }).add('base', baseplate(4, 4)))
  .plates({ pack: 'skyline', spacing: mm(5) })
  .slice({ walls: 2, infill: { density: 0.15, pattern: 'gyroid' } })
  .use(j.rules.fdm)

const P = j.compile(job)
P.plates
// → [{ plate: 1, parts: ['base', '1x1x3 ×4'], fill: 0.67 },          168² + 4 · 41.5² = 35'113 mm² of 52'500
//    { plate: 2, parts: ['2x1x6 ×2', '2x2x3'], fill: 0.26 }]          2 · 83.5 · 41.5 + 83.5² = 13'903 mm²
P.plates.lowerBound
// → { footprints: 49'016 mm², bedArea: 52'500 mm², plates: 1 }   by area one plate would do (93 %); by shape it can't,
//   since the 83.5 mm 2×2 bin doesn't fit the 82 mm strip left beside the 168 mm base
P.diagnostics
// → [{ level: 'info', kind: 'print.overhang', at: '*.label', message: 'label shelf at 45.0°: at the limit, no support needed' }]
P.metrics()
// → { printTime: 9 h 12 min, filament: 268 g, cost: 5.90 usd, supportVolume: 0, plates: 2 }

const { report } = j.export.tmf(P, { plates: true })
report.kept            // → ['plates', 'settings', 'part names', 'quantities']

34 Print-in-place mechanism: an articulated snake that comes off the bed already moving

34-print-in-place-mechanism.js · 99 lines
// 34 · Print-in-place mechanism: an articulated snake that comes off the bed already moving
//
// Model
//   A chain of n rigid links and n − 1 revolute joints. Each joint is the subgroup SO(2) of SE(3),
//   so Grübler–Kutzbach gives M = 6(n − 1 − j) + Σfᵢ = n − 1 degrees of freedom.
//   Printing in place means every pair of mating surfaces is separated by the fit class
//   'printInPlace'. That gap is measured along the surface normal, so on a 45° cone an axial
//   offset of g leaves only g · cos 45° = 0.71 g.
//   Each joint is checked by sweeping it through its limits and integrating the swept interference.
//
// Notice
//   - Conical knuckles (45°) let the pins print without support. The rules check that no support lands inside a gap.
//   - The naive axial offset fails the clearance rule; offsetFace offsets along the normal and passes.
//   - A four-hinge coupon calibrates the gap for your printer. The whole snake then recompiles tighter, from cache.
//
// Results in `// →` comments show the illustrative shape of a result.

import { j, mm, deg, turn } from 'jig'

// ── 1. One link: body, fork (behind), tongue (ahead), conical knuckles ───────
// Link pitch 18 mm, height 9 mm in thirds: prongs z 0–3 and 6–9, the next link's tongue z 3–6.
const gap = j.fit.gap('printInPlace')
const link = (name, { naive = false } = {}) => j.part(name)
  .params({ P: mm(18), W: mm(12), H: mm(9) })
  .extrude(j.sketch('body', { on: j.plane.XY }).rect('r', 14, 'W', { center: true, r: 2 }).profiles(), 'H', { id: 'body' })
  .cut(j.sketch('slot', { on: j.plane.XZ }).rect('s', 8, mm(3).add(gap.mul(2)), { at: [-5, 4.5], center: true }).profiles(),
    { through: 'all' }, { id: 'slot' })                                    // the fork: room for the previous tongue
  .extrude(j.sketch('tongue', { on: j.plane.offset(j.plane.XY, mm(3)) }).slot('t', [7, 0], [13, 0], 6).profiles(),
    mm(3), { id: 'tongue', op: 'join' })
  .add(j.cone(mm(1.8), mm(0), mm(1.8)), { at: j.tx.move(13, 0, 6), op: 'join' })                          // knuckle up
  .add(j.cone(mm(1.8), mm(0), mm(1.8)), { at: j.tx.mirror(j.plane.XY).then(j.tx.move(13, 0, 3)), op: 'join' })   // knuckle down
  .revolve(j.sketch('recess', { on: j.plane.XZ })                          // two half-cone sections about the fork axis x = −5
    .polyline('up', [[-5, 6], [-3.2, 6], [-5, 7.8]], { closed: true })
    .polyline('down', [[-5, 3], [-3.2, 3], [-5, 1.2]], { closed: true }).profiles(),
    j.axis.through(j.pt(-5, 0, 0), j.pt(-5, 0, 1)), turn(1), { op: 'cut', id: 'recess' })
  .with(b => naive
    ? b.move(j.feat('recess').faces(), j.tx.move(0, 0, gap))                // axial offset: wrong on a cone
    : b.offsetFace(j.feat('recess').faces(), gap))                          // normal offset: right on any surface
  .chamfer(j.feat('body').sideFaces().edges('|Z').where(e => e.convex), mm(3), { id: 'ends' })
  .port('fork', j.frame({ origin: j.pt(-5, 0, 0), x: j.dir('+X'), z: j.dir('+Z') }))
  .port('tongue', j.frame({ origin: j.pt(13, 0, 0), x: j.dir('+X'), z: j.dir('+Z') }))

// ── 2. The chain: n links, n − 1 revolute joints, printed as one body ───────
const snake = (n, opts) => Array.from({ length: n - 1 }, (_, k) => k + 1).reduce((a, i) => a
  .add(`s${i}`, link('link', opts))
  .joint(`h${i}`, j.joint.revolute({ limits: [deg(-35), deg(35)] }), `s${i - 1}:tongue`, `s${i}:fork`),
  j.assembly('flexi-snake').add('s0', link('head', opts)))                 // s0 is grounded: the first component
  .with(a => a.printInPlace(Array.from({ length: n }, (_, i) => `s${i}`), { clearance: 'printInPlace' }))

const S = j.compile(snake(12))
S.dof()                       // → 11
j.inspect.mobility(snake(12))   // → { grubler: { n: 12, joints: 11, sumF: 11, M: 6·(12 − 1 − 11) + 11 = 11 }, solverDOF: 11 }

// ── 3. Clearance rules: the cone trap ───────────────────────────────────────
j.check(j.compile(snake(12, { naive: true })), j.rules.printInPlace)
// → [{ level: 'error', kind: 'print.thinFeature', at: 's1/recess ↔ s0/knuckle', message: 'normal gap 0.28 mm < printInPlace 0.40 mm',
//      fix: 'offset along the normal (offsetFace) instead of moving the recess by 0.40 mm in z' }]
j.check(S, j.rules.printInPlace)
// → []   (normal gap 0.40 mm everywhere; supports inside gaps: 0 mm³; knuckle overhang 45.0°)

// ── 4. Sweep every hinge through its limits ──────────────────────────────────
S.sweep('h5')
// → { joint: 'h5', range: [-35°, 35°], steps: 36, sweptInterference: 0 mm³, minClearance: 0.4 mm at ±35° (s4 ↔ s5 chamfers) }

const square = j.compile(snake(12).replace('s5', link('link').suppress('ends')))
square.diagnostics
// → [{ level: 'error', kind: 'asm.sweptInterference', at: ['s4', 's5'], message: '6.2 mm³ swept overlap beyond ±28°',
//      fix: "keep the 'ends' chamfer (free to ±38°) or set limits to ±27°" }]

// ── 5. Calibrate the gap on your printer: a four-hinge coupon ────────────────
const coupon = j.fit.coupon({ kind: 'print-in-place', range: [mm(0.2), mm(0.5)], steps: 4 })   // hinges at 0.2/0.3/0.4/0.5 mm
j.compile(j.print('coupon', { printer: j.printer('mk4'), material: j.material('PLA'), parts: [coupon] })).metrics()
// → { printTime: 14 min, filament: 2.1 g }

const results = [                                                         // measured by hand after printing
  { gap: mm(0.2), free: false }, { gap: mm(0.3), free: true, note: 'needs one firm twist' },
  { gap: mm(0.4), free: true }, { gap: mm(0.5), free: true, wobble: 'noticeable' },
]
const cal = j.fit.calibrate(results)
// → { classes: { printInPlace: 0.30 mm, … }, basis: 'smallest freed gap', samples: 4, previous: 0.40 mm }
j.fit.profile('mk4-pla', { printer: j.printer('mk4'), material: j.material('PLA'), classes: cal.classes })

// ── 6. Recompile tighter, then print ─────────────────────────────────────────
const job = j.print('snake', { printer: j.printer('mk4'), material: j.material('PLA') })
  .add('snake', snake(12))
  .fit('mk4-pla')
  .supports(false)
  .use(j.rules.printInPlace)

const P = j.compile(job)
P.why(gap)                    // → { value: 0.30 mm, src: 'fit mk4-pla (calibrated, printInPlace)', previous: 0.40 mm }
P.trace.filter(t => t.cached).length / P.trace.length
// → 0.79   (only the recess offsets and the slot height changed; bodies, tongues and chamfers came from cache)
P.summary()
// → { plates: 1, orientation: { snake: '+Z (as modelled; knuckle axes vertical)' }, supports: 0 mm³,
//     bedChamfer: '0.4 mm on 46 bed edges, including the 22 inside hinge gaps', warnings: 0 }
P.metrics()                   // → { printTime: 1 h 38 min, filament: 14.2 g, cost: 0.31 usd, sweptInterference: 0 }
j.export.tmf(P).report.kept   // → ['plates', 'settings', 'part names']

35 Functional bracket: orient for the load, size by a beam formula, search thickness against mass

35-functional-bracket.js · 97 lines
// 35 · Functional bracket: orient for the load, size by a beam formula, search thickness against mass
//
// Model
//   A cantilever shelf bracket under a point load F at x = 120 mm from the wall. Bending moment
//   M(x) = F · (120 − x). The stress at a section is σ = M / Z, with section modulus Z = I / c
//   (b·t²/6 for a b × t rectangle). The gusset stiffens the arm until it ends, so the critical
//   section is where the gusset stops, not at the wall.
//   Printed parts are anisotropic: strong within a layer, weaker across layers. The orientation
//   should keep the bending stress inside the layers. layerStrengthRisk measures how much of the
//   load path crosses layers.
//   FEA (`sim`) is an extension; the beam formula is the honest proxy until then.
//
// Notice
//   - preset.functional takes the load, puts "load not across layers" first in the orientation order, and uses 4 walls.
//   - The screw holes turn into teardrops once the part lies on its side: an orientation ↔ geometry fixpoint.
//   - The search finds that a shorter gusset with a thicker arm is lighter. That is not obvious, and it is worth a table.
//
// Results in `// →` comments show the illustrative shape of a result.

import { j, mm } from 'jig'

// ── 1. The bracket ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
const petg = j.material('PETG').with({ strength: { inPlane: j.q('45 MPa'), acrossLayers: j.q('25 MPa') } })

const bracket = j.part('bracket')
  .params({ t: mm(7.5), g: mm(90), b: mm(20) })
  .material(petg)
  .extrude(j.sketch('L', { on: j.plane.XZ })                               // leg 8 mm × 100 mm, arm 150 mm × t
    .polyline('p', [[0, 0], [8, 0], [8, '100 - t'], [150, '100 - t'], [150, 100], [0, 100]], { closed: true }).profiles(),
    { symmetric: 'b' }, { id: 'L' })
  .fillet(j.sel.edges('|Y').of(j.feat('L')).where(e => e.concave).expect(1), mm(6), { id: 'corner' })
  .rib(j.sketch('gusset', { on: j.plane.XZ })
    .line('g', [8, '100 - t - 0.75 * g'], ['8 + g', '100 - t']).wire(['g']), mm(6), { id: 'gusset' })
  .hole([j.pt(8, 0, 30), j.pt(8, 0, 70)], j.hole.counterbore(mm(4.5), mm(8.5), mm(3), mm(8)), { id: 'screws' })   // heads on the arm side
  .chamfer(j.feat('L').sideFaces().edges('|Y').where(e => e.convex), mm(1), { id: 'ease' })

const loaded = bracket.use(j.preset.functional({
  load: { at: j.sel.faces('+Z').of(j.feat('L')).near([128, 0, 100]), dir: '-Z', force: j.q('100 N') } }))   // ~10 kg of shelf per bracket

// ── 2. The strength proxy: σ = M / Z where the gusset ends ──────────────────
const sigmaArm = j.metric('sigmaArm', prog => {
  const g = prog.param('g').value
  const sec = j.inspect.section(prog, j.plane.offset(j.plane.YZ, mm(8).add(g)))
  const M = j.q('100 N').mul(mm(120).sub(g))
  return M.div(sec.Z.top).to('MPa')
}, { dir: 'min', unit: 'MPa', about: 'bending stress in the arm at the gusset tip (beam theory)' })

const B = j.compile(loaded)
j.inspect.section(B, j.plane.offset(j.plane.YZ, mm(98)))
// → { area: 150 mm², centroid: [98, 0, 96.25], I: 703 mm⁴ (= 20 · 7.5³ / 12), Z: { top: 187.5 mm³, bottom: 187.5 mm³ } }
j.evaluate(j.objective.minimize(sigmaArm), B)
// → { sigmaArm: 16.0 MPa }   M = 100 N · 30 mm = 3000 N·mm;  3000 / 187.5 = 16.0 MPa;  in-plane safety factor 45 / 16 = 2.8

// ── 3. Orientation for strength, not just for supports ──────────────────────
const job = j.print('bracket', { printer: j.printer('mk4'), material: petg }).add('bracket', loaded)
const P = j.compile(job)
P.decisions.filter(d => d.kind === 'orient' || d.kind === 'hole')
// → [{ at: 'bracket', kind: 'orient', chose: '+Y (on its side)', alternatives: ['+Z', '-X'],
//      reason: 'functional: layerStrengthRisk 0.03 vs 0.48 (+Z) vs 0.71 (-X, leg on bed); support 0 mm³' },
//    { at: 'screws', kind: 'hole', chose: 'teardrop 45°', reason: 'axis X ⟂ build direction Y' }]
P.trace.find(t => t.pass === 'fixpoint')
// → { pass: 'fixpoint', level: 'L5', note: 'orientation ↔ teardrops converged in 2' }

const upright = j.compile(job.orient('-X'))                              // leg flat on the bed: neat, and weak
upright.metrics().layerStrengthRisk                                      // → 0.71
// The arm's 16.0 MPa now pulls layers apart: 25 / 16 gives a safety factor of 1.6 instead of 2.8. Same geometry, weaker part.

P.summary()
// → { orientation: '+Y', walls: 4 (functional), infill: 25 % gyroid, supports: 0 mm³, warnings: 0 }
P.metrics()
// → { printTime: 2 h 06 min, mass: 43.2 g, filament: 14.1 m, layerStrengthRisk: 0.03, sigmaArm: 16.0 MPa }

// ── 4. Search: arm thickness against gusset length ──────────────────────────
const space = j.design({
  t: j.param.range(mm(5), mm(9), { step: mm(0.5), default: mm(7.5) }),
  g: j.param.choice([mm(60), mm(75), mm(90)], { default: mm(90) }),
}, p => j.print('bracket', { printer: j.printer('mk4'), material: petg }).add('bracket', loaded.params(p)),
{ objective: j.objective.lexicographic([
  j.objective.require(prog => prog.metric('sigmaArm').lte(j.q('18 MPa'))),   // in-plane strength / 2.5
  j.objective.require(prog => prog.metric('layerStrengthRisk') <= 0.1),
  j.objective.minimize('mass'),
]) })

const r = await j.search.grid(space)
r.table()
// → rank  t       g      sigmaArm   mass     printTime   feasible
//   1     9.0 mm  75 mm  16.7 MPa   42.1 g   2 h 02 min  ✓      4500 N·mm / (20 · 9² / 6)
//   2     7.5 mm  90 mm  16.0 MPa   43.2 g   2 h 06 min  ✓      3000 N·mm / 187.5 mm³
//   3     8.0 mm  90 mm  14.1 MPa   44.3 g   2 h 08 min  ✓
//   …     9.0 mm  60 mm  22.2 MPa   40.4 g   1 h 55 min  ✗ sigmaArm
r.best.point                    // → { t: 9 mm, g: 75 mm }
r.summary
// → { points: 27, compiled: 27, cacheHitRate: 0.58, note: 'L and leg features shared across g; gusset shared across t' }

const { report } = j.export.tmf(j.compile(space.at(r.best.point)))
report.kept                     // → ['plates', 'settings', 'part names', 'orientation +Y']

36 Organic lattice: a TPU wrist rest built from distance fields

36-organic-lattice.js · 96 lines
// 36 · Organic lattice: a TPU wrist rest built from distance fields
//
// Model
//   A field gives every point its signed distance to the surface (negative inside).
//   union = min, intersect = max, subtract = max(f, −g), so field booleans never fail. A true distance
//   field never changes faster than distance itself, and that bound lets the mesher step safely.
//   smoothUnion(k) blends within a band of width k.
//   The rest is a smooth outer body, a 1.2 mm skin, and a gyroid lattice inside that is graded
//   along x: firmer at the ends, softer under the wrist. A noise blend textures the top.
//   Meshing (dual contouring, voxel = lw(0.5)) is a lowering, and its report says what was lost.
//
// Notice
//   - Softness is designed in geometry (graded cell size and wall thickness), not set as slicer infill.
//   - The lattice walls never go below lw(2), so the minimum-wall rule holds without exceptions.
//   - The noise blend breaks the distance bound. Meshing reports it (field.notDistance) and shortens its step.
//   - Changing the noise seed re-meshes only the bricks the blend touches.
//
// Results in `// →` comments show the illustrative shape of a result.

import { j, mm, lw } from 'jig'

// ── 1. The body: a capsule spine smoothly blended into a rounded slab ────────
const spine = j.field.capsule(j.pt(-95, 8, 9), j.pt(95, 8, 9), mm(11))           // top of the spine at z = 20, toward the back
const slab = j.field.box(240, 75, 12, { r: mm(6) }).map(j.tx.move(0, 0, 6))
const body = spine.smoothUnion(slab, mm(8))
  .intersect(j.field.box(240, 75, 20, { r: mm(4) }).map(j.tx.move(0, 0, 10)))    // envelope 240 × 75 × 20 mm, flat bottom

// Field booleans can't fail, and polynomial smooth-min keeps the distance bound, so the body meshes safely.

// ── 2. Skin, texture, lattice ────────────────────────────────────────────────
const skin = body.shell(mm(1.2))
  .blend(j.field.noise(mm(6), { seed: 7 }), (p, ctx) => p.z.gt(mm(14)) ? 0.06 : 0)   // ±0.4 mm texture on the top only

const along = p => Math.abs(p.x.div(mm(120)).value)                               // 0 at the centre, 1 at the ends
const lattice = j.field.gyroid(mm(12), { thickness: lw(2) })
  .grade('cell', (p, ctx) => mm(16).sub(mm(6).mul(along(p))))                     // 16 mm cells in the middle → 10 mm at the ends
  .grade('thickness', (p, ctx) => lw(2).add(lw(1).mul(along(p))))                 // 0.9 mm → 1.35 mm toward the ends

const pockets = [[-100, -25], [100, -25], [-100, 25], [100, 25]]
  .map(([x, y]) => j.field.cyl(mm(4), mm(1.5)).map(j.tx.move(x, y, 0)))          // Ø8 × 1.5 mm for silicone bumpers
  .reduce((a, f) => a.union(f))

const rest = skin.union(lattice.intersect(body.offset(mm(-1.2)))).subtract(pockets)

skin.mesh({ voxel: lw(0.5) }).report.warnings
// → [{ kind: 'field.notDistance', maxSlope: 1.07, note: 'the noise blend breaks the distance bound; meshing steps shrink by 1/1.07' }]

// ── 3. Meshing: a lowering with a report ─────────────────────────────────────
const meshed = rest.mesh({ voxel: lw(0.5), method: 'dual-contouring' })
const M = j.compile(meshed)
M.summary()
// → { voxel: 0.225 mm, bricks: 1'122 (34 × 11 × 3), triangles: 8.4 M, watertight: true, genus: 1'806,
//     maxDeviation: 0.11 mm (half a voxel), stepScale: 0.93 }
M.diagnostics
// → [{ level: 'info', kind: 'field.featureBelowVoxel', at: 'skin.blend', message: 'noise detail below 0.225 mm smoothed (3 % of texture energy)' }]

const reseeded = j.compile(skin.blend(j.field.noise(mm(6), { seed: 8 }), (p, ctx) => p.z.gt(mm(14)) ? 0.06 : 0)
  .union(lattice.intersect(body.offset(mm(-1.2)))).subtract(pockets).mesh({ voxel: lw(0.5) }))
reseeded.metrics().cacheHitRate
// → 0.67   (374 of 1'122 bricks re-meshed: only the top layer, where the blend weight is non-zero)

// ── 4. A part, a print job, the rules ────────────────────────────────────────
const wristRest = j.part('wrist-rest')
  .material(j.material('TPU-95A'))
  .import(j.mesh(meshed).decimate({ faces: 1_200_000, keep: 'features' }))

j.inspect.hausdorff(meshed, j.mesh(meshed).decimate({ faces: 1_200_000, keep: 'features' }))
// → { max: 0.04 mm, mean: 0.006 mm }   (well under one layer)

const job = j.print('wrist-rest', { printer: j.printer('mk4'), material: j.material('TPU-95A') })
  .add('rest', wristRest)
  .supports(false)                                             // flat bottom; the gyroid is self-supporting
  .slice({ layer: mm(0.2), walls: 2, top: 4, bottom: 3, infill: { density: 0 } })   // the lattice is the infill
  .seam('rear')
  .use(j.rules.fdm)

const P = j.compile(job)
P.diagnostics
// → []   (minWall: lattice walls ≥ 0.90 mm = lw(2); bedFit: 240 × 75 mm on 250 × 210 mm; pocket bridges 8 mm ≤ 10 mm)
P.summary()
// → { orientation: '+Z (flat bottom: bed contact 14'600 mm²)', supports: 0 mm³, layers: 100, plates: 1 }
P.metrics()
// → { printTime: 11 h 40 min, mass: 118 g, filament: 40.5 m, cost: 4.13 usd, supportVolume: 0, cuspMax: 0.2 mm }
//   filament = 97.5 cm³ / (π · 0.875² mm²) = 40.5 m;  mass = 97.5 cm³ · 1.21 g/cm³ = 118 g

// ── 5. Compared with the obvious alternative ─────────────────────────────────
const plainPart = j.part('plain').material(j.material('TPU-95A')).import(j.mesh(body.mesh({ voxel: lw(0.5) })))
const plain = j.compile(j.print('plain', { printer: j.printer('mk4'), material: j.material('TPU-95A') })
  .add('plain', plainPart)
  .slice({ walls: 3, infill: { density: 0.15, pattern: 'gyroid' } }))
plain.metrics()
// → { printTime: 9 h 10 min, mass: 92 g }   lighter and faster, but uniformly firm: the slicer's infill knows nothing about wrists

j.export.tmf(P).report
// → { kept: ['plates', 'settings', 'part names'], approximated: ['field → mesh (0.11 mm)', 'decimation (0.04 mm)'], dropped: [] }

E Design process

40 Design spaces and configurations: from S/M/L to a product space

40-design-spaces-configurations.js · 111 lines
// 40 · Design spaces and configurations: from S/M/L to a product space
//
// Model
//   A configuration set is a finite space: a few named rows of overrides. jig tabulates it at compile time.
//   A design table is the same thing loaded from data. A design is a product space P = P₁ × … × Pₙ of
//   typed parameters, together with a function P → Model. Ranges carry units and a grid (step), choices
//   are finite sets, int is a range on ℤ, and dir is a direction on the sphere S². A point snaps to the grid;
//   missing coordinates fall back to each parameter's default, or to its middle value.
//   Where a metric is affine in a parameter, j.stage returns the closed form instead of recompiling.
//
// Notice
//   - Configurations, design tables and design spaces are one idea at three sizes: 3 rows, 4 rows, 25'245 points.
//   - Lengths stay Quantities inside ranges, so lw(3) still means "three line widths" at every point.
//   - .expose is the customizer surface you share. It projects the design space and does not define a second one.
//   - Every point is a plain model value: hash it, diff it, print it.
//
// Results in `// →` comments show the illustrative shape of a result.

import { j, mm, lw } from 'jig'

// ── Fixture: the open box, parametrised ───────────────────────────────────────
const base = j.sketch('base', { on: j.plane.XY }).rect('r', 'w', 'd', { center: true })
const box = j.part('box')
  .params({ w: mm(60), d: mm(40), h: mm(30), wall: mm(2) })
  .material(j.material('PLA'))
  .extrude(base.profiles(), 'h', { id: 'body' })
  .shell(j.feat('body').endFace(), 'wall', { id: 'shell' })

// ── 1. Configurations: a finite space, tabulated at compile time ─────────────
const sized = box.configs({
  S: { w: mm(40), d: mm(30), h: mm(20) },
  M: {},                                            // the params themselves
  L: { w: mm(90), d: mm(60), h: mm(45) },
})
const T = j.stage(sized)
T.tabulated                                         // → { config: ['S', 'M', 'L'], compiled: 3, ms: 38 }
T.at({ config: 'L' }).metric('mass')                // → 44.5 g   (a lookup, not a compile)
// shell volume = w·d·h − (w − 2t)(d − 2t)(h − t):
//   S  24'000 − 16'848 =  7'152 mm³ →  8.9 g
//   M  72'000 − 56'448 = 15'552 mm³ → 19.3 g
//   L 243'000 − 207'088 = 35'912 mm³ → 44.5 g      (PLA, 1.24 g/cm³, solid)

j.compile(sized.config('S')).param('h')
// → { value: 20 mm, expr: null, src: 'configs[S]', deps: [] }   (it beat params.h = 30 mm)

// ── 2. A design table is a configuration set read from data ──────────────────
const drawer = `name,w,d,h
pens,180 mm,30 mm,25 mm
cards,95 mm,60 mm,40 mm
bits,60 mm,40 mm,20 mm
cables,120 mm,80 mm,50 mm`
const family = box.configs(j.table(drawer, { key: 'name' }))
j.compile(family.config('cards')).param('w')
// → { value: 95 mm, src: 'configs[cards] (table row 2)', deps: [] }
// Units are parsed from the cells; a bare number in a Length column would be read as mm and flagged units.mixed.

// ── 3. A design: a product space of typed parameters ─────────────────────────
const trayModel = p => {
  let b = box.params({ w: p.w, d: p.d, h: p.h, wall: p.wall })
  if (p.cols > 1) b = b
    .extrude(j.sketch('div', { on: j.plane.XY }).rect('r', 'wall', 'd', { center: true }).profiles(), 'h - 1 mm', { id: 'divider' })
    .pattern(j.feat('divider'), j.pattern.linear(j.dir('+X'), { count: p.cols - 1, step: p.w.div(p.cols) }), { id: 'dividers' })
  return b
}
const tray = j.design({
  w:    j.param.range(mm(40), mm(120), { step: mm(5) }),                 // 17 values, no default → middle
  d:    j.param.range(mm(30), mm(80), { step: mm(5), default: mm(40) }), // 11 values
  h:    j.param.range(mm(20), mm(60), { step: mm(5), default: mm(30) }), //  9 values
  wall: j.param.choice([lw(2), lw(3), lw(4)]),                           //  3 values, no default → lw(3)
  cols: j.param.int(1, 5, { default: 1 }),                               //  5 values
}, trayModel)

tray.defaults()                     // → { w: 80 mm, d: 40 mm, h: 30 mm, wall: 3lw, cols: 1 }
tray.size                           // → 25'245 points   = 17 · 11 · 9 · 3 · 5

// Points snap to the grid, and provenance says so.
j.compile(tray.at({ w: mm(62) })).param('w')
// → { value: 60 mm, src: 'design point (snapped from 62 mm to the 5 mm grid)', deps: [] }
j.compile(tray.at({ cols: 3 })).features().map(f => f.id)
