// → ['body', 'shell', 'divider', 'dividers']

// ── 4. Sub-spaces are values too: fix, where, sample ─────────────────────────
const shallow = tray.fix({ h: mm(20) })                                  // 2'805 points
const fitsDrawer = tray.where(p => p.w.lte(mm(100)) && p.d.lte(mm(60))) // 12'285 points  = 13 · 7 · 9 · 3 · 5
fitsDrawer.sample(3, { seed: 4 })
// → [{ w: 55 mm, d: 45 mm, h: 35 mm, wall: 2lw, cols: 4 }, { w: 95 mm, d: 30 mm, … }, { w: 70 mm, d: 60 mm, … }]

// Orientation is a design parameter as well: dir samples the sphere.
const printSpace = j.design({
  up:    j.param.dir({ samples: 26, default: '+Z' }),
  layer: j.param.choice([mm(0.12), mm(0.2), mm(0.28)], { default: mm(0.2) }),
}, p => j.print('tray', { parts: [tray.at({ cols: 2 })] }).orient(p.up).slice({ layer: p.layer }))
printSpace.size                     // → 78 points  = 26 directions · 3 layer heights

// ── 5. The customizer surface: expose a projection of the space ─────────────
const shareable = trayModel(tray.defaults()).expose(['w', 'd', 'h', 'cols'], {
  labels: { w: 'Width', d: 'Depth', h: 'Height', cols: 'Compartments' },
  ranges: { w: [mm(40), mm(120)], d: [mm(30), mm(80)], h: [mm(20), mm(60)], cols: [1, 5] },
})
j.compile(shareable).summary().customizer
// → [{ name: 'w', label: 'Width', kind: 'Length', range: [40 mm, 120 mm], value: 80 mm }, …]   (wall stays fixed at 3lw)

// ── 6. Staging: affine metrics become closed forms ───────────────────────────
// With w, d and the wall fixed, shell volume is affine in h:
//   V(h) = h·[w·d − (w − 2t)(d − 2t)] + t·(w − 2t)(d − 2t)
const tall = j.stage(tray.fix({ w: mm(60), d: mm(40), wall: lw(3), cols: 1 }))
tall.residual.mass                  // → h ↦ 0.326 g/mm · h + 3.58 g   (t = 1.35 mm; slope 262.7 mm², intercept 2'885 mm³)
tall.residual.mass(mm(45))          // → 18.2 g
tall.at({ h: mm(45) }).metric('overhangArea')   // → 0 mm²   (not affine: solved at run time, then cached)
tall.note                           // → 'mass, volume: affine in h (exact); others: residual program'

41 Objectives and metrics: where rankings disagree is where the trade-off lives

41-objectives-metrics.js · 92 lines
// 41 · Objectives and metrics: where rankings disagree is where the trade-off lives
//
// Model
//   A metric is a function Program → Quantity with a direction (min | max) and a unit, kept in a registry.
//   An objective induces an order on candidates:
//     weighted       Σ wᵢ·mᵢ, where the weights carry units so that the sum has a single dimension
//     lexicographic  compare m₁ first, use m₂ only to break ties, and so on
//     pareto         a dominates b when it is no worse on every metric and better on at least one
//     require        feasibility comes first; infeasible candidates rank below all feasible ones
//
// Notice
//   - The weights are Quantities. "1 minute per gram" makes filament commensurable with time; a bare number would be a DimensionError.
//   - Weighted and lexicographic orders disagree on the phone stand below. The break-even weight is the price of a support.
//   - A Pareto front shows the trade-off without choosing a price at all.
//   - require(rules) removes the candidate that a weighted sum would have chosen.
//
// Results in `// →` comments show the illustrative shape of a result.

import { j, mm } from 'jig'

// ── Fixture: a phone stand, printed in one of four orientations ──────────────
const stand = j.part('phone-stand')
  .extrude(j.sketch('side', { on: j.plane.YZ })
    .polyline('p', [[0, 0], [90, 0], [90, 6], [22, 6], [14, 72], [8, 72], [12, 6], [0, 6]], { closed: true })
    .profiles(), { symmetric: mm(70) }, { id: 'body' })
  .fillet(j.sel.edges('|X').of('body').where(e => e.concave), mm(3), { id: 'root' })

const job = j.print('stand', { parts: [stand] })

// ── 1. The registry: every metric has a level, a direction and a unit ────────
const P = j.compile(job.orient('+Z'))           // upright, as modelled
P.metrics()
// → { volume: 34.0 cm³ (solid), mass: 31.5 g (as printed, with supports), filament: 10.6 m, cost: 0.69 usd,
//     printTime: 74 min, supportVolume: 3.8 cm³, overhangArea: 1'260 mm², bedContact: 540 mm²,
//     height: 72 mm, cuspMax: 0.2 mm, plates: 1, rebuildMs: 41, cacheHitRate: 0.0 }
// filament: 31.5 g ÷ 1.24 g/cm³ = 25.4 cm³, ÷ 2.405 mm² (1.75 mm filament) = 10.6 m

// ── 2. A custom metric: hand time to clean up supports ───────────────────────
const cleanup = j.metric('cleanup',
  prog => prog.metric('supportVolume').mul(j.q('0.01 minute/mm^3')),
  { dir: 'min', unit: 'minute', about: 'hand time to remove supports (shop estimate: 6 min per 0.6 cm³)' })
P.metric('cleanup')                 // → 38 min

// ── 3. Four candidate orientations, measured ─────────────────────────────────
const orients = j.design({ up: j.param.choice(['+Y', '-X', '+Z', '+X']) }, p => job.orient(p.up))
//          up   supportVolume  printTime  mass     cleanup   firstLayer
//   A     +Y        0 mm³        96 min   29.0 g    0 min    6'300 mm²   on its back
//   B     -X      600 mm³        61 min   26.2 g    6 min    2'100 mm²   on its side
//   C     +Z    3'800 mm³        74 min   31.5 g   38 min      540 mm²   upright, as modelled
//   D     +X      200 mm³        52 min   25.9 g    2 min       38 mm²   on a thin edge

// ── 4. Weighted: everything priced in minutes ────────────────────────────────
const weighted = j.objective.weighted({
  time:    ['printTime', 1],
  hands:   ['cleanup', 1],
  plastic: ['mass', j.q('1 minute/g')],          // a gram of filament is worth a minute of waiting
})
// A: 96 + 0 + 29.0 = 125.0   B: 61 + 6 + 26.2 = 93.2   C: 74 + 38 + 31.5 = 143.5   D: 52 + 2 + 25.9 = 79.9

// ── 5. Lexicographic: no support is worth any amount of time ─────────────────
const lexicographic = j.objective.lexicographic(['supportVolume', 'printTime', 'mass'])

const rw = await j.search.grid(orients, { objective: weighted })
const rl = await j.search.grid(orients, { objective: lexicographic })
rw.ranked.map(c => c.point.up)      // → ['+X', '-X', '+Y', '+Z']   D, B, A, C
rl.ranked.map(c => c.point.up)      // → ['+Y', '+X', '-X', '+Z']   A, D, B, C

// Both put C last. Leaving D aside (section 7 removes it), they disagree about A and B, and that
// disagreement is the trade-off: B saves 35 minutes and 2.8 g
// but needs 600 mm³ of support. Weighted prices support removal at 0.01 min/mm³ and picks B.
// The orders agree only once a cubic centimetre of support costs more than
//   (125.0 − 87.2) min / 600 mm³ = 0.063 min/mm³ ≈ 63 minutes per cm³.

// ── 6. Pareto: show the trade-off without pricing it ─────────────────────────
const front = await j.search.grid(orients, { objective: j.objective.pareto(['printTime', 'supportVolume']) })
front.front.map(c => c.point.up)    // → ['+X', '+Y']   D (52 min, 200 mm³) and A (96 min, 0); B and C are dominated by D

// ── 7. require(rules): feasibility before preference ─────────────────────────
// D stands on a 38 mm² edge, which j.rule.firstLayer rejects (minimum 100 mm²).
const feasibleWeighted = j.objective.lexicographic([j.objective.require(j.rules.fdm), weighted])
const rf = await j.search.grid(orients, { objective: feasibleWeighted })
rf.table()
// → rank  up   feasible  score     notes
//   1     -X   yes        93.2     B
//   2     +Y   yes       125.0     A
//   3     +Z   yes       143.5     C
//   4     +X   no         79.9     D: print.firstLayer (38 mm² < 100 mm²)
j.evaluate(feasibleWeighted, j.compile(orients.at({ up: '+X' })))
// → { feasible: false, score: 79.9, parts: { time: 52, hands: 2, plastic: 25.9 }, violations: ['print.firstLayer'] }

// The front changes too: without D, A and B form the Pareto front.

42 Search: a wall hook, trading a strength proxy against print time

42-search.js · 98 lines
// 42 · Search: a wall hook, trading a strength proxy against print time
//
// Model
//   The hook's design space is t (arm thickness) × walls × infill × orientation: 13 · 5 · 11 · 3 = 2'145 points.
//   There is no FEA in the print suite, so strength is a proxy. The custom metric `capacity` is the
//   bending capacity of the arm's root:
//     F = σ · Z_eff / L,   Z_eff = (b·t²/6) · [1 − (1 − ρ)(1 − 2w/t)³]
//   where w is the shell (walls × line width), ρ is the infill density, and σ blends the along-layer
//   strength (50 MPa) with the across-layer strength (25 MPa, PLA) by the metric layerStrengthRisk.
//   Search: Latin hypercube to explore, descent to refine, NSGA-II to map the Pareto front.
//
// Notice
//   - Candidates that differ only in walls, infill or orientation reuse every L4 feature, so the cache makes search cheap.
//   - Descent moves one coordinate at a time, which is the access pattern the per-feature cache likes best.
//   - The front says what the single "best" hides: every Newton above ~100 N costs about 7 s of print time.
//   - Seeds make every run reproducible (the suite's compile.deterministic covers search too).
//
// Results in `// →` comments show the illustrative shape of a result.

import { j, mm } from 'jig'

// ── Fixture: a J-shaped wall hook ─────────────────────────────────────────────
const profile = j.sketch('profile', { on: j.plane.XZ })
  .rect('back', 't', 'plate', { at: [0, 0] })                 // the plate against the wall
  .rect('arm', 'arm', 't', { at: [0, 0] })                    // the arm, out from the wall
  .rect('tip', 't', mm(12), { at: ['arm - t', 0] })           // the upturned tip
const hook = j.part('hook')
  .params({ b: mm(20), t: mm(6), arm: mm(40), plate: mm(50) })
  .extrude(profile.profiles(), 'b', { id: 'body' })
  .fillet(j.sel.edges('|Y').of('body').where(e => e.concave), mm(4), { id: 'root' })

// ── 1. A strength proxy, as a registered metric ──────────────────────────────
const capacity = j.metric('capacity', prog => {
  const b = prog.param('b').value, t = prog.param('t').value, arm = prog.param('arm').value
  const w = mm(0.45).mul(prog.param('walls').value)                     // shell = walls × line width (0.4 mm nozzle)
  const rho = prog.param('infill').value
  const core = Math.max(0, 1 - w.mul(2).div(t).value) ** 3              // the infilled core's share of I
  const Zeff = b.mul(t).mul(t).div(6).mul(1 - (1 - rho) * core)
  const r = prog.metric('layerStrengthRisk').value                      // 0: load within layers · 1: across them
  const sigma = j.q('50 MPa').mul(1 - r).add(j.q('25 MPa').mul(r))
  return sigma.mul(Zeff).div(arm).to('N')
}, { dir: 'max', unit: 'N', about: 'bending capacity at the arm root (beam proxy; replace with sim when available)' })

// ── 2. The design space ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
const hookSpace = j.design({
  t:      j.param.range(mm(4), mm(10), { step: mm(0.5), default: mm(6) }),   // 13 values
  walls:  j.param.int(2, 6, { default: 3 }),                                // 5
  infill: j.param.range(0.1, 0.6, { step: 0.05, default: 0.15 }),           // 11
  up:     j.param.choice(['+Y', '+Z', '-X'], { default: '+Y' }),            // 3: flat, upright, on its back
}, p => j.print('hook', { parts: [hook.params({ t: p.t })] })
  .params({ walls: p.walls, infill: p.infill })
  .orient(p.up)
  .slice({ walls: 'walls', infill: { density: 'infill', pattern: 'gyroid' } }))

j.compile(hookSpace.at({})).metric('capacity')   // → 128.8 N  (t 6, 3 walls, 15 %, flat: Z_eff = 103.0 mm³)

// The objective: be strong enough first, then fast.
const strongEnough = j.objective.require(prog => prog.metric('capacity').gte(j.q('100 N')))
const objective = j.objective.lexicographic([strongEnough, j.objective.minimize('printTime')])

// ── 3. Explore: Latin hypercube ──────────────────────────────────────────────
const r1 = await j.search.lhs(hookSpace, { budget: 24, seed: 3, objective })
r1.table()
// → rank  t       walls  infill  up   capacity  printTime  feasible  cacheHit
//   1     6.5 mm  3      0.25    +Y   150 N     36 min     yes       0.62
//   2     7.5 mm  2      0.40    +Y   173 N     39 min     yes       0.58
//   …
//   24    4.5 mm  5      0.10    +Z    59 N     31 min     no        0.71
r1.stats                          // → { compiles: 24, features: { computed: 31, cached: 65 }, cacheHitRate: 0.68, ms: 2'140 }

// ── 4. Refine: coordinate descent from the best LHS point ────────────────────
const r2 = await j.search.descent(hookSpace, { from: r1.best.point, steps: 20, objective })
r2.best.point                     // → { t: 5 mm, walls: 4, infill: 0.15, up: '+Y' }
r2.best.metrics                   // → { capacity: 102 N, printTime: 31 min }
// path: (6.5, 3, .25) → (6, 3, .2) → (5.5, 3, .15) 112 N → (5, 4, .15) 102 N; (5, 3, .15) is 95 N and infeasible
r2.stats.cacheHitRate             // → 0.86   (3 of 4 moves leave the geometry untouched)

// The two near-optimal answers differ in kind: a thinner arm with one more wall beats a thicker arm.
// t 5.0 mm, 4 walls: Z_eff = 81.8 mm³ → 102 N     t 5.5 mm, 3 walls: Z_eff = 89.5 mm³ → 112 N, but 2 min slower

// ── 5. Map the trade-off: NSGA-II on (capacity ↑, printTime ↓) ───────────────
const r3 = await j.search.nsga2(hookSpace, {
  pop: 24, gens: 12, seed: 7,
  objective: j.objective.pareto(['capacity', 'printTime']),   // directions come from the registry
})
r3.front.map(c => [c.metrics.capacity, c.metrics.printTime, c.point])
// → [[ 80 N, 26 min, { t: 4.5 mm,  walls: 3, infill: 0.15, up: '+Y' }],
//    [102 N, 31 min, { t: 5 mm,    walls: 4, infill: 0.15, up: '+Y' }],
//    [150 N, 36 min, { t: 6.5 mm,  walls: 3, infill: 0.25, up: '+Y' }],
//    [212 N, 45 min, { t: 8 mm,    walls: 3, infill: 0.3,  up: '+Y' }],
//    [340 N, 58 min, { t: 10 mm,   walls: 4, infill: 0.3,  up: '+Y' }]]
// Every front point prints flat: upright prints load the root across layers and are dominated.
// The slope above 100 N: (340 − 102) N over (58 − 31) min ≈ 8.8 N per minute.

// ── 6. Reproducibility ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
const again = await j.search.nsga2(hookSpace, { pop: 24, gens: 12, seed: 7, objective: j.objective.pareto(['capacity', 'printTime']) })
j.hash(again.front) === j.hash(r3.front)   // → true

43 The law suite: declared structures, justified laws, one runner

43-laws-property-tests-fuzzing.js · 142 lines
// 43 · The law suite: declared structures, justified laws, one runner
//
// Model
//   There is one way to state a law and one runner.
//     j.structure(Sort, kind, ops)  derives the structural laws of a kind (group, Boolean algebra, lattice, …)
//     j.law(name, gen, prop, { tier, justifies, source })  states an invariant or an oracle by hand
//     j.laws.check(laws, { n, seed })  runs each law on n generated values and shrinks any failure
//   Every law must say what it pays for: a rewrite, a cache rule, a closed form, an oracle, or a bug it catches.
//   Invariants and oracles cite the field they come from (§1.3 of the README). Heuristics never become laws.
//
// Grounding
//   Property-based testing with shrinking; the laws themselves come from solid modelling (Requicha 1980,
//   Mäntylä 1988), layered manufacturing (Dolenc & Mäkelä 1994) and classical geometry (Cavalieri, Pappus).
//
// Notice
//   - Nobody writes associativity by hand: declaring the structure generates it.
//   - A law without `justifies` is refused. Most refused laws should be plain assertions in an example.
//   - Shrinking finds two kinds of bug: engine bugs and wrong properties. The first one below is a wrong property.
//   - The examples elsewhere never call laws inline; they point here.
//
// Results in `// →` comments show the illustrative shape of a result.

import { j, mm } from 'jig'

// ── Fixtures ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
const box = j.part('box')
  .params({ w: mm(60), d: mm(40), h: mm(30), wall: mm(2) })
  .extrude(j.sketch('base', { on: j.plane.XY }).rect('r', 'w', 'd', { center: true }).profiles(), 'h', { id: 'body' })
  .shell(j.feat('body').endFace(), 'wall', { id: 'shell' })

// ── 1. Structures are declared once; their laws are derived ──────────────────
// This is how the library itself declares two of its sorts (users only do this for sorts they add).
const shapeLaws = j.structure(j.Shape, 'booleanAlgebra', {
  join: (a, b) => a.union(b), meet: (a, b) => a.intersect(b), eq: (a, b) => a.volume().eq(b.volume(), j.q('1e-6 mm^3')),
  justifies: 'rewrite: chains of unions fuse into one n-ary boolean',
})
shapeLaws.map(L => L.name)
// → ['shape.join.assoc', 'shape.join.comm', 'shape.join.idem', 'shape.meet.assoc', 'shape.meet.comm', 'shape.meet.idem',
//    'shape.absorption', 'shape.distributive', 'shape.inclusionExclusion']

const transformLaws = j.structure(j.Transform, 'group', {
  op: (a, b) => a.then(b), id: j.tx.identity, inv: a => a.inverse(), eq: (a, b) => a.eq(b, { tol: 1e-12 }),
  justifies: 'rewrite: placement chains fuse; ports align through inverses',
})

// ── 2. The built-in suite ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
j.laws.check(j.laws.suite, { n: 200, seed: 1 }).map(r => [r.law, r.tier, r.ok ? '✓' : '✗', r.source ?? ''])
// → law                   tier         ok  source
//   quantity.*            structural   ✓   dimensional analysis
//   point.affine          structural   ✓
//   transform.group       structural   ✓   rigid motions SE(3)
//   shape.boolean         structural   ✓   Requicha 1980
//   region.boolean        structural   ✓   Requicha 1980
//   field.lattice         structural   ✓   Hart 1996
//   timeline.monoid       structural   ✓
//   pattern.action        structural   ✓
//   brep.eulerPoincare    invariant    ✓   Mäntylä 1988
//   mesh.euler            invariant    ✓
//   sketch.dof            invariant    ✓
//   compile.deterministic invariant    ✓
//   extrude.volume        oracle       ✓   Cavalieri
//   revolve.volume        oracle       ✓   Pappus–Guldinus
//   slice.volume          oracle       ✓   Cavalieri
//   slice.cusp            oracle       ✓   Dolenc & Mäkelä 1994
//   snap.deflection       oracle       ✓   beam theory
//   gear.centreDistance   oracle       ✓   involute gearing
//   stack.soundness       oracle       ✓   interval arithmetic
//   plates.bound          oracle       ✓   bin-packing lower bound

// On a fixture the results are concrete. For the box:
//   brep.eulerPoincare: V 16 − E 24 + F 11 − (L 12 − F 11) − 2(S 1 − G 0) = 0   (the rim face has two loops)
//   extrude.volume:     area 2'400 mm² · 30 mm = 72'000 mm³ before the shell

// ── 3. Writing a law: say what it pays for, or it is refused ─────────────────
const gapLaw = j.law('printInPlace.gap',
  j.gen.params(j.lib.hinge.pin({ knuckles: 5, clearance: 'printInPlace' })),
  hinge => j.compile(hinge).metric('minGap').gte(j.fit.gap('printInPlace')),
  { tier: 'invariant', justifies: 'catches hinges that fuse when printed', source: 'house rule, calibrated in 50' })

const vague = j.law('box.looksRight', j.gen.params(box), b => j.compile(b).diagnostics.length === 0)
j.laws.check([gapLaw, vague], { n: 100, seed: 3 })
// → [{ law: 'printInPlace.gap', tier: 'invariant', ok: true, n: 100, justifies: 'catches hinges that fuse when printed' },
//    { law: 'box.looksRight', ok: false, error: 'no justifies: make it an example assertion, or say what it pays for' }]

// ── 4. Fuzzing profile detection: a wrong property, caught by shrinking ──────
const shoelace = pts => Math.abs(pts.reduce((acc, [x, y], i) => {
  const [x2, y2] = pts[(i + 1) % pts.length]
  return acc + x * y2 - x2 * y
}, 0)) / 2

const areaLaw = gen => j.law('profile.area', gen,
  pts => j.sketch('fz', { on: j.plane.XY }).polyline('p', pts, { closed: true }).profiles().area()
    .eq(j.q(`${shoelace(pts)} mm^2`), j.q('1e-6 mm^2')),
  { tier: 'oracle', justifies: 'oracle: profile areas match the shoelace formula', source: 'Gauss area formula' })

j.laws.check([areaLaw(j.gen.polygon({ vertices: [3, 12], radius: mm(50) }))], { n: 500, seed: 11 })
// → [{ law: 'profile.area', ok: false, counterexample: [[12.4, -3.1], [40.2, 18.8], …  9 vertices],
//      shrunk: [[0, 0], [2, 2], [2, 0], [0, 2]],
//      note: 'self-intersecting bow-tie: even–odd profiles keep both lobes (1 + 1 mm²); the shoelace formula cancels them (+1 − 1)' }]

// The engine is right and the property is wrong. Restrict the generator to the domain the formula covers:
j.laws.check([areaLaw(j.gen.polygon({ vertices: [3, 12], radius: mm(50), simple: true }))], { n: 500, seed: 11 })
// → [{ law: 'profile.area', ok: true, n: 500 }]

// ── 5. Fuzzing CSG: the classic printing hazard ──────────────────────────────
const printableUnion = j.law('union.manifold',
  j.gen.csg({ count: 2, depth: 3, primitives: ['box', 'cyl', 'sphere'], size: mm(40), snap: mm(5) }),
  ([a, b]) => j.compile(j.part('u').add(a.union(b))).body().topology.residual === 0,
  { tier: 'invariant', justifies: 'catches unions the slicer would read as two bodies', source: 'Mäntylä 1988' })
j.laws.check([printableUnion], { n: 300, seed: 5 })
// → [{ law: 'union.manifold', ok: false,
//      shrunk: [j.cyl(mm(5), mm(10)), j.cyl(mm(5), mm(10)).moved(j.tx.move(10, 0, 0))],
//      detail: 'the cylinders touch along a line: a non-manifold edge',
//      diagnostic: { kind: 'boolean.nonManifold', fix: 'separate them by ≥ 0.01 mm, or overlap by ≥ lw(1) so the slicer sees one body' } }]
// A snap grid makes these coincidences likely, which is the point: real models are full of round numbers.

// ── 6. Reference robustness, over the model's own parameters ─────────────────
const fragile = box.fillet(j.sel.edges('|Z').of('box').nth(3), mm(4), { id: 'corner' })
j.laws.check(j.laws.for(fragile), { only: ['refs.robust'], n: 100, seed: 2 })
// → [{ law: 'refs.robust', ok: false,
//      counterexample: { w: 37 mm, d: 52 mm }, shrunk: { w: 40 mm, d: 40 mm },
//      note: "nth(3) sorts edges by length, so it flips where w = d: corner moves from top-right to top-left" }]
const sturdy = box.fillet(j.feat('body').sideFaces().edges('|Z').near(j.pt(30, 20, 15)).expect(1), mm(4), { id: 'corner' })
j.laws.check(j.laws.for(sturdy), { only: ['refs.robust'], n: 100, seed: 2 })
// → [{ law: 'refs.robust', ok: true, n: 100 }]

// ── 7. Determinism: an undeclared effect is named ────────────────────────────
const bumpy = box.feature('bumps', (bodies, ctx) =>
  bodies.map(b => b.union(j.sphere(mm(2 + Math.random())).moved(j.tx.move(0, 0, 30)))))
j.laws.check(j.laws.for(bumpy), { only: ['compile.deterministic'], n: 3 })
// → [{ law: 'compile.deterministic', ok: false, culprit: { at: 'bumps', reason: 'lambda reads Math.random (an undeclared effect)' },
//      fix: 'use j.field.noise(scale, { seed }) or take the value from ctx.seed' }]

// ── 8. What stays out of the suite ───────────────────────────────────────────
// The 45° overhang rule, layer-strength risk and the fit classes are heuristics. They are calibrated metrics
// (see 16 and 50), and a "law" about them would only test the calibration data against itself.
// Mobility (Grübler–Kutzbach) is an analysis: two coaxial hinges make the formula wrong while the model is fine (see 15).

// ── 9. In CI ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
const results = j.laws.check([...j.laws.suite, ...shapeLaws, ...transformLaws, gapLaw, printableUnion], { n: 200, seed: 1 })
results.filter(r => !r.ok).length   // → 1   (union.manifold: kept as a regression case until the kernel heals line contacts)

44 Variants, remixes and merges: models are values, so history is algebra

44-variants-remixes-merges.js · 102 lines
// 44 · Variants, remixes and merges: models are values, so history is algebra
//
// Model
//   A model is an immutable value with a content hash, the root of a Merkle DAG of features.
//   j.diff(a, b) compares feature graphs, not files: params, features, specs and references.
//   j.merge(base, ours, theirs) is a three-way merge on that graph. A change made on one side only
//   is applied, the same change made on both sides is applied once, and different changes to the same
//   path are conflicts. Conflict resolution is a slot: the default keeps base and reports, and a lambda wraps it.
//   j.remix(model, { from, license }) records attribution in L0, where it travels with every export.
//
// Notice
//   - Branches need no branching tool: const thin = mine.params({ t: mm(3) }) is a branch.
//   - The merge re-resolves references through genealogy, so my logo stays on the top face after upstream edits.
//   - Attribution changes the hash of the value but not the geometry, so every feature cache still hits.
//   - Upstream can keep publishing. Rebasing a remix is the same merge again.
//
// Results in `// →` comments show the illustrative shape of a result.

import { j, mm } from 'jig'

// ── Fixture: the author's model family and two published versions ────────────
const deskPlate = ({ t, fit }) => j.part('desk-plate')
  .params({ t })
  .extrude(j.sketch('outline', { on: j.plane.XY }).rect('r', 80, 50, { center: true, r: 4 }).profiles(), 't', { id: 'body' })
  .hole(j.sketch('holes', { on: j.plane.XY }).point('h1', [32, 17])
    .pattern(['h1'], j.pattern.mirror(j.axis.X).times(j.pattern.mirror(j.axis.Y))), j.hole.clearance('M3', { fit }), { id: 'mount' })

const v1 = deskPlate({ t: mm(4), fit: 'snug' })
const v2 = deskPlate({ t: mm(3.5), fit: 'slide' })    // upstream: "holes were tight; also saves 12 % filament"

j.hash(v1)                          // → 'b3:4e1a07…'
j.diff(v1, v2)
// → { added: [], removed: [],
//     changed: [{ path: 'params.t', from: 4 mm, to: 3.5 mm }, { path: 'mount.spec.fit', from: 'snug', to: 'slide' }] }

// ── 1. A remix: fork with attribution ────────────────────────────────────────
const logo = await j.load.svg('my-logo.svg')                       // an effect; the result is a hashed value
const upstream = j.remix(v1, { from: 'ana/desk-plate', license: 'CC-BY-4.0' })
const mine = upstream
  .params({ t: mm(5) })                                            // stiffer, for a monitor arm clamp
  .emboss(j.region.svg(logo, { height: mm(20) }), mm(0.6), { on: j.feat('body').endFace(), op: 'join', id: 'logo' })

j.hash(upstream) === j.hash(v1)     // → false   (attribution is part of the value)
j.compile(upstream).trace.every(p => p.cached)   // → true    (geometry identical: every feature is a cache hit)
j.compile(mine).ir.text('L0').split('\n').slice(0, 3)
// → ['source desk-plate  b3:9d22c1…',
//    '  remix-of ana/desk-plate @ b3:4e1a07…  license CC-BY-4.0',
//    '  loaded my-logo.svg  sha256:51f0…']

j.diff(v1, mine)
// → { added: ['logo (emboss, join, on body/end)'], removed: [],
//     changed: [{ path: 'params.t', from: 4 mm, to: 5 mm }], meta: ['remix-of ana/desk-plate'] }

// ── 2. Three-way merge: upstream's fix into my remix ─────────────────────────
const m1 = j.merge(v1, mine, v2)    // base, ours, theirs
m1.conflicts
// → [{ path: 'params.t', kind: 'both-changed', base: 4 mm, ours: 5 mm, theirs: 3.5 mm }]
j.diff(mine, m1.model)
// → { changed: [{ path: 'mount.spec.fit', from: 'snug', to: 'slide' }],          (theirs, applied)
//     unresolved: ['params.t kept at base (4 mm) until resolved'] }            (the default for conflicts)

// ── 3. Resolving the conflict: two ways ──────────────────────────────────────
// (a) As a value edit, like any other change:
const resolvedA = m1.model.params({ t: mm(5) })

// (b) As a slot: wrap the default resolver with a lambda that knows my intent.
const m2 = j.merge(v1, mine, v2, {
  resolve: (c, ctx) => c.path === 'params.t' ? c.ours : ctx.default(c),
})
m2.conflicts                        // → []
j.hash(m2.model) === j.hash(resolvedA)   // → true   (both routes give the same value)

const M = j.compile(m2.model)
M.why(j.feat('body').endFace())     // → { resolved: ['body/end'], chain: ['extrude(outline) cap'], note: 'unchanged by the merge' }
M.param('t')                        // → { value: 5 mm, src: 'merge: ours (resolver lambda)', deps: [] }
M.decisions.filter(d => d.at.startsWith('mount'))
// → [{ at: 'mount', kind: 'hole', chose: 'vertical: Ø3.4 mm + slide 0.2 mm', reason: 'fit class from upstream v2' }]

// ── 4. Branches are plain values ─────────────────────────────────────────────
const branches = {
  mine:  m2.model,
  thin:  m2.model.params({ t: mm(3) }),
  thick: m2.model.params({ t: mm(6) }),
  plain: m2.model.suppress('logo'),
}
Object.entries(branches).map(([name, b]) => [name, j.hash(b).slice(0, 10), j.compile(b).metric('mass')])
// → [['mine',  'b3:7c10ae', 25.1 g],      plate area ≈ 3'950 mm² (PLA, solid)
//    ['thin',  'b3:e2245f', 15.3 g],      3 mm: 14.7 g + 0.6 g logo
//    ['thick', 'b3:0b9d31', 30.0 g],      6 mm: 29.4 g + 0.6 g logo
//    ['plain', 'b3:51c6d8', 24.5 g]]      5 mm, no logo

// ── 5. Upstream publishes again: rebasing is the same merge ──────────────────
const v3 = deskPlate({ t: mm(3.5), fit: 'slide' }).fillet(j.sel.edges('>Z').of('body'), mm(1), { id: 'soften' })
const rebased = j.merge(v2, m2.model, v3, { resolve: (c, ctx) => c.path === 'params.t' ? c.ours : ctx.default(c) })
rebased.conflicts                   // → []
rebased.decisions
// → [{ kind: 'order', chose: ['logo', 'soften'], reason: 'both sides appended after mount; supports are disjoint, so they commute' }]
j.diff(m2.model, rebased.model)
// → { added: ['soften (fillet on the outer top edges; the logo edges belong to feature logo, so of(body) excludes them)'] }
j.export.tmf(j.compile(rebased.model)).report.kept
// → ['plates', 'settings', 'part names', 'attribution: ana/desk-plate (CC-BY-4.0)']

45 Print rules: design-for-printing as data

45-rules-print-dfm.js · 101 lines
// 45 · Print rules: design-for-printing as data
//
// Model
//   A rule is a predicate over a compiled program (topology, analysis fields, orientation, printer
//   context) that yields diagnostics: { level, kind, at, message, fix }. A rule set is a named list.
//   Rule sets compose like style sheets: right-biased by rule name and idempotent, so
//   [fdm, bridge(15 mm)] is fdm with a longer bridge.
//   Thresholds use symbolic units (lw, layer, nozzle), so one rule set is right on any printer.
//   Rules feed three consumers: the diagnostics list, objectives (require), and release gates (preset.production).
//
// Notice
//   - Every finding names its feature and carries a fix written as code, ready to paste.
//   - Horizontal holes made with j.hole become teardrops by default. The rule exists for holes made any other way.
//   - Changing the process changes the verdict: the same lid passes some resin rules and fails others.
//   - Production does not add rules. It raises their level, so iterating stays quiet and release stays strict.
//
// Results in `// →` comments show the illustrative shape of a result.

import { j, mm, deg, lw, layer } from 'jig'

// ── Fixture: a sensor-box lid with four problems ─────────────────────────────
const lid = j.part('lid')
  .params({ wall: mm(0.6) })
  .extrude(j.sketch('top', { on: j.plane.XY }).rect('r', 70, 45, { center: true, r: 3 }).profiles(), mm(1.2), { id: 'top' })
  .extrude(j.sketch('lip', { on: j.feat('top').endFace() })
    .rect('outer', 66, 41, { center: true }).rect('inner', '66 mm - 2 * wall', '41 mm - 2 * wall', { center: true })
    .profiles(), mm(6), { id: 'lip' })
  .cut(j.sketch('cable', { on: j.plane.YZ }).circle('c', 3, { at: [0, 4.2] }).profiles(), { through: 'all' }, { id: 'cable' })  // a cut, not a j.hole
  .cut(j.sketch('win', { on: j.plane.XZ }).rect('w', 14, 3, { at: [-7, 3.2] }).profiles(), { through: 'all' }, { id: 'window' })
  .emboss(j.region.text('rev 2', { size: mm(3) }), mm(0.2), { on: j.feat('top').startFace(), op: 'cut', id: 'rev' })

// ── 1. The FDM rule set ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
const L = j.compile(j.print('lid', { parts: [lid] }).orient('+Z'))   // lip up, top plate on the bed
j.check(L, j.rules.fdm)
// → [{ level: 'warning', kind: 'print.thinWall', at: 'lip', message: 'wall 0.6 mm < 2lw (0.9 mm): a single perimeter',
//      fix: "lid.params({ wall: lw(2) })" },
//    { level: 'warning', kind: 'print.overhang', at: 'cable', message: 'horizontal Ø6 mm hole: its top arc overhangs up to 90°',
//      fix: "replace the cut with .hole(j.point.center(j.feat('lip').sideFace('outer.right')), j.hole.simple(mm(6), mm(2)), { id: 'cable' }); j.hole makes a 45° teardrop when the axis is horizontal" },
//    { level: 'warning', kind: 'print.bridge', at: 'window', message: 'bridge span 14 mm > 10 mm',
//      fix: "split the window in two (rect('w', 6, 3) twice), or add a 45° chamfer to its top edge" },
//    { level: 'warning', kind: 'print.textIllegible', at: 'rev', message: 'stroke 0.30 mm < 1lw (0.45 mm); depth 0.2 mm < 3 layers (0.6 mm)',
//      fix: "j.region.text('rev 2', { size: mm(5) }), depth layer(3)" }]

// ── 2. Applying the fixes: the teardrop comes from the default, not from the rule ─
const fixed = lid
  .params({ wall: lw(2) })
  .suppress('cable')
  .hole(j.point.center(j.feat('lip').sideFace('outer.right')), j.hole.simple(mm(6), mm(2)), { id: 'cable2' })
  .suppress('window')
  .cut(j.sketch('win2', { on: j.plane.XZ }).rect('w', 6, 3, { at: [-7, 3.2] }).pattern(['w'], j.pattern.linear(j.dir('+X'), { count: 2, step: mm(8) })).profiles(),
    { through: 'all' }, { id: 'window2' })
  .suppress('rev')
  .emboss(j.region.text('rev 2', { size: mm(5) }), layer(3), { on: j.feat('top').startFace(), op: 'cut', id: 'rev2' })

const F = j.compile(j.print('lid', { parts: [fixed] }).orient('+Z'))
F.decisions.find(d => d.at === 'cable2')
// → { at: 'cable2', kind: 'hole', chose: 'teardrop 45°, point +Z', alternatives: ['round', 'bridged'], reason: 'axis ⟂ build direction' }
j.check(F, j.rules.fdm)             // → []

// ── 3. Your own rules: thresholds tweaked, custom checks added ───────────────
const insertWalls = j.rule.custom('insert-walls', (prog, ctx) =>
  prog.find('hole').filter(h => h.spec.kind === 'insert')
    .map(h => ({ h, wall: j.inspect.wall(j.feat(h.id).bores(), { min: lw(4) }) }))
    .filter(x => x.wall.min.lt(lw(4).resolve(ctx)))
    .map(x => ({ level: 'warning', kind: 'rule.insert-walls', at: x.h.id,
                 message: `${x.wall.min} of plastic around a heat-set insert; 4lw holds the knurl`,
                 fix: `j.lib.insert('M3x5.7').boss({ wall: lw(4) })` })))

const house = j.rules('house', [j.rules.fdm, j.rule.bridge({ max: mm(15) }), j.rule.overhang({ max: deg(50) }), insertWalls])
j.check(L, house).map(d => d.kind)
// → ['print.thinWall', 'print.overhang', 'print.textIllegible']   (the 14 mm bridge passes the house limit of 15 mm)

// ── 4. Other processes, other verdicts ───────────────────────────────────────
const resin = j.compile(j.print('lid', { printer: j.printer('generic-msla'), material: j.material('resin-standard'), parts: [lid] }))
j.check(resin, j.rules.msla)
// → [{ level: 'warning', kind: 'print.island', at: 'rev', message: '4 letter islands start mid-air in the chosen 30° tilt', fix: 'supports: auto, or move the text to a side face' }]
// The 0.6 mm wall passes (msla minimum 0.5 mm), overhangs and bridges are left to supports, and 0.3 mm strokes resolve at 50 µm pixels.

const tightHinge = j.lib.hinge.pin({ knuckles: 5, clearance: mm(0.25) })   // a print-in-place hinge, see 15
j.check(j.compile(j.print('hinge', { parts: [tightHinge] })), j.rules.printInPlace)
// → [{ level: 'warning', kind: 'asm.interference', at: 'hinge', message: 'knuckle gap 0.25 mm < printInPlace 0.40 mm: likely to fuse',
//      fix: "j.lib.hinge.pin({ knuckles: 5, clearance: 'printInPlace' })" }]

// ── 5. Rules as an objective: infeasible means excluded ──────────────────────
const walls = j.design({ wall: j.param.choice([mm(0.6), lw(2), lw(3)]) }, p => j.print('lid', { parts: [fixed.params({ wall: p.wall })] }))
const r = await j.search.grid(walls, { objective: j.objective.lexicographic([j.objective.require(j.rules.fdm), j.objective.minimize('mass')]) })
r.table()
// → rank  wall   feasible  mass     violations
//   1     2lw    yes       6.1 g    (lip 214 mm × 6 mm × 0.9 mm on a 1.2 mm top plate)
//   2     3lw    yes       6.8 g
//   3     0.6mm  no        5.6 g    print.thinWall

// ── 6. preset.production: same rules, higher stakes ──────────────────────────
const P = j.compile(j.print('lid', { parts: [lid] }).orient('+Z').use(j.preset.production))
P.diagnostics.map(d => [d.level, d.kind])
// → [['error', 'print.thinWall'], ['error', 'print.overhang'], ['error', 'print.bridge'], ['error', 'print.textIllegible']]
const out = j.export.tmf(P)
out.data                            // → null
out.report                          // → { refused: true, reason: '4 errors under preset.production', kept: [], approximated: [], dropped: [] }
j.export.tmf(j.compile(j.print('lid', { parts: [fixed] }).orient('+Z').use(j.preset.production))).report.refused   // → false

F Scientific study

50 A factorial calibration experiment: from pin-hole coupons to a fit profile

50-factorial-calibration-experiment.js · 117 lines
// 50 · A factorial calibration experiment: from pin-hole coupons to a fit profile
//
// Model
//   An experiment is a value: factors × levels, a design, replicates, a randomisation and a seed.
//   Factors: clearance (5 levels) × hole orientation (2) × material (2) × layer height (3) = 60 cells.
//   Response: does the pin slide in by hand? (binary), plus an ordinal grade seized < press < slide < loose.
//   Material and layer height are hard to change within one print, so they form whole plots
//   (one print job each); orientation and clearance vary inside the plate. This is a split-plot design.
//   Analysis: logistic regression  logit P(slide) = β₀ + β_c·c + β_h·horizontal + β_m·PETG + β_t·layer,
//   then solve P(slide) = 0.9 for c in each condition. The solutions are the calibrated `slide` class.
//
// Notice
//   - The plan is hashed before anything is printed. That hash is the pre-registration.
//   - Printing and measuring are effects. Their results come back as data, and the analysis of that data is pure.
//   - The output is a fit profile (see 16) that every fit-aware slot can use.
//
// Results in `// →` comments show the illustrative shape of a result.

import { j, mm } from 'jig'

// ── 1. The coupon: five pin-hole pairs, one per clearance level ─────────────
const clearances = [mm(0.10), mm(0.15), mm(0.20), mm(0.25), mm(0.30)]
const coupon = j.fit.coupon({ kind: 'pin-hole', range: [mm(0.10), mm(0.30)], steps: 5 })
  .params({ pinD: mm(5), depth: mm(8), label: true })     // each pair is embossed with its clearance

j.compile(coupon).summary()
// → { bodies: 6, pairs: 5, labels: ['.10', '.15', '.20', '.25', '.30'], volume: 4.1 cm³, bbox: [62, 14, 10] mm }

// ── 2. The experiment, pre-registered ───────────────────────────────────────
const exp = j.experiment({
  hypothesis: [
    'H1: horizontal holes need ≥ 0.04 mm more clearance than vertical holes to reach P(slide) ≥ 0.9',
    'H2: PETG needs more clearance than PLA (β_m < 0)',
    'H3: across 0.12–0.28 mm, the layer-height effect on required clearance is smaller than the orientation effect',
  ],
  factors: {
    clearance: clearances,
    orientation: ['vertical', 'horizontal'],             // hole axis ∥ or ⟂ build direction
    material: ['PLA', 'PETG'],
    layer: [mm(0.12), mm(0.2), mm(0.28)],
  },
  responses: { slides: 'bool', grade: ['seized', 'press', 'slide', 'loose'] },
  design: 'full-factorial',
  wholePlots: ['material', 'layer'],                     // one print job per (material, layer) per replicate
  replicates: 3,
  randomize: { order: 'whole-plots', within: 'plate-position' },
  seed: 50,
})

exp.runs.length                          // → 180 observations = 5 · 2 · 2 · 3 cells × 3 replicates
exp.runs.slice(0, 2)
// → [{ run: 1, print: 'P07', material: 'PETG', layer: 0.2 mm, orientation: 'horizontal', clearance: 0.25 mm, slot: 'B3' },
//    { run: 2, print: 'P07', material: 'PETG', layer: 0.2 mm, orientation: 'vertical',   clearance: 0.10 mm, slot: 'A1' }]
const registered = j.hash(exp)          // → 'sha256:9c1e…'   (publish it before printing)

// ── 3. The prints: 18 jobs, coupons placed at randomised plate positions ─────
const jobs = exp.wholePlots.map(w => j.print(`cal-${w.print}`, {
  printer: j.printer('mk4'), material: j.material(w.material),
}).slice({ layer: w.layer })
  .add('vert', coupon, { orient: '+Z' })                // pins standing up: vertical holes
  .add('horiz', coupon, { orient: '+Y' })               // pins lying down: horizontal holes (teardrops off for this study)
  .set('holes.teardrop', false)                         // raw escape hatch: the study needs round holes
  .plates({ pack: (parts, ctx) => ctx.default(w.shuffle(parts)) }))   // the experiment's seeded plate positions

j.compile(jobs[0]).metrics()
// → { plates: 1, printTime: 38 min, filament: 9.6 g, supportVolume: 0 }
jobs.length                              // → 18 = 2 materials · 3 layer heights · 3 replicates

// ── 4. Measurements come back as data (an effect) ──────────────────────────
const rows = await j.load.csv('data/cal-2026-10-results.csv')
// columns: run, slides, grade, measuredHoleD, measuredPinD, operator
const recorded = exp.record(rows)        // still a value; its hash now includes the data's content hash
recorded.missing                         // → []   (180 of 180 recorded)

// ── 5. Analysis: logistic regression with print-level clustering ───────────
const fitModel = recorded.analyze({
  model: 'logistic',
  formula: 'slides ~ clearance + orientation + material + layer',
  cluster: 'print',                      // whole plots are correlated; use cluster-robust errors
})
fitModel.coefficients
// → { intercept: -4.0, clearance: 40.0 /mm, horizontal: -2.0, PETG: -1.2, layer: -8.0 /mm }
//   (95% CIs: clearance [31, 49], horizontal [-2.7, -1.3], PETG [-1.8, -0.6], layer [-15, -1])

// Required clearance for P = 0.9 (logit 2.197) at layer 0.2 mm:
//   PLA vertical:   c = (2.197 + 4.0 + 1.6) / 40 = 0.195 mm
//   PLA horizontal: + 2.0 / 40 = 0.245 mm       PETG: + 1.2 / 40 more
fitModel.hypotheses
// → { H1: { supported: true, estimate: '+0.050 mm', ci: ['+0.033', '+0.068'] },
//     H2: { supported: true, estimate: 'β_m = -1.2' },
//     H3: { supported: true, layerEffect: '+0.032 mm over 0.12→0.28', orientationEffect: '+0.050 mm' } }

// ── 6. From the model to fit profiles ──────────────────────────────────────
const cal = j.fit.calibrate(rows, { model: fitModel, target: 0.9, by: ['material', 'orientation'], at: { layer: mm(0.2) } })
cal.classes
// → { PLA:  { vertical: { slide: 0.195 mm }, horizontal: { slide: 0.245 mm } },
//     PETG: { vertical: { slide: 0.225 mm }, horizontal: { slide: 0.275 mm } } }

const mk4pla = j.fit.profile('mk4-pla', {
  printer: j.printer('mk4'), material: j.material('PLA'),
  classes: cal.classes.PLA,              // other classes (press, snug, free) are scaled from the same curve
  holeComp: mm(0.1), elephantFoot: mm(0.2),
})
const mk4petg = j.fit.profile('mk4-petg', { printer: j.printer('mk4'), material: j.material('PETG'), classes: cal.classes.PETG })

// Any model can now resolve fit classes against the calibration, with provenance:
const block = j.part('axle-block').fit('mk4-pla')
  .add(j.box(mm(20), mm(20), mm(10)))
  .hole(j.pt(10, 10, 10), j.hole.clearance('M5', { fit: 'slide' }), { id: 'axle' })
const P = j.compile(block)
P.param('axle.d')
// → { value: 5.39 mm, src: "fit 'mk4-pla' (calibrated, exp sha256:9c1e…), slide/vertical = 0.195 mm" }

// ── 7. Honest limits, recorded with the result ─────────────────────────────
fitModel.diagnostics
// → [{ level: 'info', kind: 'experiment.extrapolation', message: 'layer 0.32 mm is outside the studied range [0.12, 0.28]' }]

51 A human-study protocol: three modelling paradigms, novices, and a phone stand

51-human-study-protocol.js · 134 lines
// 51 · A human-study protocol: three modelling paradigms, novices, and a phone stand
//
// Model
//   Paradigm (sketch-first | CSG-first | field-first) is the factor of interest. Task (three phone-stand
//   briefs) and position (1st, 2nd, 3rd) are nuisance factors. A 3 × 3 Graeco-Latin square balances all
//   three: every paradigm meets every task once and every position once across the three sequences.
//   Each participant follows one sequence (within-subject), so participant variance cancels.
//   Logging stores only the model values participants compiled. Compiles are deterministic, so every
//   measure (diagnostics, rule violations, time to spec) can be recomputed later from those values.
//
// Notice
//   - The brief is an objective: j.objective.require over the compiled Program, so "done" is checked identically for everyone.
//   - Errors come from the same diagnostics registry the engine already emits; no hand coding of videos is needed.
//   - The protocol, analysis plan and ethics notes are hashed together before the first participant: that is the pre-registration.
//
// Results in `// →` comments show the illustrative shape of a result.

import { j, mm, deg, minute } from 'jig'

// ── 1. The briefs, as executable specs ─────────────────────────────────────
// Participants tag the face the phone rests on with a port named 'phone'.
const phoneAngle = prog => prog.node('port:phone').frame.z.angleTo(j.dir('+Z'))
const briefs = {
  A: j.objective.require([                               // desk stand with a cable slot
    prog => phoneAngle(prog).gte(deg(60)) && phoneAngle(prog).lte(deg(70)),
    prog => prog.find(n => n.kind === 'port' && n.id === 'cable').length === 1,
    j.rules.fdm,
  ]),
  B: j.objective.require([                               // bedside stand, landscape, with a 56 mm charging-puck pocket
    prog => phoneAngle(prog).gte(deg(50)) && phoneAngle(prog).lte(deg(65)),
    prog => prog.node('port:puck') != null,
    j.rules.fdm,
  ]),
  C: j.objective.require([                               // travel stand: fits in an 80 × 60 × 20 mm envelope
    prog => prog.metric('bbox').every((d, i) => d.lte([mm(80), mm(60), mm(20)][i])),
    j.rules.fdm,
  ]),
}

// ── 2. Paradigm starters: what each group sees in the first minute ─────────
const starters = {
  'sketch-first': j.part('stand')
    .extrude(j.sketch('side', { on: j.plane.YZ }).polyline('p', [[0, 0], [70, 0], [20, 60]], { closed: true }).profiles(), { symmetric: mm(35) }),
  'csg-first': j.part('stand')
    .add(j.box(mm(70), mm(70), mm(6)))
    .add(j.box(mm(70), mm(6), mm(80)).moved(j.tx.rotate(j.axis.X, deg(-25)))),
  'field-first': j.part('stand')
    .import(j.mesh(j.field.box(mm(70), mm(70), mm(6)).smoothUnion(j.field.capsule([0, 20, 0], [0, 45, 60], mm(4)), mm(6)))),
}

// ── 3. The design: a Graeco-Latin square ───────────────────────────────────
//              position 1      position 2      position 3
//   seq 1      sketch · A      CSG · B         field · C
//   seq 2      CSG · C         field · A       sketch · B
//   seq 3      field · B       sketch · C      CSG · A
const study = j.experiment({
  hypothesis: [
    'H1: CSG-first reaches a spec-satisfying model faster than sketch-first for novices (median time ratio < 0.8)',
    'H2: field-first produces fewer print-rule violations in final models than sketch-first',
    'H3: sketch-first produces the most sketch.* and ref.* diagnostics per minute',
  ],
  factors: {
    paradigm: ['sketch-first', 'csg-first', 'field-first'],
    task: ['A', 'B', 'C'],
    position: [1, 2, 3],
  },
  responses: {
    timeToSpec: 'duration (censored at 25 min)', success: 'bool', diagnosticsPerMin: 'rate',
    ruleViolations: 'count', printed: 'bool', tlx: 'score 0–100', sus: 'score 0–100',
  },
  design: 'graeco-latin',
  replicates: 8,                                         // 8 participants per sequence → 24 participants
  randomize: { order: 'participants-to-sequences' },
  protocol: {
    eligibility: 'adults; < 10 h prior CAD use (screening questionnaire); have used a 3D printer or want to',
    session: '10 min tutorial per paradigm, then 25 min per task; breaks between tasks; about 2 h in total',
    consent: 'written informed consent; screen recording only with an explicit opt-in; withdraw at any time without giving a reason',
    data: 'pseudonymous ids; logs hold model values and timestamps only; raw recordings deleted after coding; 5-year retention',
    approval: 'institutional ethics approval required before the first session; pilots (n = 3) are excluded from analysis',
    compensation: 'fixed, not contingent on performance',
  },
  seed: 51,
})

study.runs.length                        // → 72 = 24 participants × 3 tasks
study.sequences[1]
// → [{ position: 1, paradigm: 'csg-first', task: 'C' }, { position: 2, paradigm: 'field-first', task: 'A' }, { position: 3, paradigm: 'sketch-first', task: 'B' }]
const preregistration = j.hash(study)    // → 'sha256:51ab…'   (hashes hypotheses, design, protocol and the analysis plan below)

// ── 4. The log: a sequence of model values, nothing else ───────────────────
// The workbench appends { t, model } on every compile. Loading the logs is an effect.
const logs = await j.load.json('data/study51/sessions.json')

const measuresOf = (session, brief) => {
  const progs = session.log.map(e => ({ t: e.t, prog: j.compile(e.model) }))   // recomputed, cached by hash
  const first = progs.find(p => j.evaluate(brief, p.prog).feasible)
  const final = progs[progs.length - 1].prog
  const diags = progs.flatMap(p => p.prog.diagnostics)
  return {
    timeToSpec: first ? first.t : minute(25),
    success: Boolean(first),
    diagnosticsPerMin: diags.length / session.minutes,
    byKind: Object.groupBy(diags, d => d.kind.split('.')[0]),
    ruleViolations: j.check(final, j.rules.fdm).filter(d => d.level !== 'info').length,
    edits: session.log.slice(1).map((e, i) => j.diff(session.log[i].model, e.model)),   // the edit trajectory
    finalModel: session.log[session.log.length - 1].model,
  }
}

const rows = logs.map(s => ({ ...s.cell, ...measuresOf(s, briefs[s.cell.task]) }))
const recorded = study.record(rows)
j.hash(j.compile(logs[0].log[3].model)) === logs[0].log[3].hash   // → true   (recomputing a logged model reproduces it)

// ── 5. The analysis plan (pre-registered with the design) ──────────────────
const analysis = recorded.analyze({
  model: 'mixed',
  formulas: {
    timeToSpec: 'log(timeToSpec) ~ paradigm + task + position + (1 | participant)',   // censored: Tobit at 25 min
    success: 'success ~ paradigm + task + position + (1 | participant)',              // logistic link
    ruleViolations: 'ruleViolations ~ paradigm + task + position + (1 | participant)', // Poisson link
  },
  contrasts: ['csg-first - sketch-first', 'field-first - sketch-first'],
  correction: 'holm',
  exclusions: ['technical failure > 5 min', 'did not attempt a task'],
})
analysis.summary
// → { timeToSpec: { 'csg-first/sketch-first': 0.71 [0.58, 0.87], 'field-first/sketch-first': 0.93 [0.76, 1.14] },
//     ruleViolations: { 'field-first/sketch-first': 0.48 [0.31, 0.74] }, H1: 'supported', H2: 'supported', H3: 'supported' }

// ── 6. Printing the finals: the ground truth the rules only predict ────────
// Every final model is printed once on the same printer (an effect); 'printed' records whether it met the brief physically.
const printJobs = rows.map(r => j.print(`p51-${r.participant}-${r.task}`, { printer: j.printer('mk4'), parts: [r.finalModel] }))
printJobs.length                         // → 72

52 Corpus measurement: what do 10,000 real printable models look like?

52-corpus-measurement.js · 114 lines
// 52 · Corpus measurement: what do 10,000 real printable models look like?
//
// Model
//   Thingi10K (Zhou & Jacobson, 2016) is a dataset of 10,000 models uploaded to Thingiverse.
//   For every model we measure topology (manifold, watertight, shells, Euler characteristic, genus),
//   printability (overhang area as uploaded and after auto-orientation, print-rule diagnostics),
//   and repairability (does .repair() make it watertight, and how far does it move the surface?).
//   For a closed orientable 2-manifold with k shells, χ = V − E + F = Σ (2 − 2gᵢ), so genus is defined only after a topology check.
//   Loading files is an effect. Each loaded file becomes a content-hashed value, so every measurement is pure and cached.
//
// Notice
//   - Measuring a corpus uses the same calls as checking one model; the corpus is just a list of values.
//   - A seeded sample gives a cheap pilot; the full run reuses every cached measurement from it.
//   - Reproducibility is data: the manifest of content hashes, the seed, the engine version and the code hash.
//
// Results in `// →` comments show the illustrative shape of a result; they are not findings about the dataset.

import { j, deg } from 'jig'

// ── 1. The corpus index (an effect) and a seeded pilot sample ──────────────
const index = await j.load.csv('data/thingi10k/metadata.csv')     // file_id, thing_id, license, ext, …
index.length                                                     // → 10000

const pilot = j.design({ i: j.param.int(0, index.length - 1) }, p => index[p.i]).sample(500, { seed: 52 })
// a design over row indices doubles as a seeded, reproducible sampler: same seed, same 500 files

// ── 2. Loading by format; unsupported formats are counted, never dropped silently ─
const loaders = { stl: j.load.stl, obj: j.load.obj, '3mf': j.load.tmf }
const load = async row => {
  const loader = loaders[row.ext.toLowerCase()]
  if (!loader) return { row, skipped: `unsupported format .${row.ext}` }
  const src = await loader(`data/thingi10k/raw_meshes/${row.file_id}.${row.ext}`)
  return { row, src, kind: j.ingest.auto(src).kind }               // sanity check: should be 'stl-mesh'
}

// ── 3. One measurement function, pure once the file is loaded ─────────────
const measure = ({ row, src, kind, skipped }) => {
  if (skipped) return { id: row.file_id, skipped }
  const topo = j.compile(j.mesh(src)).mesh()
  // → { faces, vertices, manifold, watertight, eulerChar, genus, shells, boundaryLoops, selfIntersections }
  const closed = topo.manifold && topo.watertight
  const out = {
    id: row.file_id, license: row.license, kind, faces: topo.faces, shells: topo.shells,
    manifold: topo.manifold, watertight: topo.watertight, selfIntersecting: topo.selfIntersections > 0,
    genus: closed ? topo.genus : null,                             // undefined unless the topology check passes
    overhangAsUploaded: j.inspect.overhang(src, { dir: '+Z', max: deg(45) }).fraction,
  }
  if (closed) {
    // closed and manifold, so χ = Σ(2 − 2gᵢ) holds (the suite's mesh.euler) and the genus is meaningful
    const P = j.compile(j.print(`t${row.file_id}`, { parts: [j.part(row.file_id).import(src)] }))
    const up = P.decisions.find(d => d.kind === 'orient').chose     // e.g. '+Y': the auto-orientation's build direction
    out.overhangAuto = j.inspect.overhang(src, { dir: up, max: deg(45) }).fraction
    out.supportVolume = P.metric('supportVolume')
    out.violations = j.check(P, j.rules.fdm).filter(d => d.level !== 'info').map(d => d.kind)
  } else {
    const fixed = j.mesh(src).repair({ holes: true, normals: true, selfIntersections: true, degenerate: true })
    const after = j.compile(fixed).mesh()
    out.repairedWatertight = after.manifold && after.watertight
    out.repairDeviation = j.inspect.hausdorff(src, fixed)          // how far the repair moved the surface
  }
  return out
}

// ── 4. Run the pilot, then the full corpus (cached results are reused) ─────
const run = async rows => {
  const out = []
  for (let k = 0; k < rows.length; k += 64) {                      // bounded concurrency for the loading effect
    const batch = await Promise.all(rows.slice(k, k + 64).map(load))
    out.push(...batch.map(measure))
  }
  return out
}
const pilotRows = await run(pilot)       // look at these first: do the measures mean what we think?
const allRows = await run(index)         // the 500 pilot files are not recomputed: compiles are cached by content hash
allRows.length                           // → 10000

// ── 5. Distributions ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
const share = (rows, f) => rows.filter(f).length / rows.length
const quantiles = (xs, qs = [0.1, 0.5, 0.9]) => {
  const s = xs.filter(x => x != null).sort((a, b) => a - b)
  return Object.fromEntries(qs.map(q => [`p${q * 100}`, s[Math.floor(q * (s.length - 1))]]))
}
const loaded = allRows.filter(r => !r.skipped)
const summary = {
  skipped: allRows.length - loaded.length,
  manifold: share(loaded, r => r.manifold),
  watertight: share(loaded, r => r.watertight),
  multiShell: share(loaded, r => r.shells > 1),
  genus: quantiles(loaded.map(r => r.genus)),
  overhangAsUploaded: quantiles(loaded.map(r => r.overhangAsUploaded)),
  overhangAuto: quantiles(loaded.map(r => r.overhangAuto)),
  repairedToWatertight: share(loaded.filter(r => r.repairedWatertight != null), r => r.repairedWatertight),
  repairDeviation: quantiles(loaded.map(r => r.repairDeviation?.to('mm').value)),
}
summary
// → { skipped: 41, manifold: 0.74, watertight: 0.69, multiShell: 0.31,
//     genus: { p10: 0, p50: 0, p90: 4 },
//     overhangAsUploaded: { p10: 0.00, p50: 0.06, p90: 0.31 }, overhangAuto: { p10: 0.00, p50: 0.02, p90: 0.18 },
//     repairedToWatertight: 0.83, repairDeviation: { p10: 0.00, p50: 0.01, p90: 0.42 } }   (fractions; mm for deviation)

const violationCounts = Object.groupBy(loaded.flatMap(r => r.violations ?? []), k => k)
Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(violationCounts).map(([k, v]) => [k, v.length]))
// → { 'print.overhang': 2410, 'print.thinWall': 1187, 'print.bedFit': 96, 'print.thinFeature': 803, 'print.island': 655 }

// ── 6. Reproducibility record ──────────────────────────────────────────────
const record = {
  corpus: j.hash(index.map(r => r.file_id)),                       // the manifest of what was measured
  contentHashes: loaded.length,                                    // every loaded file's hash is in L0 of its compile
  seed: 52, pilotSize: pilot.length,
  rules: j.hash(j.rules.fdm), engine: j.version,                   // results change when the rules or the engine do
}
const probe = await load(index[0])
j.hash(j.compile(j.mesh(probe.src)).mesh()) === j.hash(j.compile(j.mesh(probe.src)).mesh())   // → true   (the same file gives the same measurements)

60 The design process as a value

60-process-as-value.js · 96 lines
// 60 · The design process as a value
//
// Model
//   A process is a builder like any other: an immutable sequence of steps, built with
//   step (a pure transform), diverge (make n alternatives), critique (filter with rules or a lambda),
//   converge (rank with an objective and keep the best), print and measure (effects), and loop (repeat until a condition holds).
//   Processes compose with then, like feature timelines. They hash, diff and cache, so a changed tail reruns alone.
//   Running it needs effect handlers for print and measure. Recorded effects can be replayed,
//   which makes a whole design session reproducible.
//
// Notice
//   - Only the print and measure steps touch the world. Re-running a process after a change recomputes only the steps downstream of it.
//   - Two processes can be compared with j.diff, just like two models.
//   - A replayed run is exactly reproducible. That turns design sessions into data for 61.
//
// Results in `// →` comments show the illustrative shape of a result.

import { j, mm, lw } from 'jig'

// ── 1. The object family: a rail hook, parametric ─────────────────────────
const hook = ({ t = lw(6), reach = mm(35) } = {}) => j.part('rail-hook')
  .params({ rail: mm(20), t, reach, width: mm(16) })
  .extrude(j.sketch('side', { on: j.plane.XZ })
    .line('back', [0, 0], [0, 26]).line('top', 'back.end', [24, 26]).line('lip', 'top.end', [24, 18])   // the J over the rail
    .line('stem', 'back.start', [0, -30]).line('arm', 'stem.end', [35, -30]).line('tip', 'arm.end', [35, -22])
    .dim('top', 'rail + t').dim('arm', 'reach')
    .offset('body', ['back', 'top', 'lip', 'stem', 'arm', 'tip'], 't')
    .profiles(), { symmetric: 'width' }, { id: 'body' })
  .fillet(j.sel.edges('|Y').where(e => e.concave), mm(3), { id: 'roots' })
  .use(j.preset.functional)

// ── 2. The process ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
const brief = { rail: mm(20), load: 'two coats', printer: 'mk4', material: 'PETG' }

const conceptFirst = j.process
  .step('frame', b => ({ brief: b, fit: 'mk4-petg' }))
  .diverge(6, (ctx, i) => hook({ t: lw(5 + (i % 3)), reach: mm(30 + 5 * Math.floor(i / 3)) }).fit(ctx.fit))
  .critique(j.rules.fdm)                                          // concepts with rule errors are dropped, with reasons
  .converge(j.objective.lexicographic([j.objective.minimize('layerStrengthRisk'), j.objective.minimize('printTime')]))
  .step('coupon', model => ({ model, coupon: j.fit.coupon({ kind: 'slot', range: [mm(0.1), mm(0.4)], steps: 4 }) }))
  .print(c => c.coupon)                                           // effect: print only the coupon first
  .measure({ snapsOnRail: ['tight', 'good', 'loose'], bestSlot: 'index' })
  .step('calibrate', (c, ctx) => c.model.override({ rail: mm(20).add(ctx.measured.bestSlotClearance) }))
  .loop(j.process.print(m => m).measure({ holds: 'bool', wobble: 'bool' }), { until: r => r.holds && !r.wobble, max: 3 })

j.hash(conceptFirst)                      // → 'sha256:60c3…'
conceptFirst.steps.map(s => s.kind)
// → ['step', 'diverge', 'critique', 'converge', 'step', 'print', 'measure', 'step', 'loop']

// ── 3. Running it: effects are handlers you pass in ─────────────────────────
const effects = {
  print: async prog => j.export.tmf(prog).data,                   // hand the 3MF to your printer or print queue
  measure: async form => (await j.load.json('data/hook-measurements.json'))[form.id],   // or a form on your phone
}
const run1 = await j.process.run(conceptFirst, { input: brief, effects, seed: 60 })
run1.trace
// → [{ step: 'diverge', made: 6 },
//    { step: 'critique', kept: 4, dropped: [{ i: 0, kind: 'print.thinWall' }, { i: 3, kind: 'print.overhang' }] },
//    { step: 'converge', chose: 5, scores: [[0.08, 52], [0.11, 47], …] },
//    { step: 'print', what: 'coupon', minutes: 14 }, { step: 'measure', bestSlot: 2 },
//    { step: 'loop', iterations: 2, until: 'holds && !wobble' }]
run1.metrics
// → { prints: 3, printMinutes: 116, filament: 38.7 g, designerMinutes: 22 }   (coupon 14 min + 2 hooks × 51 min)

// ── 4. Change one step: only its downstream cone reruns ────────────────────
const stiffer = conceptFirst.with(p => p.replace('converge',
  j.objective.weighted({ risk: ['layerStrengthRisk', 10], time: ['printTime', 0.05] })))
const run2 = await j.process.run(stiffer, { input: brief, effects: run1.replay() })   // replay recorded measurements
run2.trace.map(t => [t.step, t.cached])
// → [['frame', true], ['diverge', true], ['critique', true], ['converge', false], ['coupon', false], …]
j.hash(run2.value) === j.hash(run1.value)   // → false: the weighted objective picked concept 4 instead of 5

// ── 5. Processes are comparable values ─────────────────────────────────────
const couponFirst = j.process
  .step('frame', b => ({ brief: b, fit: 'mk4-petg' }))
  .step('coupon', c => ({ ...c, coupon: j.fit.coupon({ kind: 'slot', range: [mm(0.1), mm(0.4)], steps: 4 }) }))
  .print(c => c.coupon)
  .measure({ snapsOnRail: ['tight', 'good', 'loose'], bestSlot: 'index' })
  .diverge(6, (ctx, i) => hook({ t: lw(5 + (i % 3)), reach: mm(30 + 5 * Math.floor(i / 3)) }).fit(ctx.fit))
  .critique(j.rules.fdm)
  .converge(j.objective.lexicographic([j.objective.minimize('layerStrengthRisk'), j.objective.minimize('printTime')]))
  .loop(j.process.print(m => m).measure({ holds: 'bool', wobble: 'bool' }), { until: r => r.holds && !r.wobble, max: 3 })

j.diff(conceptFirst, couponFirst)
// → { moved: [{ step: 'coupon', from: 5, to: 2 }, { step: 'print(coupon)', from: 6, to: 3 }, { step: 'measure', from: 7, to: 4 }],
//     removed: ['calibrate'], added: [], note: 'fit known before concepts: diverge sees the calibrated clearance' }

// ── 6. Composing processes reuses work ─────────────────────────────────────
// then concatenates processes, and grouping doesn't matter, so a run of a.then(b).then(c) can reuse a cached
// run of a.then(b) when only c changed. A print can't be undone, so there is nothing more to the algebra than that.
const a = j.process.step('x', v => v), b = j.process.critique(j.rules.fdm), c = j.process.converge(j.objective.minimize('mass'))
j.hash(a.then(b).then(c)) === j.hash(a.then(b.then(c)))          // → true
const c2 = j.process.converge(j.objective.minimize('printTime'))
(await j.process.run(a.then(b).then(c2), { input: brief, effects })).trace.map(t => [t.step, t.cached])
// → [['x', true], ['critique', true], ['converge', false]]   (only the changed tail runs)

61 Designing the design process

61-designing-the-design-process.js · 116 lines
// 61 · Designing the design process
//
// Model
//   Three processes (values, as in 60) compete on the same jobs:
//     calibrate-first : coupon → calibrate → design → critique → print → measure ⟲
//     print-and-fix   : design → print → measure → adjust ⟲ (up to 5 rounds)
//     analyse-first   : design → critique (rules) → fit stack check → converge → print → measure ⟲
//   An experiment crosses process × part family × printer, with replicates. The responses are
//   meta-metrics of the process, not of the part: prints wasted, minutes to the first good print,
//   filament wasted, designer minutes. A seeded printer model drives a cheap simulated pilot;
//   a smaller real run confirms it.
//   The final step designs the objective itself, because the ranking of processes depends on it.
//
// Notice
//   - Effects are injected, so the same process runs against a simulated printer or a real one.
//   - On the mk4, weighted, lexicographic and constrained objectives each crown a different process. The objective is a design decision.
//   - The winner depends on the printer, an interaction you only see when the process is a value you can vary.
//
// Results in `// →` comments show the illustrative shape of a result.

import { j, mm, gram } from 'jig'

// ── 1. Three processes over the same steps ─────────────────────────────────
const families = {
  'snap-box': (fit, p = {}) => j.part('snap-box').fit(fit).params({ w: mm(50), d: mm(35), h: mm(25), ...p }),
  'pin-hinge': (fit, p = {}) => j.assembly('pin-hinge').add('leaf', j.lib.hinge.pin({ knuckles: 5, clearance: 'printInPlace' })).fit(fit),
  'threaded-cap': (fit, p = {}) => j.part('cap').fit(fit).add(j.lib.thread('M30x2', { length: mm(10), internal: true, fit: 'slide' })),
}
const coupon = j.fit.coupon({ kind: 'pin-hole', range: [mm(0.1), mm(0.4)], steps: 4 })
const design = j.process.step('design', ctx => families[ctx.family](ctx.fit ?? 'default'))
const check = j.process.print(m => m).measure({ works: 'bool', defect: ['none', 'tight', 'loose', 'fused', 'other'] })

const processes = {
  'calibrate-first': j.process.print(() => coupon).measure({ bestPair: 'index' })
    .step('calibrate', (c, ctx) => ({ ...ctx, fit: j.fit.calibrate(ctx.measured) }))
    .then(design).critique(j.rules.fdm)
    .then(check.loop(check, { until: r => r.works, max: 4 })),
  'print-and-fix': design
    .then(check.loop(j.process.step('adjust', (m, ctx) => m.override(ctx.adjustFor(ctx.measured.defect))).then(check),
      { until: r => r.works, max: 5 })),
  'analyse-first': j.process.diverge(4, (ctx, i) => families[ctx.family](ctx.fit ?? 'default').override({ gapScale: 0.8 + 0.15 * i }))
    .critique(j.rules.fdm).critique(j.rules.printInPlace)          // rules and clearance checks before any print
    .converge(j.objective.minimize('fitWorstCase'))                // the stack check of 16, as an objective
    .then(check.loop(check, { until: r => r.works, max: 4 })),
}
Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(processes).map(([k, p]) => [k, j.hash(p).slice(0, 14)]))
// → { 'calibrate-first': 'sha256:61a0…', 'print-and-fix': 'sha256:61b7…', 'analyse-first': 'sha256:61c2…' }

// ── 2. Meta-metrics: metrics of a process run ──────────────────────────────
j.metric('printsWasted', run => run.prints.filter(p => !p.kept).length, { dir: 'min', unit: 'count', about: 'prints not kept, coupons included' })
j.metric('minutesToFirstGood', run => run.elapsedUntil(r => r.works), { dir: 'min', unit: 'min' })
j.metric('filamentWasted', run => run.prints.filter(p => !p.kept).reduce((g, p) => g.add(p.filament), gram(0)), { dir: 'min', unit: 'g' })
j.metric('designerMinutes', run => run.designerTime, { dir: 'min', unit: 'min' })

// ── 3. A simulated printer from the calibration study (50) ─────────────────
// Each printer is a logistic model of whether a modelled clearance works; handlers get the run's seeded ctx.random.
const printerModel = ({ beta0, betaC }) => ({
  print: async (prog, ctx) => ({ minutes: prog.metric('printTime'), filament: prog.metric('filament') }),
  measure: async (form, ctx) => {
    const c = ctx.lastPrint.param('fit.slide').value.to('mm').value
    const pWorks = 1 / (1 + Math.exp(-(beta0 + betaC * c)))
    return { works: ctx.random() < pWorks, bestPair: Math.round((c - 0.1) / 0.1) }
  },
})
const printers = { mk4: printerModel({ beta0: -5.6, betaC: 40 }), ender3: printerModel({ beta0: -7.2, betaC: 32 }) }

// ── 4. The experiment: simulated pilot first, then a real confirmation ─────
const exp = j.experiment({
  hypothesis: [
    'H1: calibrate-first wastes fewer prints than print-and-fix on an uncalibrated printer (ender3)',
    'H2: the process × printer interaction on minutesToFirstGood is non-zero',
  ],
  factors: { process: Object.keys(processes), family: Object.keys(families), printer: Object.keys(printers) },
  responses: { printsWasted: 'count', minutesToFirstGood: 'min', filamentWasted: 'g', designerMinutes: 'min' },
  design: 'full-factorial', replicates: 4, randomize: { order: 'runs' }, seed: 61,
})
exp.runs.length                          // → 72 = 3 processes · 3 families · 2 printers · 4 replicates

const simulated = await Promise.all(exp.runs.map(r =>
  j.process.run(processes[r.process], { input: { family: r.family }, effects: printers[r.printer], seed: r.seed })))
const pilot = exp.record(simulated.map((run, i) => ({ ...exp.runs[i], ...run.metrics })))
pilot.analyze({ model: 'mixed', formula: 'printsWasted ~ process * printer + family + (1 | replicate)' }).table('printer')
// → printer   process          printsWasted  minutesToFirstGood  filamentWasted
//   mk4       calibrate-first  1.0           128                 6.1 g
//   mk4       print-and-fix    1.4           104                 21.0 g
//   mk4       analyse-first    0.8           139                 13.2 g
//   ender3    calibrate-first  1.1           146                 7.0 g
//   ender3    print-and-fix    2.6           171                 39.5 g
//   ender3    analyse-first    1.3           162                 20.8 g

// The real confirmation: one family, two replicates per cell, printed for real.
const confirm = exp.runs.filter(r => r.family === 'snap-box' && r.replicate <= 2)   // 12 runs, printed on real printers (an effect)

// ── 5. Designing the objective: three reasonable objectives, three winners ─
const averaged = pilot.means(['process'])   // mean over families and printers
// → { 'calibrate-first': { printsWasted: 1.05, minutesToFirstGood: 137 },
//     'print-and-fix':   { printsWasted: 2.00, minutesToFirstGood: 137.5 },
//     'analyse-first':   { printsWasted: 1.05, minutesToFirstGood: 150.5 } }
const objectives = {
  lexicographic: j.objective.lexicographic([j.objective.minimize('printsWasted'), j.objective.minimize('minutesToFirstGood')]),
  weighted: j.objective.weighted({ waste: ['printsWasted', 5], time: ['minutesToFirstGood', 1] }),
  capped: j.objective.lexicographic([j.objective.require(r => r.printsWasted <= 1.5), j.objective.minimize('filamentWasted')]),
}
Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(objectives).map(([k, o]) => [k, pilot.rank(o, { by: 'process' })[0]]))
// → { lexicographic: 'calibrate-first'   (ties on waste 1.05, then 137 < 150.5 min),
//     weighted:      'calibrate-first'   (142.25 vs 147.5 vs 155.75),
//     capped:        'calibrate-first'   (6.6 g vs 17.0 g; print-and-fix fails the cap) }
// On average they agree. Per printer they do not:
pilot.rank(objectives.weighted, { by: 'process', where: { printer: 'mk4' } })[0]       // → 'print-and-fix'   (111 vs 133 vs 143)
pilot.rank(objectives.lexicographic, { by: 'process', where: { printer: 'mk4' } })[0]  // → 'analyse-first'   (0.8 prints wasted)
pilot.rank(objectives.capped, { by: 'process', where: { printer: 'mk4' } })[0]         // → 'calibrate-first' (6.1 g)

// The objective is chosen before the real run and hashed with the experiment: that is part of the design of the process.
const chosen = objectives.capped
j.hash({ exp, objective: chosen })       // → 'sha256:61f9…'   (pre-registered)
